nodes.start_phrase: Our By-Laws conta in “proxy access” provisions which give an eligible shareho lder (or a group of up to 20 shareholders aggreg ating their shares) that has owned 3% or more of the outstanding common stock continuously for at least three years the right to nominate the greater of two nominees and 20% of the number of directors to be elected at the applicable annual general meeting,
nodes.summary:
- Shareholder notice timing for annual meetings: To bring business or nominate directors, notices must generally arrive 90–120 days before the prior year’s meeting anniversary. If the meeting is moved more than 30 days earlier or 60 days later, or if no prior meeting occurred, notices are due no earlier than 120 days before and no later than the later of 90 days before the meeting or 10 days after the public announcement of the meeting date. Proxy access has separate deadlines. The By-Laws set required form and content for notices, which may limit shareholders’ ability to present matters or nominations.

Any such meeting must be scheduled within 90 days of the secretary’s receipt of the request, and requests must meet By-Law form and content requirements.
- Indemnification: Unless the Board decides otherwise, the company will indemnify directors, officers, and employees to the fullest extent permitted by law for proceedings (civil, criminal, administrative, investigative, or arbitrative, including appeals) arising from their service to the company or at its request.

nodes.summary:
- Advance notice for annual meeting business and director nominations: shareholder notices generally must be delivered to the principal office 90–120 days before the anniversary of the prior year’s annual meeting. If the meeting is moved more than 30 days earlier or 60 days later, or if no prior-year meeting occurred, the notice window shifts to no earlier than 120 days before the meeting and no later than the later of 90 days before the meeting or 10 days after public announcement of the meeting date. The By-Laws prescribe specific form and content requirements, and noncompliance may prevent shareholders from bringing matters or nominating directors. Proxy access users have separate deadlines.
- Proxy access: an eligible shareholder, or a group of up to 20 shareholders, that has owned at least 3% of outstanding common stock continuously for at least three years may include in the company’s proxy materials nominees equal to the greater of two directors or 20% of the board seats up for election, subject to By-Law conditions.
- Special meetings: may be called by the Chair, the Board, or the corporate secretary upon written request from shareholders holding at least 20% of outstanding common stock entitled to vote. The Board sets the date, time, and place (if any), with the meeting to occur within 90 days of the secretary’s receipt of the request. The By-Laws specify required form and content of such requests.
- Indemnification: unless the Board decides otherwise, the company will indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted by law, directors, officers, and employees (including those serving at the company’s request in similar roles elsewhere) for civil, criminal, administrative, investigative, or arbitrative proceedings, including appeals, arising from their service.

nodes.heading: Indemnification of Directors, Officers and Employees.
nodes.start_phrase: Our By-L aws provi de that unless the Board determines otherwise, we shall indemnify , to the full extent permitted by law, any person who was or is, or who is threatened to be made, a party to an action, suit or proceeding (including appeals), whether civil, criminal, administrative, investigative or arbitrative,
nodes.summary:
- Annual meeting advance notice requirements: shareholder proposals and director nominations generally must be received 90–120 days before the prior year’s meeting anniversary; if the meeting is moved more than 30 days earlier or 60 days later, or no prior meeting occurred, notices are due no earlier than 120 days before the meeting and no later than the later of 90 days before the meeting or 10 days after public announcement. The by-laws prescribe required form and content, and late or nonconforming submissions may be excluded. Separate deadlines apply for proxy access.
- Proxy access: an eligible shareholder, or a group of up to 20 shareholders, owning at least 3% of outstanding common stock continuously for at least three years, may include in the company’s proxy materials nominees equal to the greater of two or 20% of the board seats up for election, subject to by-law conditions.
- Special meetings: may be called by the Chair, the Board, or the corporate secretary upon a written request from holders of at least 20% of outstanding common stock entitled to vote. The Board sets the date, time, and place, which must be within 90 days of the secretary’s receipt of the request. The by-laws specify the required form and content of such requests.
- Indemnification: by-laws provide, to the fullest extent permitted by law, indemnification for directors, officers, and employees (including those serving at the company’s request at other entities) for expenses, judgments, fines, and settlements in civil, criminal, administrative, investigative, or arbitrative matters, with potential advancement of expenses at the Board’s discretion.
- Independent director indemnification agreements: the company separately agrees to indemnify independent directors to the fullest extent permitted by law for liabilities, costs, and settlements (including attorneys’ fees, penalties, taxes, and related charges) arising from their board service, with advancement of expenses upon request; exclusion applies for acts known or believed by the director to be clearly in conflict with the company’s best interests.
- North Carolina anti-takeover protections: under the North Carolina Shareholder Protection Act, a 95% shareholder vote is generally required to approve a “business combination” with a 20%+ beneficial owner (or former such owner still an affiliate) unless fair price and procedural requirements are met. “Business combination” includes mergers, consolidations/conversions, and sales or leases of all or a substantial part of the corporation’s assets, among other transactions (definition continues).

nodes.title: Certain Anti-Takeover Effects of North Carolina Law
nodes.heading: Certain Anti -Takeover Effects of North Car olina Law
nodes.start_phrase: The North Carolina Shareholder Protection Act generally requires the affirmative vote of 95% of a public corporation’ s voting shares to approve a “business combination” with any entity that a majority of continuing directors determines beneficially owns, directly or indirectly ,
nodes.summary:
- Indemnification and advancement of expenses: The company’s by-laws provide indemnification for individuals involved in actions, suits, or proceedings (including attorneys’ fees, judgments, fines, and settlements), with the Board able to advance expenses prior to final disposition.
- Independent director indemnification agreements: Separate agreements provide full legal indemnification to independent directors for liabilities and costs (including penalties, settlements with or without court approval, interest, assessments, and excise taxes) arising from their service as directors or committee members, with expenses advanced upon request; exclusions apply for acts the director knew or believed were clearly in conflict with the company’s best interests.
- North Carolina anti-takeover provisions: The North Carolina Shareholder Protection Act generally requires a 95% shareholder vote to approve certain “business combinations” with 20%+ beneficial owners unless fair price and procedural safeguards are met. “Business combination” includes mergers/conversions, substantial asset sales/leases, and specified asset-for-securities exchanges (≥$5,000,000). Opt-out periods have expired and PepsiCo did not opt out, which may deter takeover attempts, affect potential share purchase prices, and delay or prevent changes of control.
- Notes and indenture summary: Prior SEC shelf registrations on Form S-3 cover multiple note issuances (including sterling notes, 2024, 2026, May/July 2028, 2027, 2031, 2032, 2033, 2039, and 2050 notes). The notes were issued under a May 21, 2007 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon as trustee, governed by the Trust Indenture Act of 1939; the indenture is incorporated by reference in the company’s Form 10-K.

nodes.summary:

nodes.heading: Curr ency of Payment of Euro Notes .

nodes.title: Definition of Business Day
nodes.heading: Definition of Business Day.
nodes.start_phrase: The term “business day” with respect to the sterling notes means any day other than a Saturday or Sunday or a day on which banking institutions in the City of New York or the City of London are authorized or required by law or executive order to close.
nodes.summary:

- Payment dates (interest, maturity, redemption) falling on a non-business day are made on the next business day with no additional interest.
- Interest terms: each series bears a stated annual rate; interest is calculated on an ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA) basis, using the actual days from (and including) the accrual start date to (but excluding) the next scheduled interest payment date.
- Optional redemption for sterling notes: issuer may redeem in whole or in part at any time before maturity with 30–60 days’ notice via the depositary; redemption price is the greater of (i) 100% of principal or (ii) the present value of Remaining Scheduled Payments of principal and interest (excluding accrued to the redemption date), discounted on a semi-annual ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA) basis at the Comparable Government rate (text truncated).

- The definition of “Comparable Government Bond Rate” is provided: it is determined for euro notes by matching the gross redemption yield of the notes to the yield of a Comparable Government Bond based on its middle market price at 11:00 a.m. London time on the third business day before the redemption date, selected by an independent investment bank and rounded to three decimal places (0.0005 rounded up).

nodes.title: 2050 Notes.
nodes.heading: 2050 Notes .
nodes.start_phrase: The 2050 notes are redeemable as a whole or in part, at our option at any time and from time to time prior to April 9, 2050 (six months prior to the maturity date of the 2050 notes), at a redemption price equal to the greater of (i) 100% of the principal amount of such notes and (ii) the sum of the present values of the Remaining Scheduled Payments of principal and interest thereon (exclusive of interest accrued to the date of redemption),
nodes.summary:
- Outlines optional redemption terms for euro-denominated 2039 and 2050 notes.
- Prior to six months before maturity, both series are subject to a make-whole call at the greater of: (i) 100% of principal or (ii) the present value of Remaining Scheduled Payments of principal and interest (excluding accrued interest to the redemption date), discounted on an ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA) basis at the Comparable Government Bond Rate plus 20 bps; in all cases plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date.
- On or after six months before maturity, both series are redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest.
- Specific call windows: 2039 notes—make-whole prior to April 16, 2039; par call on/after April 16, 2039. 2050 notes—make-whole prior to April 9, 2050; par call on/after April 9, 2050.
- Defines “Comparable Government Bond Rate” for the euro notes as the price (percentage) that equates the notes’ gross redemption yield to that of the applicable Comparable Government Bond, determined using the middle market price at 11:00 a.m. London time on the third business day before the redemption date, as selected by an independent investment bank.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Comparable Government Bond Rate” means, with respect to any redemption date for each series of euro notes, the price, expressed as a percentage (rounded to three decimal places, with 0.0005 being rounded upwards),
nodes.summary:
- Outlines optional redemption terms for euro-denominated notes maturing in 2039 and 2050.
- Before the par call window (six months prior to maturity), each series may be redeemed at the greater of 100% of principal or a make-whole amount equal to the present value of Remaining Scheduled Payments discounted at the Comparable Government Bond Rate plus 20 bps (ACTUAL/ACTUAL (ICMA)), plus accrued interest.
- On or after the par call dates (April 16, 2039 for the 2039 notes; April 9, 2050 for the 2050 notes), each series is redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued interest.
- Defines key terms: Comparable Government Bond Rate (based on the gross redemption yield of an appropriate German government bond determined by an independent investment bank using middle market prices at 11:00 a.m. London time, rounded to three decimals); Comparable Government Bond (closest-maturity German government bond or a suitable alternative determined with broker/market maker input); Remaining Scheduled Payments (future principal and interest, with the next interest payment reduced by accrued interest if the redemption date is not an interest payment date).
- Describes general redemption mechanics: interest ceases on redeemed notes as of the redemption date; the issuer will fund the trustee/agent to pay redemption price and accrued interest; partial redemptions are allocated per applicable depositary procedures; the issuer may repurchase notes in the open market and cancel them.
- Specifies notice periods: notice of redemption must be sent 30–60 days before the redemption date, except shorter minimums apply—15 days for the 2039 notes and 10 days for the 2024, May 2028, 2032, 2033, and 2050 notes.
- States the issuer is responsible for calculating the redemption price.

nodes.title: General
nodes.heading: General
nodes.start_phrase: On and after the applicable redemption date with respect to a series of notes, interest will cease to accrue on such notes or any portio n of such notes called for redemption (unless we default in the payment of the redemption price and accrued interest).
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Comparable Government Bond” for euro-denominated notes as the German government bond with the closest maturity to the notes being redeemed, or another appropriate German government bond if none is sufficiently similar, as determined by an independent investment bank with input from three German government bond brokers/market makers, for use in calculating the Comparable Government Bond Rate.
- Defines “Remaining Scheduled Payments” for each euro note as the principal and interest that would have been due after the redemption date, with an adjustment that reduces the next scheduled interest payment by interest accrued to the redemption date if that date is not an interest payment date.
- Outlines general redemption mechanics: interest stops accruing on redeemed notes from the redemption date (unless there is a payment default); funds sufficient to pay the redemption price and, if applicable, accrued interest will be deposited with the trustee or its agent by the redemption date; partial redemptions will be selected per depositary procedures; the issuer may repurchase notes in the open market and hold or cancel them.
- Sets redemption notice periods: at least 30 days (or 15 days for the 2039 notes, or 10 days for the 2024, May 2028, 2032, 2033, and 2050 notes) and not more than 60 days before the redemption date, with notice provided to each holder.
- Assigns responsibility to the issuer for calculating the redemption price for notes or portions called for redemption.

nodes.title: Payment of Additional Amounts
nodes.heading: Payment of Additional Amounts
nodes.start_phrase: We will, subject to the exceptions and limitations set forth below , pay as additional interest on the notes such additional amounts as are necessary in order that the net payment by us of the principal of and interest on the notes to a holder who is not a United States perso n (as defined below ),
nodes.summary:
- Purpose: Explains when the issuer will “gross up” payments on the notes to non‑U.S. holders so that, after U.S. withholding, the net principal and interest equal the amounts due.
- Scope: Applies to holders who are not “United States persons,” with definitions provided for “United States” and “United States person.”
- Core commitment: The issuer will pay additional interest amounts to offset U.S. taxes withheld, subject to detailed exceptions.
- Key exceptions (no additional amounts payable) include:
  - Holder’s U.S. nexus: where the holder/beneficial owner (or related fiduciary, settlor, beneficiary, member, or shareholder) is treated as having a U.S. trade or business or permanent establishment; has a U.S. citizenship/residency or other connection not arising solely from holding the notes; is a PHC, PFIC, CFC, or has accumulated earnings to avoid U.S. tax; is a 10-percent shareholder under Code §871(h)(3); or is a bank receiving payments on a loan in the ordinary course of business.
  - Beneficial ownership chain: where the presenting holder is not the sole beneficial owner (e.g., fiduciaries, partnerships, LLCs) and the ultimate owner would not qualify for additional amounts.
  - Documentation failures: noncompliance with required certifications, identification, or information reporting needed to claim exemption or reduced withholding (including treaty forms).
  - Taxes not imposed by withholding by the issuer or paying agent; or withholding avoidable by using another paying agent.
  - Law changes effective more than 15 days after the payment due date/provision date.
  - Non‑income type taxes: estate, inheritance, gift, sales, excise, transfer, wealth, capital gains, personal property, or similar taxes.
  - Late presentation: when a note is presented for payment more than 30 days after the due/provision date.
  - Bank purchase conditions: withholding arising solely because the beneficial owner is a bank buying in the ordinary course of lending or not buying/holding solely for investment (or for resale to a non‑bank/investor).
  - FATCA: no gross‑up for withholding under Code §§1471–1474 (with variations by series on inclusion of regulations, official interpretations, §1471(b) agreements, and intergovernmental agreements).
  - EU savings directive withholding: excluded for Sterling Notes and for the 2026 Notes and July 2028 Notes.
  - Combination clause: no gross‑up for any combination of the above items.
- Series-specific organization:
  - Sterling Notes: includes EU savings directive exception; FATCA exclusion tied to §§1471–1474 and related regulations/interpretations.
  - 2026 Notes and July 2028 Notes: substantially similar exceptions; FATCA exclusion also references §1471(b) agreements and IGAs; includes EU savings directive exception.
  - 2024, 2027, May 2028, 2031, 2032, 2033, 2039, 2050 Notes: similar exceptions; FATCA exclusion also references §1471(b) agreements and IGAs; no EU savings directive exception listed.
- General limitation: Apart from the “Payment of Additional Amounts” undertaking, the issuer is not otherwise obliged to pay any taxes, assessments, or governmental charges.
- Redemption for Tax Reasons: Introduces the issuer’s right to redeem the notes if, due to changes in U.S. tax law or its official interpretation announced or effective on/after the applicable prospectus supplement date, the issuer becomes (or, per independent counsel’s opinion, will become) obligated to pay additional amounts.

nodes.title: Redemption for Tax Reasons
nodes.heading: Redemption for T ax Reasons
nodes.start_phrase: If, as a result of any change in, or amendment to, the laws (or any regulations or rulings promulgated under the laws) of the United States (or any taxing authority in the United States),
nodes.summary:
- Payment of Additional Amounts: Describes when the issuer will pay gross-up amounts to holders for certain taxes imposed on payments on the notes, with explicit exclusions (including FATCA-related taxes under IRC Sections 1471–1474) and a general statement that, except as specifically provided, no additional payments for taxes or governmental charges are required.
- Definitions: Clarifies the meanings of “United States” and “United States person” for use in the Payment of Additional Amounts and Redemption for Tax Reasons provisions.
- Redemption for Tax Reasons: If post-issuance changes in U.S. tax laws or interpretations would obligate the issuer to pay additional amounts, the issuer may redeem all (but not part) of a series of notes at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest, on 30–60 days’ notice, supported by an opinion of independent counsel.
- Certain Covenants — Limitation of Liens: The issuer and its restricted subsidiaries will not incur or guarantee debt secured by liens on principal property or on equity of restricted subsidiaries unless the notes are equally and ratably secured, subject to customary permitted liens, including: (1) pre-existing liens; (2) liens existing when an entity becomes a restricted subsidiary; (3) purchase-money, construction, improvement, or acquisition-related liens (including those incurred within 365 days of acquisition or completion); and (4) liens in favor of the issuer or its restricted subsidiaries.

nodes.title: Certain Covenants
nodes.heading: Certain Covenants
nodes.start_phrase: We will not, and will not permit any of our restricted subsidiaries to, incur , suffer to exist or guarantee any debt secured by a lien on any principal property or on any shares of stock of (or other interes ts in) any of our restricted subsidiaries unless we or that first-mention ed restricted subsidiary secures or causes such restricted subsidiary to secure the notes (and any of its or such restricted subsidiary’ s other debt, at its option or such restricted subsidiary’ s option, as the case may be, not subordinate to the notes),
nodes.summary:
- Optional tax redemption: If the issuer becomes obligated to pay “Additional Amounts” on any series of notes, it may, at its option, redeem all (but not part) of that series on 30–60 days’ notice at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest to (but excluding) the redemption date.
- Covenant—Limitation on Liens: The issuer and its restricted subsidiaries may not incur, allow to exist, or guarantee debt secured by liens on any principal property or on equity interests in restricted subsidiaries unless the notes are secured equally and ratably (or with priority) for as long as such debt is secured.
- Exceptions to the lien limitation include:
  1) Liens existing prior to the issuance of the notes.
  2) Liens on property, equity, or debt of an entity in place when it becomes a restricted subsidiary.
  3) Liens on acquired or constructed property or acquired equity, including purchase-money, acquisition, construction, or improvement liens, or debt incurred before, at, or within 365 days after acquisition, completion of construction, commencement of full operations, or equity acquisition, to finance the purchase or construction.
  4) Liens in favor of the issuer or its restricted subsidiaries.

nodes.title: Limitation of Liens
nodes.heading: Limitation of Liens
nodes.start_phrase: We will not, and will not permit any of our restricted subsidiaries to, incur , suffer to exist or guarantee any debt secured by a lien on any principal property or on any shares of stock of (or other interes ts in) any of our restricted subsidiaries unless we or that first-mention ed restricted subsidiary secures or causes such restricted subsidiary to secure the notes (and any of its or such restricted subsidiary’ s other debt, at its option or such restricted subsidiary’ s option, as the case may be, not subordinate to the notes),
nodes.summary:
- Optional redemption for tax reasons: If “Payment of Additional Amounts” becomes applicable to a series of notes, the issuer may redeem all (but not part) of that series on 30–60 days’ notice at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest to (but excluding) the redemption date.
- Limitation on Liens (negative pledge): The issuer and its restricted subsidiaries will not incur or guarantee debt secured by liens on principal property or on stock/interests of restricted subsidiaries unless the notes are equally and ratably secured (or secured prior to such debt).
  - Permitted liens include: (1) pre-existing liens; (2) liens existing when an entity becomes a restricted subsidiary; (3) purchase-money, acquisition, construction, improvement, or similar liens (including within 365 days of acquisition/construction/start-up, and including mergers); (4) liens in favor of the issuer or its restricted subsidiaries; (5) liens in favor of or required by governmental entities; and (6) extensions, renewals, or refundings of such liens.
  - General basket: Additional secured debt is permitted without equally securing the notes if, after giving effect, it does not exceed 15% of consolidated net tangible assets.
  - Structural flexibility: The indenture does not restrict transferring principal property to unrestricted subsidiaries or redesignating a subsidiary from restricted to unrestricted; such unrestricted subsidiaries are not subject to the lien covenant, and their secured debt does not trigger equal-and-ratable security for the notes.
- Consolidation, merger, or sale of assets: Allowed with conditions that (i) the issuer is the survivor or the successor is a U.S. corporation that expressly assumes the notes and indenture via supplemental indenture; (ii) no default or event of default exists immediately after the transaction; and (iii) an opinion of counsel is delivered confirming compliance. Upon completion, the successor is substituted as obligor and the issuer is released from all obligations under the notes and indenture.

nodes.title: Consolidation, Merger or Sale of Assets
nodes.heading: Consolidation, Mer ger or Sale of Assets
nodes.start_phrase: We may consolidate or merge with or into, or convey or transfer all or substantially all of our assets to, any entity (including, without limitation, a limited partnership or a limited liability company); provided that:
nodes.summary:
- Permitted liens: Adds liens in favor of or required by government entities and extensions/renewals/refundings of previously permitted liens. Overall, secured debt may be incurred by the company or its restricted subsidiaries without equally securing the notes, so long as, after giving effect, the aggregate secured debt does not exceed 15% of consolidated net tangible assets.
- Subsidiary flexibility: The indenture allows transferring principal property to an unrestricted subsidiary or redesignating a restricted subsidiary as unrestricted. Unrestricted subsidiaries are not limited by the lien covenant, and their secured debt does not require the notes to be equally and ratably secured.
- Consolidation, merger, or sale of assets: The company may merge, consolidate, or transfer substantially all assets to any entity, provided that (i) the company is the survivor or, if not, the successor is a U.S. or D.C.-organized corporation that expressly assumes the indenture and notes via a supplemental indenture; (ii) no default or event of default exists immediately after the transaction; and (iii) an opinion of counsel is delivered to the trustee confirming compliance.
- Effect of such transactions: The successor is substituted as obligor under the notes and indenture, and the company is released from all related obligations.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.start_phrase: “Consolidated net tangible assets” means the total amount of our assets and our restricted subsidiaries’ assets minus:
nodes.summary:
The excerpt provides definitions of key terms likely used in financial covenants and corporate structuring within the document. It clarifies:
- Consolidated net tangible assets: calculated from the company’s and restricted subsidiaries’ assets per US GAAP, less depreciation/valuation reserves, current liabilities (excluding intercompany), and intangible assets (goodwill, IP, unamortized debt costs).
- Debt: any indebtedness for borrowed money.
- Principal property: significant plants, offices, or warehouses owned or leased, excluding facilities deemed immaterial by the Board.
- Subsidiary: entities majority-owned (voting stock) directly or indirectly.
- Restricted subsidiary: any subsidiary not classified as unrestricted.
- Unrestricted subsidiary: subsidiaries primarily engaged in financial services (e.g., finance, banking, leasing, insurance), holding companies of such entities, or those designated as unrestricted by the Board.

nodes.title: Events of Default
nodes.heading: Events of Default
nodes.start_phrase: An “Event of Default” under the notes of a given series means:
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Events of Default” for each series of PepsiCo notes, including:
  - Failure to pay interest for 30+ days
  - Failure to pay principal or premium when due
  - Failure to make required sinking/purchase fund payments for 30+ days
  - Breach of covenants/warranties not cured within 90 days after notice from the trustee or holders of at least 51% of the series
  - Specified bankruptcy/insolvency/reorganization/administration events
  - Any additional events stated in the applicable prospectus supplement
- Remedies and acceleration:
  - For non-bankruptcy defaults, the trustee or holders of at least 51% in principal amount of a series may accelerate all amounts due (or a lesser amount if specified)
  - For bankruptcy-related defaults, acceleration is automatic without action
- Rescission and waivers:
  - Holders of at least 51% may rescind acceleration if all continuing defaults (other than nonpayment caused solely by acceleration) are cured/waived and rescission doesn’t conflict with any judgment
  - Majority holders may waive past defaults except payment defaults and provisions requiring unanimous consent
- Enforcement procedures:
  - Holders of at least 51% may prompt the trustee to institute proceedings after written notice of a continuing default, a written request, and reasonable indemnity; the trustee has 60 days to act and must not have received inconsistent directions from a majority
  - Individual holders may sue directly to enforce payment of principal/interest/premium when due
- Trustee duties and protections:
  - During an Event of Default, the trustee must act with prudence
  - The trustee need not act at holders’ direction without reasonable security/indemnity
  - Majority holders may direct the time, method, and place of remedies, subject to indenture terms
- Default notices:
  - Trustee must notify holders within 90 days of any default unless cured/waived
  - Trustee may withhold notice if in holders’ interests, except for payment defaults, which must be noticed

nodes.title: Modification and Waiver
nodes.heading: Modification and W aiver
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture may be amended or modified without the consent of any holder of notes in order to:
nodes.summary:
- Outlines when the indenture can be amended without noteholder consent, including to replace the trustee, fix ambiguities, reflect assumption of obligations after mergers or asset transfers, grant additional holder rights, add guarantors, secure notes, set note forms, maintain Trust Indenture Act qualification, or make changes not materially adverse to holders.
- Permits other amendments with consent of holders of at least a majority in principal amount of each affected series.
- Lists actions that require unanimous consent of each affected holder, such as reducing principal, interest, or premium; extending maturity or interest payment times; altering redemption terms; changing payment currency; lowering required consent thresholds; impairing enforcement rights; waiving payment defaults; adversely affecting ranking; or releasing a guarantor except as allowed by the indenture.
- Describes conditions for satisfaction and discharge of the indenture: either all notes of a series are surrendered for cancellation, or all are due/within one year of becoming due/subject to redemption within one year with proper notice arrangements, and sufficient funds are irrevocably deposited to pay all amounts due.
- Requires payment of all other sums due under the indenture and delivery of an officers’ certificate and opinion of counsel confirming compliance with all conditions for satisfaction and discharge.

nodes.title: Satisfaction, Discharge and Covenant Defeasance
nodes.heading: Satisfaction, Discharge and Covenant Defeasance
nodes.start_phrase: We may terminate our obligations under the indenture, when:
nodes.summary:
- Limits on amendments/waivers: Certain core terms cannot be changed without each affected holder’s consent, including lowering the required consent threshold, impairing the right to sue for payment, waiving payment defaults, reducing the interest rate or extending interest payment dates, adversely affecting ranking, or releasing a guarantor except as permitted by the indenture.

- Satisfaction and discharge: The issuer may terminate its indenture obligations for a series if all notes are canceled or due/being redeemed within a year with sufficient funds irrevocably deposited, all other sums under the indenture are paid, and officers’ certificates and legal opinions confirm compliance.

- Legal defeasance: The issuer can be deemed to have paid and discharged a series in full while preserving certain obligations, including holders’ rights to payment, administrative obligations (transfer, lost notes, payment office, trust funds), trustee protections, and the defeasance provisions.

- Covenant defeasance: The issuer may be released from specified covenants so that failure to comply with them is not a default. After covenant defeasance, certain defaults (other than non-payment, bankruptcy, and insolvency) no longer apply for that series.

- Conditions to defeasance: Requires irrevocable deposit with the trustee of cash, government obligations, or a combination sufficient to pay all principal, interest, and any premium (with accountant’s opinion on sufficiency); favorable tax opinions confirming no income recognition for holders; absence of defaults (with a 91-day bankruptcy-related condition for legal defeasance); no trustee conflict under the Trust Indenture Act; no breach of other agreements; no investment company issues; and delivery of officers’ certificates and legal opinions.

- Book-entry, delivery, and settlement: Notes are issued as global securities held with a common depositary for Clearstream and Euroclear, registered in the depositary’s nominee name. Transfers of global notes occur only in whole to Clearstream/Euroclear or their nominees; investors hold through participants or indirect participants in those systems, with ownership and transfers reflected in their book-entry records. Procedures are based on current Clearstream/Euroclear rules and may change.

nodes.title: Book-Entry, Delivery and Settlement
nodes.heading: Book-Entry , Delivery and Settlement
nodes.start_phrase: We have obtained the information in this section concerning Clearstream and Euroclear and their book-entry systems and procedures from sources that we believe to be reliable.
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for legal defeasance and covenant defeasance: must not breach other agreements; resulting trust must not be an unregistered investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940; delivery to the trustee of an officers’ certificate and legal opinion confirming all conditions precedent are met.
- Notes issued as fully registered global notes held with a common depositary for Clearstream and Euroclear; transfers of global notes permitted only as a whole to Clearstream/Euroclear or their nominees.
- Investors hold beneficial interests through Clearstream/Euroclear participants; records and transfers are maintained in their book-entry systems.
- Settlement and trading: distribution and secondary market trading clear through Clearstream/Euroclear; settle in same-day funds; payments made in sterling for sterling notes and euro for euro notes (subject to any prospectus supplement).
- Operational framework: Clearstream/Euroclear maintain electronic links enabling cross-border clearance and settlement without physical certificates; special procedures facilitate secondary market trades.
- Responsibilities and disclaimers: issuer provides information on Clearstream/Euroclear from believed reliable sources but disclaims accuracy/responsibility; does not supervise or control their systems; policies of the clearing systems govern payments, transfers, and exchanges; procedures may be modified or discontinued at any time.
- Beneficial owners are not registered holders under the indenture, receive no physical certificates, and must rely on the depositary and its participants to exercise rights, including receiving reports.

nodes.title: Certificated Notes
nodes.heading: Certificated Notes .
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to certain conditions, the notes represented by the global notes are exchangeable for certificated notes in definitive form of like tenor in minimum denominations of £100,000 principal amount and integral multiples of £1,000 in excess thereof with respect to the sterling notes and €100,000 principal amount and integral multiples of €1,000 in excess thereof with respect to the euro notes if:
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for exchanging global notes into certificated notes:
  - If the common depositary is unwilling, unable, or unqualified to act and no successor is appointed within 90 days.
  - If the issuer decides not to have all notes of a series represented by a global note.
  - If an event of default leading to acceleration has occurred and is continuing.
- Exchange mechanics:
  - Exchangeable into certificated notes of the same series in authorized denominations, registered as directed by the common depositary.
  - Otherwise, global notes are not exchangeable except for another global note of the same aggregate denomination registered to the common depositary or its nominee.
- Denominations:
  - Sterling notes: minimum £100,000 and integral multiples of £1,000.
  - Euro notes: minimum €100,000 and integral multiples of €1,000.
- Same-day payment and transfer for certificated notes:
  - May be executed at an office/agency in the City of London (initially the paying agent’s office) or by mailed check.
  - If holders provide wire instructions, payments must be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to specified accounts.
- Transfer/registration fees:
  - No service charge for registration of transfer, but taxes or governmental charges related to the registration may be required.

nodes.title: Same-day Payment
nodes.heading: Same-day Payment .
nodes.start_phrase: Payments (including principal, interes t and any additional amounts) and transfers with respect to notes of any series in certificated form may be executed at the office or agency maintained for such purpose within the City of London (initially the office of the paying agent maintained for such purpose) or, at our option, by check mailed to the holders thereof at the respective addresses set forth in the register of holders of the applicable notes of such series, provided that all payments (including principal, interest and any additional amounts) on notes in certificated form, for which the holders thereof have given wire transfer instructions, will be required to be made by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the accounts specified by the holders thereof.
nodes.summary:
- Explains when global notes can be exchanged for certificated notes, including: (1) the common depositary is unwilling, unable, or unqualified and no successor is appointed within 90 days; (2) the issuer elects to issue certificated notes; or (3) a default leading to acceleration has occurred and is continuing.
- Specifies minimum exchange denominations: £100,000 plus £1,000 increments for sterling notes; €100,000 plus €1,000 increments for euro notes.
- Describes exchange mechanics: certificated notes issued in authorized denominations and registered as directed by the common depositary; otherwise, global notes are not exchangeable except for another global note of the same aggregate denomination in the name of the common depositary or its nominee.
- Details same-day payment and transfer procedures for certificated notes: payments may be made at a City of London office/agency (initially the paying agent) or by mailed check; if wire instructions are on file, payments must be made by wire of immediately available funds; no service charge for transfer registrations, but applicable taxes or governmental charges may be required.
- Introduces Exhibit 10.7: the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan – Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), as amended and restated effective January 1, 2021, with updates through December 2021.

structure.title: THE PEPSICO INTERNATIONAL RETIREMENT PLAN DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM (PIRP-DC)
structure.heading:
Exhibit 10.7
THE PEPSICO INTERNA TIONAL RETIREMENT PLAN
DEFINED CONTRIBUTION PROGRAM
(PIRP-DC)
structure.start_phrase: PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Corporation”) first established the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan ef fective as of September 1, 1980.
structure.summary:
- Exhibit 10.7: The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan – Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC), amended and restated effective January 1, 2021, with updates through December 2021.
- Plan structure and scope: history and general information; key definitions and rules of construction.
- Membership provisions: eligibility criteria, admission process, and active vs. inactive membership status.
- Contributions framework: rules governing contributions and applicable offsets.
- Member accounts: accounting of interests, vesting rules, and special vesting for approved transfers and status changes.
- Benefit distributions: general distribution rules, distributions upon termination of employment or death, valuation methods, and designation of dependants.
- Administration: authority to administer, facility of payment, claims and appeals procedures, limitations on actions, venue restrictions, and effects of specific references.
- Plan changes: continuation, amendment, and termination procedures.
- Miscellaneous provisions: unfunded plan status, plan costs, treatment of temporary absences, taxes, no guarantee of employment or right to benefits, charges and recovery of excess payments, prohibited misconduct, notices, documentation, currency of payments, governing law, ERISA exemption, Section 409A exemption, and electronic signatures.
- Signature section and appendix.

nodes.title: HISTORY AND GENERAL INFORMATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I – HIST ORY AND GENERAL INFORMA TION
nodes.start_phrase: PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Corporation”) first established the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan ef fective as of September 1, 1980.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: History and general information of PepsiCo, Inc.’s international retirement plan structure, documenting key amendments, restatements, and plan design changes from 1980 through 2021.
- Establishment and early structure:
  - 1980: Creation of the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, comprising a Trust Indenture and Plan Rules.
  - 1982: Plan amended and restated in full.
- 2003 reconfiguration:
  - Split into “Plan A Rules” (benefits funded via a trust under the Trust Indenture) and “Plan B Rules” (benefits funded by the Corporation as they arise).
- 2005 amendment:
  - For individuals subject to U.S. taxation, no benefit rights may arise, increase, or be enhanced; benefits determined as if employment ended before becoming subject to U.S. tax.
- 2010 consolidation:
  - Plan A and Plan B Rules combined into a single plan document setting the terms of the Defined Benefit (DB) Program.
- 2011 introduction of DC Program:
  - New Defined Contribution (DC) Program established for selected international employees, including:
    - Employees on assignments outside their home countries where home plan participation is impractical.
    - Selected senior globalists on U.S. tax-equalized packages.
  - This document governs the DC Program; together, the DB and DC Programs comprise a single Plan.
  - DC Program also referred to as the PepsiCo International Pension Plan (PIPP).
- Subsequent DC Program updates:
  - 2016 amendment and restatement: Expanded eligibility to certain localized employees outside their home country who previously participated in a company retirement program and lack an available company-provided program post-localization.
  - 2019 amendment and restatement: Recognition of same-sex and opposite-sex domestic partners for certain purposes for active Members or those on authorized leave on/after January 1, 2019.
  - 2021 amendment and restatement: DC Program updated effective January 1, 2021.
- Funding and legal status:
  - At all times, the Plan is unfunded and unsecured for U.S. Internal Revenue Code and ERISA purposes.
  - Benefits are obligations of each executive’s individual employer; participants are unsecured general creditors of that employer.
  - Intended ERISA exemption as a plan maintained outside the U.S. primarily for nonresident aliens.

nodes.title: DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE II – DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this governing document for the DC Program, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article II of the PepsiCo International Retirement Plan – Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC) sets out core definitions used throughout the DC Program and rules for construing the document.
- Governance and roles:
  - “Corporation” is PepsiCo, Inc.; “PepsiCo Organization” is the controlled group under IRC §414.
  - “Vice President” (Global Benefits & Wellness) has broad discretionary authority to interpret terms, set or change valuation dates, approve employers, determine eligibility, adjust interest methodology, and decide service crediting.
- Plan structure:
  - “Plan” consists of a Defined Benefit Program (PIRP-DB) and a Defined Contribution Program (PIRP-DC).
  - “DB Program” and “DC Program” are defined and referenced as separate governing documents.
- Employer and employee status:
  - “Employers” includes PepsiCo and Associated Companies; an “Approved Employer” is one authorized to enroll Eligible Employees.
  - “Associated Company” is an entity controlled by or associated with the Corporation that agrees to the DC Program terms.
  - “Eligible Employee” criteria cover non-U.S.-based full-time salaried staff of an Approved Employer not accruing DB benefits, with specific pathways (international assignments, multiple/first assignments where no corporate home-country plan exists, selected senior globalists on U.S. tax-equalized packages, and certain localized employees lacking a local plan). Part-time eligibility may be approved.
  - “Member,” “Active Member,” “Inactive Member,” and “Entry Date” are defined for participation status and timing.
- Family/beneficiary definitions:
  - “Eligible Spouse” is determined under the law of the Member’s principal residence, limited to one spouse.
  - “Eligible Domestic Partner” rules outline recognition via civil union or equivalent, enrollment in specified health program, or other written criteria, with claims timing and exclusivity rules (cannot have both spouse and domestic partner).
  - “Dependant” is the recipient of a Member’s PIRP-DC Account upon death.
- Compensation and accounts:
  - “Salary” defines compensation for crediting: non-U.S. payroll uses home notional base salary (plus bonus for those becoming Active Members on/after Jan 1, 2021), U.S. payroll uses base plus annual bonus; VP may add notional bonus.
  - “PIRP-DC Account” is an unfunded notional account on the Employer’s books; “Pay Credit” and “Interest Credit” are the components credited to it.
  - “Interest Rate” initially tied to the 30-year Treasury rate (IRS September prior to the Plan Year), adjustable by the VP to maintain a reasonable market rate and stay within IRC §409A earnings limits.
- Service and mobility:
  - “Service” includes continuous employment with Approved Employers, with detailed rules on authorized leaves, breaks in service, and VP-approved pre/post-transfer service counting.
  - “Approved Transfer” covers moves or secondments to U.S./territories or changes making the Member a U.S. Person when initiated/approved by the Corporation or Employer.
  - “Status Change” is any other change causing U.S. Person status.
  - “U.S. Person” follows IRC §7701(b) (citizen, green card, substantial presence, or election) and includes a tax-return-based rule unless VP determines no U.S. source earned income from PepsiCo.
- Valuation and timing:
  - “Valuation Date” is each business day (or as set by VP), with at least an annual Plan Year-end valuation and special valuations for Approved Transfers or certain Status Changes.
  - “Distribution Valuation Date” is set by the VP; currently the month-end immediately after the distribution-triggering event (e.g., Dec 30 → Dec 31; Dec 31 → Jan 31 following year), with values as of close of business (or prior business day).
  - “Plan Year” is the calendar year; “Effective Date” of the DC Program is Jan 1, 2011.
- Construction rules:
  - Gender/number usage is inclusive; singular includes plural and vice versa.
  - Year counting: any 365/366-day period may constitute a year; partial years/months can be prorated; VP may authorize counting in days or calendar months.
  - “Hereof/Hereunder” refer to the entire DC Program, not specific sections.
  - “Including” and examples are interpreted as “without limitation.”
  - Document hierarchy and cross-referencing conventions are defined (articles, sections, subsections, paragraphs, subparagraphs, clauses).

nodes.title: MEMBERSHIP
nodes.heading: ARTICLE III – MEMBERSHIP
nodes.start_phrase: Every person who the V ice President determines is an Eligible Employee shall be eligible for Membership.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Vice President has sole authority to determine who qualifies as an “Eligible Employee” and to approve Membership.
- Admission requires the individual to be an Eligible Employee, not a U.S. Person during the relevant period, and to receive Vice President approval; Membership becomes effective on the individual’s Entry Date.
- The “relevant time” includes a sufficient pre-entry period to ensure PIRP-DC Accounts are not treated as deferred compensation subject to U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.
- No person may be admitted to Membership without Vice President approval.
- Defines Active Membership as periods when the individual is employed as an Eligible Employee, is not a U.S. Person, and is currently approved as Active by the Vice President; otherwise, the Member is Inactive.

nodes.title: CONTRIBUTIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IV – CONTRIBUTIONS
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent provided in subsections (a) and (b) below , the Employer shall allocate Pay Credits and Interest Credits to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account, each determined by the V ice President as follows –
nodes.summary:
- Article IV covers how Contributions are credited to a Member’s PIRP-DC Account: Pay Credits and Interest Credits, each determined by the Vice President (VP).
- Pay Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active Member during the Plan Year.
  - Standard calculation: Annualized Salary as of the Valuation Date multiplied by an applicable percentage (5%, 8%, 10%, 12%, or 18%) set by the VP.
  - Special rule (effective for individuals becoming Active on/after Jan 1, 2021 with no Service as a U.S. Person): Pay Credit based on “points” (age + years of Service, in whole years and days) with tiers from 5% to 12% of Eligible Pay.
  - VP sets/adjusts the applicable percentage at Entry or re-entry and may change it each Plan Year; no guaranteed right to any initial or increased percentage.
  - Pay Credits stop as needed to comply with IRC §401(a)(17) compensation limit and Section 9.14 limitations.
- Interest Credits:
  - Eligibility: Must be an Active or Inactive Member during the year and have a prior-year balance.
  - Calculation: Interest Rate for the period since the last Valuation Date multiplied by the prior Valuation Date account balance; determined by the VP.
- Timing and proration:
  - Credits are determined as soon as administratively practicable after each Valuation Date.
  - Pay Credits are prorated for partial years of Active Membership; Interest Credits are prorated for partial years of Membership.
  - Fractional year is based on days of (Active) Membership divided by total days in the Plan Year.
  - Paid leave counts as Active Membership; unpaid leave does not (Pay Credit may be prorated or not provided accordingly).
  - In a final year, prorated credits are determined as of the Distribution Valuation Date.
  - VP’s calculations are conclusive and binding on Members and their Dependants.
- Offsets (Section 4.02):
  - The Corporation may reduce payments/benefits by amounts owed by the Member to the Corporation.
  - The Corporation may offset for:
    - Material benefits under other retirement plans (corporate or governmental) to the extent tied to Service or Salary already used for DC Program Pay Credits.
    - Termination indemnities or similar payments related to employment termination, to the extent tied to Service already used for DC Program Pay Credits.
  - Reductions may affect Pay/Interest Credits, account balances (Article V), or distributions (Article VI).
  - All determinations, including materiality and application, are in the VP’s sole, independent discretion.

nodes.title: MEMBER ACCOUNTS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE V – MEMBER ACCOUNTS
nodes.start_phrase: Pay Credits and Interest Credits shall be credited to a Member ’s PIRP-DC Account as of the V aluation Date to which such credits relate (or , in the case of Pay Credits and Interest Credits that relate to the Member ’s final year of Membership, as of the Member ’s Distribution V aluation Date) or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter .
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Member PIRP-DC Accounts are credited: Pay Credits and Interest Credits are posted as of the relevant Valuation Date (or the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date for the final year), or as soon as administratively practicable thereafter.
- Clarifies that PIRP-DC Accounts are not actual funded accounts: they are bookkeeping devices only; no assets are segregated, and accounts are not funded, insured, or secured; they track employer liability.
- Sets vesting rules (subject to Sections 4.02 and 9.14): Members become fully vested after 3 years of Service, or earlier upon death or disability while employed; disability is determined by the Vice President under appropriate standards.
- Provides special vesting provisions:
  - Automatic special vesting for Active Members with an Approved Transfer during a Plan Year, effective the last business day before the earlier of the transfer or the date the Member becomes a U.S. Person in connection with the transfer.
  - Special vesting for Status Changes upon Member request and Vice President approval, effective the last business day before the Status Change; both request and approval must be finalized before the vesting date.
  - Special vesting grants vesting to the same extent as under Section 5.02 as of the special vesting date.
- All special vesting rights are subject to maintaining full exemption from U.S. Internal Revenue Code Section 409A; Section 5.03 does not apply if inconsistent with this requirement.

nodes.title: DISTRIBUTION OF BENEFITS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VI – DISTRIBUTION OF BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: A Member ’s PIRP-DC Account shall be distributed based upon first to occur of the Member ’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization or death, as provided in Sections 6.02 and 6.03 respectively , subject to Section 4.06 (vesting).
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Outlines how and when PIRP-DC Account benefits are distributed and how the Plan is administered, including claims and decision-making authority.
- Distribution triggers and form:
  - Benefits are distributed upon the earlier of a Member’s termination of employment with the PepsiCo Organization or death, subject to vesting.
  - All distributions are paid in cash as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the Member’s Distribution Valuation Date.
- Termination (including disability):
  - If distribution is due to termination, payment timing follows the rule above.
  - For disability-related terminations, the Vice President determines disability status and the effective termination date.
- Death benefits and beneficiary order:
  - Upon death, benefits are paid in a single lump sum on the first day of the month after the Distribution Valuation Date.
  - Primary payee is the Member’s designated Dependant(s). If no valid Dependant designation exists or all designated Dependants predecease the Member, payment goes to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner; if none, to the estate.
- Valuation up to payout:
  - The PIRP-DC Account continues to receive Interest Credits and be debited for expenses until the Distribution Valuation Date.
- Beneficiary (Dependant) designations:
  - Members may designate, change, or revoke Dependants at any time before the effective date of the election.
  - If married, naming anyone other than the Eligible Spouse as Dependant requires the Eligible Spouse’s written consent; revocations do not require spousal consent.
  - Designations/changes/consents must follow Vice President–adopted rules, be in writing on VP-provided forms, and are not effective until filed with the Vice President.
- Plan administration and authority:
  - The Vice President administers the Plan, interprets provisions, and issues regulations; actions are in sole discretion and are final and binding.
  - The Vice President may delegate responsibilities to others; references to VP actions include actions by delegates/designates.
- Facility of payment:
  - If a payee is under legal disability or otherwise incapacitated, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply payments for the person’s benefit; such payments discharge Plan liability.
- Claims procedure and discretionary review:
  - The Vice President (or designee) has exclusive discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility, and decide benefit amounts; benefits are paid only if the Vice President decides the Petitioner is entitled.
  - Discretion applies even where not expressly granted; the VP may consider Company intent.
  - Decisions are final, conclusive, and binding, and are reviewable by a court only under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
  - The section begins to address denials of claims but is cut off in the excerpt.

nodes.title: ADMINISTRATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VII – ADMINISTRA TION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the V ice President, who shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as he deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Centralized administration: The Vice President administers the Plan, with sole, absolute discretion to interpret provisions, decide eligibility and benefit amounts, and issue regulations; all determinations are final and binding.
- Delegation allowed: The Vice President may delegate duties to other persons or entities; references to actions by the Vice President include actions by delegates.
- Facility of payment: If a payee is legally disabled or otherwise unable to manage finances, the Vice President may direct payments to a legal representative or apply them for the person’s benefit; such payment fully discharges Plan liability for that amount.
- Claims authority and standard of review: The Vice President (or designee) has exclusive discretionary authority over claims; benefits are paid only if the Vice President decides the Petitioner is entitled. Court review is under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- Consideration of company intent: The Vice President may consider the Company’s intent when interpreting Plan provisions, even if not expressly contemplated in plan documents.
- Initial claim decisions: Written denial notices within 90 days of claim receipt (extendable to 180 days with timely notice) must state reasons, cite specific Plan provisions, identify needed additional information, and describe review procedures and timelines.
- Appeals/review process: Petitioners are entitled to a full and fair review, may submit relevant comments and documents, and receive consideration of all such materials. Decision on review within 60 days (extendable once by 60 days with notice), with written reasons and specific Plan citations, and free access to relevant documents upon request.
- Record limitation and exhaustion: Any court or tribunal review is limited to the record before the Vice President at the time of decision. Petitioners must fully exhaust Plan claims and appeals before filing suit. Exhaustion cannot be excused except under narrow conditions for clear, written document requests where the Petitioner is legally entitled and the documents are material.
- Statute of limitations: A two-year limitations period applies to all claims and actions.
  - For benefit claims, accrual is the earliest of: receipt of the benefit calculation; the identified payment commencement date; when the Petitioner knew or should have known of the relevant acts or facts; or the first payment/provision/denial of the benefit.
  - For other claims, accrual is when the Petitioner knew or should have known of the acts or facts giving rise to the claim.
  - Communications during or after the appeals process do not toll or extend the two-year period.
- Venue restriction: Any court or tribunal action must be filed in New York state or federal court located nearest the Corporation’s headquarters.
- Clarification on discretion: Specific references to the Vice President’s discretion in certain provisions do not limit the breadth of discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Defined “Petitioner”: Includes any former or current Eligible Employee, Member, Dependent, or other person or entity asserting a right to benefits under the Plan.

nodes.title: AMENDMENT AND TERMINATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VIII – AMENDMENT AND TERMINA TION
nodes.start_phrase: While the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely , it assumes no contractual obligation as to its continuance.
nodes.summary:
- States the Corporation intends to continue the Plan indefinitely but assumes no contractual obligation to do so.
- Reserves the Corporation’s sole discretion to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Plan at any time, to the fullest extent allowed by law.
- Protects Members’ and Dependants’ Plan account balances as of the date of any amendment or termination, except where the Member becomes entitled to amounts under another employer plan or practice.
- Clarifies that specific payment forms and timing are not protected by the balance-protection rule.
- Authorizes the Corporation to amend the Plan at any time, with or without retroactive effect, subject to the balance-protection provision; other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Allows the Corporation to terminate the Plan entirely or only with respect to one or more Employers; if not all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for employees of the remaining Employers.

nodes.title: MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IX – MISCELLANEOUS
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers’ obligations under the Plan shall not be funded, but shall constitute liabilities by the Employer payable when due out of the Employer ’s general funds.
nodes.summary:
- Plan status and funding: The plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the employer’s general assets and participants are unsecured general creditors.
- Plan expenses: All administrative costs are borne by participating employers, allocated based on their share of members.
- Absences and employment status: A non-terminal absence generally leads to deemed termination after 12 months unless the Vice President decides otherwise; military/national service does not trigger termination while the employer treats the individual as employed.
- Taxes: The plan may withhold amounts needed to satisfy taxes or assessments on benefits.
- Employment relationship: The plan does not guarantee employment or create rights beyond its terms; cessation of membership upon termination does not create damages claims.
- Offsets and recovery: Benefits may be reduced to cover employer/PepsiCo losses caused by a member’s misconduct. Any excess, premature, or misdirected payment must be repaid; the plan has a constructive trust/equitable lien, offset rights, and may pursue legal action to recover overpayments with interest, and recipients must cooperate.
- Prohibited Misconduct and forfeiture: If the Vice President determines a member engaged in prohibited misconduct up to two years after leaving PepsiCo, all pay and interest credits are forfeited and recoverable. Misconduct includes:
  - Participation in competitors involving “Covered Products.”
  - Soliciting PepsiCo employees to leave.
  - Using or disclosing PepsiCo confidential information.
  - Acts contrary to PepsiCo’s interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading, gross misconduct).
  - Fraud.
  Whistleblower protections and Defend Trade Secrets Act safe harbors are preserved.
- Notices and documents: Notices to members may be sent to last known address or by other VP-approved methods; members can obtain a copy of the plan.
- Currency: Benefits are paid in USD or another VP-approved eligible currency using VP-approved exchange methodology.
- Governing law: New York law and applicable U.S. federal law (as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York) govern.
- ERISA exemption: The plan is intended to be exempt as a non-U.S. plan for nonresident aliens; active membership is limited to nonresident aliens working outside the U.S., and records are maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A exemption: The plan is intended to remain fully exempt from IRC §409A. U.S. Persons cannot receive benefit enhancements tied to U.S. service or compensation; limited interest credits may accrue only on non-U.S.-sourced pay credits. Eligibility for annual enhancements is determined post-year (with special commencement-year rules). The Vice President has broad authority to preserve the exemption.
- Electronic signatures: Electronic signatures and records have the same legal effect as manual/paper records where permitted by law.

nodes.title: SIGNATURE
nodes.heading: ARTICLE X – SIGNA TURE
nodes.start_phrase: The PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DC Program document, as amended and restated, is hereby adopted as of this 20th day of December , 2021, to be ef fective as of January 1, 2021 or as otherwise stated herein.
nodes.summary: This section is the signature and adoption page (Article X – Signature) for the amended and restated PepsiCo International Retirement Plan, DC Program. It formally adopts the plan as of December 20, 2021, with an effective date of January 1, 2021 (unless otherwise specified). The document is executed by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer of PepsiCo, Inc., and includes Law Department approval by Jeffrey A. Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel. Both signatures are dated (December 20, 2021 for execution and December 10, 2021 for legal approval).

nodes.title: APPENDIX
nodes.heading: APPENDIX
nodes.start_phrase: Effective January 1, 2013, the V ice President, in his or her sole discretion, may establish Pay Credit Schedules other than those provided for in Section 4.01 of the DC Program to apply in the case of a Member (or Members) specifically designated by the Vice President for this purpose, provided that each such arrangement otherwise meets all applicable requirements of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix provision effective January 1, 2013 authorizes the Vice President, in his or her sole discretion, to establish alternative Pay Credit Schedules for specifically designated Members, different from those in Section 4.01 of the DC Program.
- Any such alternative arrangements must comply with all applicable requirements of the Plan.
- The excerpt is from Exhibit 10.9: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP), Plan Document for the Pre-Section 409A Program, Restated as of January 1, 2022.

structure.title: PEPSICO PENSION EQUALIZATION PLAN (PEP) Plan Document for the Pre-Section 409A Program January 1, 2022 Restatement
structure.heading:
Exhibit 10.9
PEPSICO
PENSION EQUALIZA TION PLAN
(PEP)
Plan Document for the Pre-Section 409A Program
January 1, 2022 Restatement
structure.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
structure.summary:
- Document type and scope: Restated plan document (effective January 1, 2022) for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) – Pre-Section 409A Program, covering pension benefits that are “grandfathered” under Section 409A (generally benefits earned and vested by December 31, 2004). Applies to salaried employees participating in the PepsiCo Salaried Plan whose qualified plan benefits are limited by Internal Revenue Code caps and to certain employees eligible under a pre-1989 formula.
- Historical context: Reflects the 1989 full restatement, the 2005 Pre-409A document (effective January 1, 2005), and a 2016 restatement that made no material changes to the Pre-409A provisions, which largely preserve the 1989 rules.
- Comprehensive definitions: Article II provides detailed definitions governing eligibility, benefit calculations, and payment forms (e.g., Accrued Benefit, Actuarial Equivalent, Credited Service, Covered Compensation, Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Normal/Early/Late/Disability Retirement, Vested Pension, Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, 75% Survivor Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Single Lump Sum, Cashout Limit, PBGC Rate, FICA Amount, Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner, Pre-2005 and Post-2004 Participants, Section 409A terms).
- Participation and service: Rules for who participates and how service and credited service are determined.
- Eligibility for benefits: Requirements and timing for Normal, Early, Vested, Late, and Disability Retirement Pensions and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension; vesting rules; reemployment provisions; and timing of payments, including small benefit cashouts.
- Benefit amounts and calculations: Formulas for determining the Pre-409A pension, a “PEP Guarantee” to ensure promised equalization levels, survivor benefit calculations, actuarial and other adjustments, and exclusions for certain employment periods.
- Distribution options and elections: Available forms of payment (various annuities and lump sums), timing rules (including Annuity Starting Date rules), advance election procedures, survivor option rules, beneficiary designations, and handling of FICA and related income taxes.
- Administration and claims: Administrative authority (PepsiCo Administration Committee/PAC), claims and appeals procedures, requirement to exhaust plan remedies before litigation, limitations periods for actions, and venue restrictions.
- Miscellaneous provisions: No employment guarantee, anti-alienation, unfunded/nonqualified status, corporate action and indemnification provisions, Section 409A compliance framework (as applicable), authorized transfers, and electronic signatures.
- Amendment/termination and ERISA structure: Company rights to amend or terminate, plan continuation provisions, ERISA plan structure, and applicable law.
- Appendices and special rules: Detailed appendices addressing accruals for 1993/1994, the plan document for Pre-2005 Participants, special early retirement benefits (PFS and P98), provisions for transferred/transition individuals, Pre-409A “PBG” rules and related appendix, and guiding principles for fiduciary committee appointments.

nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE I.
Foreword
nodes.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt introduces the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) for salaried employees participating in the Salaried Plan, explaining that it provides supplemental pension benefits where Qualified Plan benefits are limited by the Internal Revenue Code and, for certain employees, benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula. It traces the Plan’s document history and scope:
- 1989 restatement: governs rights/benefits for employees whose Credited Service ended before 1/1/1989 (and before other earlier effective dates, as applicable).
- 2005 “Pre-409A” document: effective 1/1/2005 and restated through 12/31/2008; clarifies it governs benefits earned and vested on or before 12/31/2004 as grandfathered under Section 409A.
- 2016 restatement: effective 4/1/2016 with no material modifications; incorporates the 12/31/2011 merger of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan. The Pre-409A PBG PEP document (as of 10/3/2004, amended through 1/1/2011, and later as noted) is appended and continues to govern grandfathered PBG benefits, with certain administrative provisions now under the main Pre-409A PEP document. The merger/restatements did not change time or form of payment in a way that would be a material modification under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-6(a)(4).
- 2021 restatement: reflects updates through 1/1/2021, including Salaried Plan actuarial factor updates effective 1/1/2019.
- 2022 restatement: primarily updates claims, exhaustion, limitation, and termination provisions.

The document explains the ongoing integration of the Pre-409A Program with the Section 409A Program: benefits earned/vested after 1/1/1989 are governed by the 409A Program document; together they describe a single plan. Amounts subject to the Pre-409A Program and the 409A Program are tracked separately to preserve the grandfathered status and exemption from Section 409A for Pre-409A benefits.

It then begins Article II (Definitions and Construction), defining key terms, including:
- Accrued Benefit: pension payable at Normal Retirement Date based on Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service.
- Actuarial Equivalent: a benefit of equivalent value determined using specified actuarial assumptions applied uniformly; new rights/features added by amendment do not automatically adopt these factors unless explicitly stated. For annuities with survivor or inflation features and certain period-certain/life forms with Annuity Starting Dates after 12/31/2018, the Plan Administrator specifies the factors to be used (effective 1/1/2019).

nodes.title: Definitions and Construction
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE II.
Definitions and Construction
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases.
nodes.summary:
- Scope and structure
  - Article II defines key terms used in the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program and sets interpretation rules.
  - Article III outlines who participates and how service and credited service are measured (by reference to the Salaried Plan).

- Actuarial Equivalent rules (benefit valuation/conversion)
  - Post-2018 annuity forms: Plan Administrator specifies factors (mortality table and interest rates); effective 1/1/2019, Schedule 1 applies (2019 mortality table; 5% interest for non-inflation forms; 4.2% for 5% inflation; 4.6% for 7% inflation). Factors can be changed by the Plan Administrator and applied retroactively to previously accrued benefits.
  - Pre-2019 annuity forms: use factors then applicable under the Salaried Plan, but ignore post-12/31/2004 factor changes that would increase the annuity (except for the “Limit on the Pre-409A Pension Benefit” in Section 5.1(b)(3)).
  - Lump sums: use Salaried Plan factors, substituting this Plan’s PBGC Rate definition (120% of PBGC termination rate at the Annuity Starting Date). Post-2004 Salaried Plan amendments that would increase (or, for certain post-2014 changes, alter) the lump sum are generally not applied to Pre-409A benefits unless expressly adopted; PPA factors effective 1/1/2008 are generally applied; 2015 lookback/stability changes are not, except for Section 5.1(b)(3).
  - Other adjustments (e.g., early retirement reductions): follow Salaried Plan factors, disregarding post-2004 changes that would increase benefits, except as noted for Section 5.1(b)(3).
  - Application must be uniform and consistent; new plan features may have different factors if specifically adopted.

- Core definitions (selected highlights)
  - Accrued Benefit, Pension (distinguishing Pre-409A vs 409A portions), Retirement Pension types (Normal, Early, Late, Disability), Vested Pension, Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension.
  - Annuity forms and elections: Single Life Annuity, Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity (50%), 75% Survivor Annuity, Single Lump Sum, Advance Election, PEP Election, Annuity Starting Date (with reemployment rule).
  - Service measures: Service and Credited Service determined under the Salaried Plan; Severance from Service Date references Salaried Plan.
  - Earnings and offsets: Highest Average Monthly Earnings (without Code 401(a)(17) cap), Covered Compensation, Primary Social Security Amount (detailed estimation rules for retirement/vested/spouse’s benefits and disability; excludes dependent/spousal/death benefits; fixed as of Severance from Service Date), Taxable Wage Base, FICA Amount under Code 3101, 3121(a), 3121(v)(2).
  - Spousal/partner status: Eligible Spouse (married on earlier of Annuity Starting Date or death). Eligible Domestic Partner (effective 1/1/2019 for active/leave participants): established via valid civil union, enrollment in Company health benefits as domestic partner, or other criteria set by Plan Administrator; cannot have both an Eligible Spouse and an Eligible Domestic Partner; only one Eligible Domestic Partner at a time; definitions of “applicable date” and “state” included.
  - Governance and plan references: Company, PepsiCo Organization (controlled group under Code 414), Plan/Pre-409A Program/409A Program (separate document for 409A), Section 409A, ERISA, Code. Plan Administrator is the PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) or delegates.
  - PAC composition and oversight: Chair is the Company’s SVP, Total Rewards (or acting equivalent); Chair appoints four other experienced members guided by stated principles; semiannual written activity reports made available to U.S.-based executives at least senior vice president.
  - PBGC and PBGC Rate definition for lump sum valuations.

- Construction/interpretation rules
  - Gender/number neutrality; “hereof/hereunder” refer to entire Plan.
  - “Including” and examples are non-limiting (“without limitation”).
  - Document hierarchy and cross-reference conventions (articles, sections, subsections, etc.) clarified.

- Participation and service (Article III)
