  - Participation: An Employee is a Participant while they would currently be entitled to a Pension if employment ended (or would be but for vesting under Section 4.7). Eligibility can later cease and follows all Salaried Plan exclusions.
  - Service and Credited Service used for entitlement and benefit amount are determined under Article III, Part B of the Salaried Plan.

- Effective dates and participant categories
  - Pre-409A Program effective date: 1/1/2005 (specific provisions may have different effective dates).
  - Participant types distinguished: Pre-2005 Participants (terminated employment by 12/31/2004 with rights not materially modified after 10/3/2004) and Post-2004 Participants. Plan Year is calendar year. Normal Retirement Age is 65 or later when 5 years of service is first attained; corresponding Normal and Late Retirement Dates defined.

nodes.title: Participation and Service
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE III.
Participation and Service
nodes.start_phrase: It is expressly contemplated that an Employee, who is entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan as of a particular time, may subsequently cease to be entitled to receive a Pension under the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Defines when an employee is a Participant: during periods they would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be entitled but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7; participation can later cease and is subject to all eligibility exclusions under the Salaried Plan.
- Establishes that entitlement to a pension or a pre-retirement spouse’s pension is based on the participant’s Service, with Service determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Specifies that the amount of both the participant’s pension and the pre-retirement spouse’s pension is based on Credited Service, also determined under Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Introduces Article IV on Requirements for Benefits: participants may receive a Pre-409A pension and eligible surviving spouses may receive survivor benefits; amounts are determined under Article V.
- Normal Pre-409A Retirement Pension eligibility follows Section 4.1 of Part B of the Salaried Plan, ignoring any changes on or after the Effective Date from those in effect as of December 31, 2004; status for amount determination is fixed as of December 31, 2004 (form and timing of payment not fixed).
- Early Pre-409A Retirement Pension eligibility mirrors Section 4.2 of Part B of the Salaried Plan with the same December 31, 2004 freeze for amount determination.
- Pre-409A Vested Pension: available to participants vested under Section 4.7 whose eligible employment ends before qualifying for Normal or Early Pre-409A Retirement Pension (subject to the same post–December 31, 2004 change limitation).

nodes.title: Requirements for Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IV .
Requirements for Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be entitled to receive a Pre-409A Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse shall be entitled to certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article IV outlines eligibility, vesting, timing, and small‑benefit cashout rules for Pre‑409A pensions and survivor benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre‑409A Program; Article V begins the rules for calculating benefit amounts.

- Eligibility categories (frozen to pre‑2005 rules): 
  - Normal, Early, Late, Disability, and Vested Pre‑409A Retirement Pensions mirror the corresponding eligibility provisions of Part B of the Salaried Plan, but disregard any requirement changes on or after the Effective Date from those in effect on December 31, 2004. 
  - For determining the amount (but not the form or timing) of benefits, a participant’s status in each category is fixed as of December 31, 2004. 
  - Late retirement rules exclude any ERISA 203(a)(3)(B) suspension notice requirement and a specific adjustment under Part B Section 5.7(d).

- Pre‑retirement spouse’s benefits:
  - Payable only if the participant dies before his Annuity Starting Date; commencement aligns with the Salaried Plan’s corresponding pre‑retirement spouse’s pension (ignoring post‑Effective Date changes), subject to cashout rules.
  - Active/disabled/retired case: payable if the Eligible Spouse is entitled under the Salaried Plan; for deaths after 12/31/2004, the participant must have met retirement eligibility on that date. Amount determined under Section 5.3.
  - Vested terminated case: payable if the Eligible Spouse is entitled under the Salaried Plan; for deaths after 12/31/2004, the participant must have met vested (but not retirement) requirements on that date. Amount under Section 5.3.
  - If vested spouse coverage is in effect, the participant’s benefit (under Section 5.2(b)) is reduced by an age‑based annual charge for each year of coverage (pro‑rated for partial years); no reduction applies for the 90 days following termination of employment.

- Vesting: A participant is fully vested/nonforfeitable under this plan when fully vested in the Salaried Plan.

- Time of payment and interest:
  - Distributions commence per Section 6.1.
  - Any interest due to delayed payment (under the Salaried Plan’s Part A Section 3.1(e)) accrues only under the 409A Program and is paid with the 409A Pension, consistent with Section 409A limits; no interest is credited for delays caused by the participant.

- Small‑benefit cashouts (limited cashout feature):
  - Participant cashouts: If the actuarial lump sum value of the Pre‑409A Pension is at or below the Cashout Limit on the applicable commencement date, it is paid as a lump sum. Before 12/1/2012, thresholds were $15,000 ($10,000 for Pre‑2005 Participants). The applicable commencement date is generally the month after termination (or the Annuity Starting Date if the value only then falls under the limit), with special coordination before 12/1/2012 with any 409A Pension start.
  - Pre‑retirement spouse cashouts: Similar thresholds and commencement rules, keyed to the month after the participant’s death (or the spouse’s benefit commencement date if the value only then falls under the limit), with coordination before 12/1/2012 with any 409A spouse benefit.
  - Special cashout of vested pensions: The Plan Administrator may, in its discretion, cash out Pre‑409A Vested Pensions in a single lump sum on specified dates in 2012–2014 if the annuity has not started, the value is at/below the Cashout Limit, and it is practicable to calculate/distribute; selections must be documented in writing before each cashout date.
  - Lump sums are in lieu of all other payments and are intended to conform to Treasury Regulations for “limited cashout” features to preserve grandfathered (pre‑409A) status; no participant or spouse election is allowed.

- Reemployment: If a participant is reemployed and eligible to re‑participate in the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, Pre‑409A payments are suspended when (or as if) the Salaried Plan pension is suspended under pre‑2005 terms, and then recommence per Section 6.1 (even if the Salaried Plan pension resumes earlier).

- Article V (amount of benefits) overview:
  - For Post‑2004 Participants, the Pre‑409A Pension (or spouse’s benefit) is determined under Sections 5.1 or 5.3, subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5. For Pre‑2005 Participants, amounts are determined under Appendix Article B.
  - Section 5.1: For Post‑2004 Participants, the Pre‑409A Pension equals Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension, determined on the greater of two specified bases (including a present‑value method as of 12/31/2004 assuming voluntary termination and earliest possible commencement) and subject to a stated limitation; defined terms and detailed calculation rules follow in the remainder of Article V.

nodes.title: Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE V .
Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: When a Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Post-2004 Participant under this Plan, the amount of such Pre-409A Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4 and 5.5.
nodes.summary:
- Article V sets out how Pre-409A retirement benefits are determined, distinguishing Post-2004 Participants (calculated under Sections 5.1 or 5.3) from Pre-2005 Participants (benefits determined under Appendix Article B).
- Section 5.1 (Participant’s Pre-409A Pension):
  - Core formula: Pre-409A Pension = Total Pension − Salaried Plan Pension.
  - Two calculation bases; pay the greater, subject to a cap:
    - Present Value Method: values the benefit as of 12/31/2004 using the Plan’s 2004 Lump Sum Factors, with interest/survivorship to the Earliest Date.
    - Accrued Benefit Method: uses the 12/31/2004 Accrued Benefit with early commencement reductions based on retirement/vested status.
    - Cap: final amount cannot exceed Total Pension minus Salaried Plan Pension calculated at the actual Annuity Starting Date; for this cap, 12/31/2004 “freeze” rules and post-2004 change limitations are not applied.
  - Definitions:
    - Total Pension is the greater of (i) the Salaried Plan benefit ignoring Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and certain deferral adjustments, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2). “Greater of” reflects relative value of payment forms. Generally measured as of 12/31/2004.
    - Salaried Plan Pension is the benefit under the Salaried Plan, generally measured as of 12/31/2004.
- Section 5.2 (PEP Guarantee):
  - Eligibility: 1988 pensionable earnings with an Employer of at least $75,000 (as defined under the Salaried Plan in 1988).
  - Formulas:
    - Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service + 1% of HAME for each year over 10 − 1⅔% of Primary Social Security Amount (PSSA) × years of Credited Service (max 30). Special prorating for Vested Pensions; disability uses service and pay at disability (or earlier date per 5.1(b)).
    - Formula B (for certain pre-7/1/1975 eligible employees): greater of (A) 1½% × HAME × service − 50% of PSSA, or (B) 3% × HAME × service up to 15 years − 50% of PSSA.
  - Special rules and reductions:
    - Default surviving Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner annuity is 50% of the participant’s annuity without reducing the participant’s amount; reduced if the survivor is more than 10 years younger (extra reductions beyond 20 years).
    - Early retirement reduction: 0.25% per month before Normal Retirement Date; vested benefits paid early are reduced to actuarial equivalents; adjustments for elected forms with larger survivor benefits, non-spouse survivors, or inflation-protected annuities to keep actuarial value equivalent.
    - Lump sum payments are the actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, reflecting survivor and early retirement adjustments.
- Section 5.3 (Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pre-409A Pension for Post-2004 Participants):
  - Amount equals Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension minus the Salaried Plan pre-retirement spouse’s pension.
  - Total is the greater of: (i) a Salaried Plan-based calculation (ignoring Code limits and certain deferral adjustments, applying 5.1(b) principles), or (ii) the spouse’s PEP Guarantee-based amount.
  - Normal rule bases the benefit on a hypothetical Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity with appropriate early commencement reductions; special minimum for active/disabled participants provides at least 25% of the participant’s PEP Guarantee (if a comparable benefit exists under the Salaried Plan) without early reduction.
- Section 5.4 (Adjustments):
  - Rehired participants: recalculation if the Salaried Plan benefit is recomputed for additional Credited Service; PEP Guarantee is adjusted for prior/in-service distributions, coordinated with specified plans.
  - Coordination with “specified plans” (the Salaried Plan and similar nonqualified plans): if benefits there increase after PEP is determined, recalculation occurs and overpayments are recoverable; no duplication of payments.
- Section 5.5 (Excludable Employment):
  - Level 22+ executives on limited-duration assignments earn no benefits (or increases) for that assignment after 6/30/1997.
  - For agreements after 1/1/2009, executives who irrevocably waive eligibility or agree not to participate earn no benefits (or increases) thereafter; such agreements can be executed before or after eligibility/participation and are irrevocable once signed.
- Article VI (Distribution Options) overview:
  - Governs distributions of Pre-409A Pensions and any continuation to beneficiaries; Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is paid as a lifetime annuity to the Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner, subject to cashout rules; 409A Program distributions are governed separately.
  - Section 6.1 (Form and timing; subject to cashout rules):
    - For participants without an Advance Election in place by the day before Retirement Date or who terminate before retirement, the Pre-409A Pension is paid in the same form and at the same time as the Salaried Plan benefit.
    - If the Salaried Plan’s Annuity Starting Date occurs while still employed (due to Code §401(a)(9)), plan payments begin the month after Severance from Service, in the same form elected under the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title: Distribution Options
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VI.
Distribution Options
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of this Article govern (i) the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to a Pre-409A Pension, and (ii) the continuation of benefits (if any) to such Participant’ s beneficiary following the Participant’ s death.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article VI governs distribution options for Pre-409A Pensions, including beneficiary continuation after a participant’s death. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pensions are paid as life annuities to eligible spouses/domestic partners (subject to cashout rules). 409A Pensions are handled under a separate 409A Program.
- Form and timing (effective for distributions beginning on/after March 1, 1992 and subject to cashout rules):
  - No Advance Election: Payment form and timing mirror the Salaried Plan; if the Salaried Plan’s annuity start date occurs while still employed, payment here starts the first of the month after severance. If the Salaried Plan form isn’t available under this program, the annuity-form determination rules in 6.1(b)(2) apply.
  - With an Advance Election (must meet 6.3 timing/receipt rules):
    - Lump sum election: single lump sum as of the first of the month on/after Retirement Date.
    - Annuity election: begins first of the month on/after Retirement Date; form set by (i) the participant’s qualifying Salaried Plan annuity election, else (ii) the participant’s PEP Election, else (iii) default to QJSA if married or Single Life if unmarried.
- Available forms of payment (Annuity Starting Dates after 1989):
  - Basic forms: Single Life Annuity; Survivor Options (100%, 75%, 50%—the 50% with spouse is a QJSA); Ten Years Certain and Life.
  - Lump sum: Single Lump Sum.
  - Combination option (only if no Advance Election): split by whole-number percentages between a lump sum and a chosen monthly annuity; calculation rules provided.
- Inflation protection (for annuities only): Optional 5% or 7% thresholds; benefits are initially reduced and then increased annually each January 1 starting the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date by the amount inflation exceeds the chosen threshold, measured using the Social Security COLA method (12 months ending September 30). Carries over to survivor benefits. Irrevocable once elected.
- Vested benefits (Pre-409A Vested Pension): Forms limited to QJSA or 75% Survivor Annuity for married participants, and Single Life Annuity for all; determined per 6.1(a).
- Election procedures:
  - General: Elections/revocations must be written on plan forms; no spousal consent required.
  - Advance Election (available on/after July 15, 1993): Choose annuity or lump sum; must be received before the start of the calendar year containing the Retirement Date and at least 6 months prior; may be changed by a new timely election or revoked by timely written revocation; void if participant is not entitled to a Pre-409A Retirement Pension.
  - PEP Election: Allowed only if an annuity Advance Election is in effect; selects annuity form and inflation protection (lump sum/combination not allowed); must be received no earlier than 180 days (90 days prior to Jan 1, 2007) and no later than the day before the Retirement Date; requires beneficiary age proof; can be changed by a new timely election; effective at close of business the day before the Retirement Date; void if no Advance Election is in effect.
- Annuity Starting Date rules and rehire: Elections apply to all unpaid accruals at the Annuity Starting Date; upon rehire, subsequent elections apply only to post-rehire accruals, with prior accruals continuing under initial elections.
- Administrative timing: An election is treated as received if postmarked that day or actually received by close of business as determined by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Special Rules for Survivor Options:
nodes.heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options :
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant makes a PEP Election for a form of payment described in Section 6.2(a)(2) and the Participant or his beneficiary (beneficiaries in the case of Section 6.2(a) (2)(iv)) dies before the PEP Election becomes ef fective, the election shall be disregarded.
nodes.summary:
- Covers special rules for survivor options tied to PEP Elections under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program.
- Death timing rules:
  - If the Participant or designated beneficiary dies before the PEP Election becomes effective, the election is disregarded.
  - If the Participant dies after the election is effective but before the Pre-409A Retirement Pension begins, the election is honored; survivor payments to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary start the first day of the month after death; any back payments owed to the Participant are paid to the Participant’s estate.
  - For the 120-payments-certain option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): if the Participant dies after the election is effective, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate. If payments to a beneficiary have begun and that beneficiary dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Restrictions when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner:
  - The 100% survivor option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(i)) is not available if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant.
  - The 75% survivor option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(ii)) is not available if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the Participant.
- Beneficiary designation requirements:
  - A beneficiary must be designated for any form including a survivor option, using a PEP Election Form or an approved Salaried Plan form; for the 120-payments-certain option, both a primary and a contingent beneficiary may be named.
  - Participants may change or revoke beneficiary designations any time before the election is finally effective, following Plan Administrator rules; designations are not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.
  - If no beneficiary is properly designated, a survivor option election under Section 6.2(a)(2) is not given effect.
  - A Participant entitled to a Pre-409A Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if permitted an optional form under Section 6.2, the beneficiary defaults to the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary:
nodes.heading: 6.5 Designation of Beneficiary :
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who has elected to receive all or part of his pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Survivor option limits with nonspouse beneficiaries based on age difference:
  - 100% survivor option available if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the participant.
  - 75% survivor option available if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the participant.
- Beneficiary designation rules for survivor options:
  - Participants electing a form with a survivor option must designate a beneficiary using the PEP Election Form or the applicable Salaried Plan form.
  - For the survivor option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv), both a primary and a contingent beneficiary may be named.
  - Participants (active or former) may change or revoke the designation any time before the election becomes finally effective, following Plan Administrator rules.
  - A designation is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.
  - If no beneficiary is properly designated, the participant’s survivor option election under Section 6.2(a)(2) is not given effect.
- Special rule for Pre-409A Vested Pensions:
  - The participant cannot name a beneficiary.
  - If an optional form of payment is permitted under Section 6.2, the beneficiary is automatically the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date.

nodes.title: Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes:
nodes.heading: 6.6 Payment of FICA and Related Income T axes :
nodes.start_phrase: As provided in section 6.7 of the Plan Document for the Section 409A Program, a portion of a Participant’ s 409A Pension, if any , shall be paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”)
nodes.summary:
- Describes how Employment Taxes (FICA, income tax withholding tied to the FICA payment, and additional “pyramiding” withholding) are satisfied: a single lump-sum portion of a participant’s 409A Pension is remitted directly to the IRS or other tax authority. If the 409A Pension is insufficient or not yet in pay status when due, a lump-sum portion of the participant’s Pre-409A Pension is used instead.
- Clarifies these tax remittances are made to applicable federal, state, local, or foreign authorities under Code Section 3401 and analogous provisions.
- Establishes Plan Administration: the Plan Administrator has broad authority to interpret the plan, issue regulations, maintain records, make benefit calculations, and rely on participant-provided information (address, age, marital status). Its determinations are final and binding.
- States neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary of the plan, and ERISA Section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to this nonqualified plan.
- Provides a facility-of-payment rule allowing the Plan Administrator to pay benefits to or for the benefit of a person under legal disability or incapacity, with such payments fully discharging the plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Outlines the claims procedure framework: the Plan Administrator (or its designee) has exclusive discretionary authority to interpret the plan, decide eligibility, and determine benefit amounts; benefits are payable only if approved by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VII.
Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Administration and authority: The Plan Administrator has broad, final, and binding discretion to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, compute benefits, and rely on participant-provided information. Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary, and ERISA §406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply.
- Facility of payment: If a payee is incapacitated or under a legal disability, the Plan Administrator may pay a legal representative or apply benefits for the person’s benefit; such payment fully discharges the Plan’s liability.
- Claims procedure and standard of review: Benefits are payable only if the Plan Administrator decides the claimant is entitled to them. Denials must include reasons, plan references, needed additional information, and review rights within 90 days (extendable to 180). Appeals must be filed within 60 days, with a full and fair review and decision within 60 days (extendable to 120). Judicial review is limited to the administrative record and uses an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard. Notices may be provided under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1.
- Discretion provisions: Specific grants of discretion do not limit the Plan Administrator’s overall discretionary authority, which is intended to be as broad as possible.
- Mandatory exhaustion: Claimants must exhaust the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court. Exhaustion is required as broadly as possible and subsequent actions are limited to the existing record. The Plan Administrator may establish procedures where not specified and may make special arrangements for class or conflict situations. Limited circumstances where failure to exhaust will not be excused are detailed.
- Definitions: “Dispute,” “Claim,” and “Claimant” are defined broadly to cover interpretations, validity, administration, ERISA compliance, benefit requests, fiduciary breach assertions, and any matters relating to the Plan.
- Limitations on actions: A two-year statute of limitations applies to claims for wrongful denial of benefits, interference with ERISA rights, and other claims. Accrual occurs at the earliest of receiving the benefit calculation, identified commencement date, actual/constructive knowledge of relevant facts, or when the benefit is first paid/provided/denied (with specific rules for interference and other claims). The appeals process does not toll the two-year period.
- Venue restriction: Any court action must be brought exclusively in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for claims filed on or after January 1, 2011.
- Miscellaneous:
  - No guarantee of employment; the Plan does not create an employment contract or limit termination rights.
  - Nonalienation: Benefits may not be assigned, pledged, garnished, or otherwise transferred, including in divorce or support situations; the Company is not liable for participants’ debts.
  - Unfunded status: Obligations are payable from the Company’s general assets; participants are unsecured general creditors.
  - Corporate action: Actions under the Plan (including amendments) may be taken by the Board of Directors or its authorized designees.

nodes.title: Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VIII.
Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of an Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to discharge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that the plan does not create an employment contract or guarantee continued employment (right to terminate with or without cause).
- Establishes strong anti-alienation of benefits: plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, or garnished (including in divorce or child support contexts), and the Company is not liable for participants’ debts.
- Confirms the plan is unfunded; obligations are paid from general assets, and participants have the status of unsecured general creditors.
- Authorizes the Company’s Board (and its delegates) to take actions under the plan, including amendments.
- Provides indemnification for employees administering the plan in good faith, to the fullest extent permitted by law unless the Board decides otherwise.
- Requires operation to preserve grandfathered, pre-409A exempt status; post-12/31/2004 changes to the Salaried Plan are disregarded to avoid material modifications under Section 409A.
- States that if a participant transfers to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability for accrued benefits remains with the Company unless an agreement provides otherwise.
- Recognizes electronic signatures and electronic records as legally valid and enforceable.
- Sets out amendment and termination provisions: the Company intends to continue the plan but retains the right to amend, terminate, or partially terminate at any time, subject to Section 409A and applicable law, and without reducing the amount of accrued benefits as of the amendment/termination date unless equivalent benefits are provided elsewhere or as necessary to preserve 409A exemption; specific forms of payment are not protected.
- Allows amendments with or without retroactive effect, including eliminating distribution options before the earlier of the participant’s Annuity Starting Date under this plan or the Salaried Plan, provided no amendment constitutes a “material modification” under Section 409A.

nodes.title: Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IX.
Amendment and T ermination
nodes.start_phrase: This Article governs the Company’ s right to amend and or terminate the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX outlines the Company’s authority to amend, terminate, or partially terminate the Pre‑409A Pension Equalization Plan, subject to Section 409A restrictions to preserve its exemption.
- Continuation: The Company intends to continue the Plan indefinitely but has no contractual obligation to do so. Amendments/terminations cannot reduce a participant’s accrued benefit under Article IV as of the action date unless an equivalent benefit is provided under another plan (and as needed to maintain the Section 409A exemption). Specific payment forms are not protected.
- Amendments: The Company may amend at any time, with or without retroactive effect, including eliminating distribution options before the earlier of a participant’s Annuity Starting Date under this Plan or the Salaried Plan. No amendment may constitute a “material modification” under Section 409A that would subject the Pre‑409A Program to Section 409A. Only the Company (not other Employers) may amend.
- Termination: The Company may terminate the Plan for all Employers or selected Employers; if only some Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for the remaining Employers’ employees.
- Article X defines the ERISA plan structure: together with the 409A Program documents, it comprises three separate ERISA plans effective July 1, 1996 (previously (b) and (c) were a single plan):
  - (a) Excess Benefit Plan under ERISA §3(36), providing benefits above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits for Salaried Plan participants.
  - (b) Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees under ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1), providing benefits above Code §401(a)(17) limits (after the excess benefit plan); for reporting, this portion may be called PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
  - (c) Preservation Top Hat Plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing grandfathered benefits to participants described in Section 5.2(a), preserving pre‑1989 provisions.

nodes.title: ERISA Plan Structure
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE X.
ERISA Plan Structure
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan document in conjunction with the plan document(s) for the 409A Program encompasses three separate plans within the meaning of ERISA, as are set forth in subsections (a), (b) and (c).
nodes.summary:
- Defines the ERISA plan structure (effective July 1, 1996) for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program as three separate plans: (a) an Excess Benefit Plan, (b) an Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan, and (c) a Preservation Top Hat Plan; notes that (b) and (c) were previously a single plan.
- Excess Benefit Plan: an ERISA §3(36) excess benefit plan providing benefits for Salaried Plan participants above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan for a select group of management/highly compensated employees under ERISA §§201(2) and 401(a)(1), providing benefits above the §401(a)(17) compensation limit (after the Excess Benefit Plan); referred to for ERISA reporting as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
- Preservation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan for a select group providing grandfathered benefits that preserve pre-1989 Salaried Plan accrual levels for eligible participants under section 5.2(a) (after considering benefits under the other two plans); referred to for ERISA reporting as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II.
- Specifies allocation order of benefits: first to the Excess Benefit Plan, then to the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan, and finally to the Preservation Top Hat Plan; confirms the three plans are severable for any and all purposes as directed by the Company.
- Sets governing law: ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; where ERISA does not preempt, New York internal law applies.
- Includes a severability clause stating that if any plan provision is invalid or unlawful, the remainder of the plan remains unaffected.

nodes.title: Applicable Law
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE XI.
Applicable Law
nodes.start_phrase: The provisions of this Plan shall be construed and administered according to, and its validity and enforceability shall be governed by , enforced in accordance with, and determined under (1) ERISA and any other applicable federal law as would be applied in cases that arise in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New Y ork, and (2) to the extent ERISA does not preempt state law , the internal laws of the state of New York.
nodes.summary:
- Governing law: The plan is construed, administered, and enforced under ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; where ERISA does not preempt, New York state internal law applies.
- Severability: If any provision is found void, invalid, or unlawful, the remainder of the plan remains in effect.
- Adoption and effective date: The amended and restated plan is effective January 1, 2022, and was adopted on December 21, 2021.
- Execution and approvals: Signed for PepsiCo, Inc. by Ronald Schellekens (Executive Vice President, Human Resources; Chief Human Resources Officer); approved by Jeffrey Arnold (Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel, Law Department) and Christine Griff (Vice President, Tax Counsel, Tax Department).
- Document context: Sections covered are Article XI (Applicable Law) and Article XII (Signature) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program.

nodes.title: Signature
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE XII.
Signature
nodes.start_phrase: This amended and restated Plan is hereby adopted and approved, to be ef fective as of January 1, 2022, this 21st day of December , 2021.
nodes.summary:
- Formal adoption and approval of an amended and restated PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program.
- Effective date set as January 1, 2022; adoption executed on December 21, 2021.
- Signatures and approvals:
  - Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President, Human Resources; Chief Human Resources Officer.
  - Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel, Law Department.
  - Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel, Tax Department.
- Introduction to an Appendix with a Foreword stating:
  - The Appendix contains additional provisions for certain individuals identified within it.
  - In the event of any conflict between the Appendix and the main Plan text, the Appendix controls.

nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX 
Foreword
nodes.start_phrase: This Appendix sets forth additional provisions applicable to individuals specified in the Articles of this Appendix.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix foreword: sets additional provisions for specified individuals and states the Appendix governs over the main Plan text in case of conflict.
- Scope: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program, Appendix Article A, addressing accruals for 1993 and 1994; effective upon Plan adoption.
- Eligibility for special accrual rules (Section A.1): applies to Salaried Plan Participants employed on December 31, 1993, whose Salaried Plan Pension is vested in 1993 (or would vest in 1994 assuming continued service as defined), and whose minimum 1993 Pension is not derived solely from the Plan portion referenced in Article X(c).
- Determination of 1993 and 1994 pension amounts will follow subsections (a) and (b) (only (a) is shown in the excerpt).
- Minimum 1993 Pension (subsection (a)):
  - Participants covered accrue a minimum 1993 Pension as of December 31, 1993.
  - Service and Credited Service are assumed to continue through December 31, 1994 for calculation purposes, unless HR records as of December 31, 1993 show a scheduled 1994 termination, in which case the assumed service only extends to that scheduled date.
  - Highest Average Monthly Earnings as of end of 1993 are to be adjusted using the plan actuary’s salary scale assumption (details truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Accruals for 1993 and 1994
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE A
Accruals for 1993 and 1994
nodes.start_phrase: This Article A of the Appendix shall be ef fective on the date the Plan is adopted.
nodes.summary:
- Article A (Accruals for 1993 and 1994) becomes effective on the Plan’s adoption date and applies to Salaried Plan Participants employed on December 31, 1993, who are vested in 1993 (or would vest in 1994 under assumed continued service) and whose minimum 1993 Pension is not solely from the portion of the Plan referenced in Article X(c).
- Minimum 1993 Pension: Each covered individual accrues a minimum pension as of December 31, 1993, determined by:
  - Assuming Service and Credited Service continue through December 31, 1994, unless HR records show a 1994 scheduled termination, in which case the assumption ends on that date.
  - Adjusting Highest Average Monthly Earnings to projected end-of-1994 levels using the Salaried Plan’s actuarial salary scale, with special rules: use the higher “Special PEP Salary Scale” if it projects higher 1994 earnings; reduce the earnings adjustment if the assumed service ends before year-end 1994.
  - Assuming attained age as of the end of the assumed continued service period.
  - Vesting as of December 31, 1993, for individuals not otherwise vested, in both the regular Pension (ignoring this subsection) and the minimum 1993 Pension. Code section 401(a)(17) is applied for 1993 as amended by OBRA 1993.
- 1994 Accrual: For individuals who receive a minimum 1993 Pension, the 1994 Pre-409A Pension accrual equals only the excess of the pension that would otherwise accrue for 1994 over the minimum 1993 Pension.
- Article B (Plan Document Applicable to Pre-2005 Participants) supplements the main Pre-409A PepsiCo PEP document for Pre-2005 Participants:
  - Capitalized terms follow the main Plan definitions.
  - Main Plan provisions apply except as replaced in Section B.4.
  - When a Pension is payable to or on behalf of a Pre-2005 Participant, Sections 5.1–5.3 in Article B replace the corresponding sections in the main document, with calculations still subject to adjustments under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5 of the main Plan.
  - Section 5.1(a): If the Pension is paid in the same form and starts at the same time as the Salaried Plan pension, the PEP Pension equals the Total Pension (same form/time) minus the Salaried Plan Pension (same form/time).

nodes.title: Plan Document Applicable to Pre-2005 Participants
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE B
Plan Document Applicable to Pre-2005 Participants
nodes.start_phrase: This Article supplements the main portion of the Pre-409A PepsiCo PEP Document with respect to the rights and benefits of Pre-2005 Participants.
nodes.summary:
- Identifies Article B as a supplement to the Pre‑409A PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan for “Pre‑2005 Participants,” stating that main Plan provisions apply except where Article B.4 replaces Sections 5.1–5.3 for these participants, with benefits still subject to specified main Plan adjustments.
- Replaces pension determination rules (5.1–5.3) for Pre‑2005 Participants:
  - 5.1 PEP Pension: Calculates the PEP benefit as either (a) the difference between “Total Pension” and “Salaried Plan Pension” when paid in the same form/time as the Salaried Plan, or (b) a proportional amount when paid in a different form/time, using actuarial value comparisons determined consistently by the Plan Administrator. Defines “Total Pension” as the greater of the uncapped Salaried Plan benefit (ignoring Code §401(a)(17)/§415 limits and a specific actuarial adjustment) or the PEP Guarantee; special Actuarial Equivalent factors apply to lump sums.
  - 5.2 PEP Guarantee: Provides an enhanced formula benefit for those with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings (as defined by the 1988 Salaried Plan), excluding non‑Employer service. Uses Formula A (3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings for first 10 years of Credited Service, 1% thereafter, minus 1⅔% of Primary Social Security Amount up to 30 years) with vesting proration, and for certain employees with pre‑7/1/1975 eligibility compares to Formula B (greater of two alternatives based on 1.5% or 3% multipliers minus 50% of Primary Social Security Amount). Specifies disability calculation rules. Includes:
    - A 50% surviving Eligible Spouse annuity without reduction (with age‑difference adjustments if spouse is >10 years younger).
    - Reductions for early retirement (0.25% per month before Normal Retirement Date), vested early commencement actuarial equivalence and pre‑retirement spouse coverage, richer spouse survivor options, non‑spouse beneficiaries, and inflation‑protected annuities (to preserve actuarial equivalence).
    - Lump‑sum conversion rules requiring actuarial equivalence including survivor and early retirement adjustments.
  - 5.3 Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s Pension: Pays the difference between the Eligible Spouse’s “Total” pre‑retirement spouse benefit (uncapped and without a specified actuarial adjustment) and the Salaried Plan pre‑retirement spouse benefit. Defines a PEP Guarantee‑based pre‑retirement spouse benefit using a QJSA proxy (separation at death, commence at spouse benefit start, death the following day) with early‑start reductions, and a special minimum of 25% of the participant’s PEP Guarantee for active/disabled employees who died before June 1, 2009 (without early reduction).
- Notes that calculations reference Salaried Plan definitions (e.g., Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, Credited Service) and are subject to specified Plan sections on adjustments.
- Introduces Article PFS (PFS Special Early Retirement Benefit): Supplements the Plan for certain PepsiCo Foods Systems employees effective July 11, 1997, defining:
  - Covered Employee as one ineligible for the Salaried Plan Early Retirement Benefit solely due to highly compensated status.
  - Effective Date, the related Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit, Severance Date (qualifying involuntary termination), and PFS as a former division of PepsiCo.

nodes.title: PFS Special Early Retirement Benefit
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE PFS
PFS Special Early Retirement Benefit
nodes.start_phrase: This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees on and after the Ef fective Date.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt covers two appendices to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (Pre‑409A Program):

- Article PFS (PFS Special Early Retirement Benefit): Establishes supplemental rules for “Covered Employees” effective July 11, 1997—specifically employees who are highly compensated and therefore ineligible for the Salaried Plan Early Retirement Benefit. It defines key terms (Article, Covered Employee, Effective Date, Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit, Severance Date, and PFS) and provides a Special Early Retirement Benefit. The benefit is a lump sum, payable as soon as practicable after the Severance Date, equal to the excess of (a) the actuarial present value of the employee’s Total Pension assuming eligibility for the Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit over (b) the actuarial present value of the Total Pension without this appendix. Calculations are as of the Severance Date and remain subject to the Plan’s general limitations and provisions.

- Article PBG (Pre‑409A): Notes the December 31, 2011 merger of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) into the PepsiCo PEP, with this appendix governing PBG PEP benefits grandfathered under Section 409A. It incorporates the PBG PEP document in effect on October 3, 2004, as amended through January 1, 2011, but replaces its administrative and related Articles VII–XI with the corresponding Articles in the main PepsiCo Pre‑409A PEP. For annuity starting dates on or after January 1, 2019, optional annuity adjustments are determined under the main plan’s provisions, and Eligible Domestic Partner provisions from the main plan also apply. The merger does not alter the time or form of payments in a way that would be a material modification under Treas. Reg. §1.409A‑6(a)(4).

nodes.title: Pre-409A
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE PBG
Pre-409A
nodes.start_phrase: Effective as of the end of the day on December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PBG PEP”) was merged with and into the PepsiCo PEP , with the PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan after the Plan merger .
nodes.summary:
- Documents the merger of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) into the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PepsiCo PEP) effective end of day December 31, 2011, with the PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan, and establishes Appendix Article PBG to govern PBG PEP benefits grandfathered under Section 409A.
- Incorporates the PBG PEP document as it existed on October 3, 2004, as amended through January 1, 2011, but excludes Articles VII–XI; for those subjects, the corresponding Articles of the main PepsiCo Pre‑409A PEP apply and cross‑references are to be read accordingly.
- Provides that for annuity starting dates on or after January 1, 2019, actuarial equivalence adjustments for optional annuities are determined under the main plan; also extends the main plan’s Eligible Domestic Partner provisions to Article PBG.
- Affirms that the plan merger and document revisions do not change the time or form of payments in a way that would be a material modification under Section 409A (Treas. Reg. 1.409A‑6(a)(4)).
- Foreword explains PBG’s PEP was established for salaried employees participating in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan to provide benefits exceeding Internal Revenue Code limits and additional benefits based on the pre‑1989 Salaried Plan formula.
- Notes the plan’s initial effective date of April 6, 1999; its status as successor to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (last restated January 1, 1989); the context of PBG’s April 6, 1999 IPO; and that the initial PBG plan closely mirrors the PepsiCo plan for eligibility and benefit determinations.
- Indicates Article II contains defined terms and construction rules for capitalized terms used in the plan.

nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I – Foreword
nodes.start_phrase: The PEP Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PBG for the benefit of salaried employees of the PBG Organization who participate in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (“Salaried Plan”).
nodes.summary:
- Identifies the PEP Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) established by PBG for salaried employees participating in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan.
- States PEP’s purpose: to provide supplemental pension benefits where IRS code limits reduce Salaried Plan benefits, and to provide benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula for certain eligible employees.
- Notes the Plan’s initial effective date of April 6, 1999, coinciding with PBG’s initial public offering.
- Explains that PEP is the successor to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (last restated January 1, 1989) and closely mirrors that plan, including historical provisions relevant to eligibility and benefit determinations.
- Clarifies coverage continuity for employees from Pepsi-Cola Company facilities who moved under PBG.
- Introduces Article II (Definitions and Construction), indicating Section 2.1 provides defined terms used with initial capitals throughout the Plan.
- References integration of a Pre-409A PBG PEP document into an appendix and notes revisions related to that incorporation.

nodes.title: Definitions and Construction
nodes.heading: ARTICLE II – Definitions and Construction
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases listed below .
nodes.summary:
- Foreword and purpose: Establishes the PEP Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) for salaried employees in the PBG/PepsiCo organization who participate in the Salaried Employees Retirement Plan, to provide pension benefits that exceed Internal Revenue Code limits and to preserve certain pre-1989 formula benefits.
- Historical context and effective dates: Plan effective April 6, 1999; successor to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (last restated Jan 1, 1989); aligned with PBG’s April 6, 1999 IPO; document closely mirrors the prior PepsiCo plan for continuity in eligibility and benefit determinations; company/plan references transition between PepsiCo and PBG through 2010.
- Core definitions: Comprehensive glossary for plan terms including Accrued Benefit, Pension, Annuity, Single Lump Sum, Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, Early/Normal/Late/Disability Retirement Pensions, Vested Pension, Eligible Spouse, Employee/Employer, Service/Credited Service, Severance from Service Date, Highest Average Monthly Earnings (without 401(a)(17) cap), Covered Compensation, PBGC and PBGC Rate, Primary Social Security Amount (with detailed estimation assumptions), Plan/Plan Administrator/Plan Year, and elections (Advance Election, PEP Election).
- Actuarial equivalence and valuation rules: Benefits valued using factors from the Salaried Plan; annuities (including survivor and inflation-protected forms) use Salaried Plan factors; lump sums follow Salaried Plan factors but substitute the PBGC Rate defined here (120% of PBGC termination rate at Annuity Starting Date); uniform application and limitations on applicability to future amendments.
- Construction and interpretation: Rules for gender/number, “hereof/hereunder,” “including” interpreted as “without limitation,” and document hierarchy and cross-reference conventions.
- Participation and service crediting: Participation applies when an employee would currently be entitled to a pension (or would be but for vesting); entitlement to participant and pre-retirement spouse benefits is based on Service; Service and Credited Service are determined under the Salaried Plan.
- Benefit framework and cross-references: Article IV sets eligibility for participant and spouse benefits, with amounts determined under Article V; eligibility for a Normal Retirement Pension is tied to the Salaried Plan; numerous operational details (e.g., annuity starting dates after reemployment, election mechanics) reference later sections (e.g., 6.2–6.4) and rely on the Salaried Plan for underlying rules.

nodes.title: Participation and Service
nodes.heading: ARTICLE III – Participation and Service
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant’ s entitlement to a Pension and to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension for his Eligible Spouse shall be determined under Article IV based upon his period of Service.
nodes.summary:
- Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program, following a clause on how paragraph and subparagraph references apply.
- Article III (Participation and Service):
  - Defines when an employee is a Participant: during periods when the employee would be currently entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be entitled but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
  - States that entitlement to a Pension and a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is based on the Participant’s period of Service, with Service determined by Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
  - Provides that the amount of both the Participant’s Pension and the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is based on Credited Service, also determined under Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
- Article IV (Requirements for Benefits):
  - Establishes that Participants may receive a Pension and surviving Eligible Spouses may receive certain survivor benefits under this Article, with benefit amounts determined under Article V.
  - Specifies eligibility for a Normal Retirement Pension by reference to the requirements in Section 4.1 of Part C of the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title: Requirements for Benefits
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IV – Requirements for Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant shall be entitled to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse shall be entitled to certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpts from Articles III (Participation and Service) and IV (Requirements for Benefits) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program, with calculations generally determined under Article V and definitions/eligibility cross-referenced to Part C of the Salaried Plan.
- Participation (3.1): An employee is a Participant during periods when they would be entitled to a pension if employment ended, or would be except for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
- Service (3.2) and Credited Service (3.3): Eligibility for pensions and pre-retirement spouse’s pensions is based on Service; the amount of benefits is based on Credited Service. Both Service and Credited Service are determined under Article III of Part C of the Salaried Plan.
- Benefit eligibility under Article IV:
  - Normal Retirement Pension (4.1): Eligible if requirements in Section 4.1 of Part C of the Salaried Plan are met.
  - Early Retirement Pension (4.2): Eligible if requirements in Section 4.2 of Part C are met.
  - Vested Pension (4.3): Available if vested under Section 4.7 and employment ends before normal/early retirement eligibility; no benefit if not vested.
  - Late Retirement Pension (4.4): No payments until the Late Retirement Date if employment continues past Normal Retirement Age; then determined under Section 4.4 of Part C, without ERISA §203(a)(3)(B) suspension notice or the Section 5.6(d) adjustment of Part C.
  - Disability Pension (4.5): Eligibility follows the Salaried Plan’s disability provisions.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (4.6): Begins when the corresponding benefit under the Salaried Plan begins and continues for the Eligible Spouse’s lifetime, subject to Section 4.9.
  - For survivors of active, disabled, and retired employees (4.6(a)): Payable if entitled under the Salaried Plan; amount per Section 5.3.
  - For survivors of vested terminated employees (4.6(b)): Payable if entitled under the Salaried Plan; amount per Section 5.3. While such coverage is in effect, the Participant’s own pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced annually by an age-based charge (0% up to age 35; 0.075% ages 35–39; 0.1% ages 40–44; 0.175% ages 45–49; 0.3% ages 50–54; 0.5% ages 55–59; 0.5% ages 60–64), pro rata for partial years; no reduction for coverage within 90 days after termination.
- Vesting (4.7): A Participant’s Accrued Benefit becomes fully vested and nonforfeitable when they are fully vested under the Salaried Plan.
- Time of payment (4.8): Distribution of a Participant’s Pre-409A Pension begins as specified in Section 6.1.
- Drafting note: Clarifies application of paragraph/subparagraph references within sections.

nodes.title: Cashout Distributions
nodes.heading: 4.9 Cashout Distributions .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding the availability or applicability of a dif ferent form of payment under Article VI, the following rules shall apply in the case of certain small benefit Annuity payments:
nodes.summary:
- Cashout Distributions (Section 4.9): Establishes rules for mandatory lump-sum cashouts of small Pre-409A Pension benefits.
  - Participant pensions: If the Actuarial Equivalent lump-sum value at the Annuity Starting Date is at or below the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator must pay a lump sum; for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012, the threshold is $10,000.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: Same cashout rule and thresholds apply to Eligible Spouses; $10,000 threshold for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012.
  - Special discretionary cashouts of Vested Pensions: The Plan Administrator may cash out, in a single lump sum, Pre-409A Vested Pensions that have not begun, are at or below the Cashout Limit, and are practicable to calculate and distribute:
    - On December 1, 2012, with written list finalized by November 30, 2012.
    - On the first day of specified months in 2013 or 2014, with written list finalized by the day before the selected date.
  - Any lump sum is in lieu of the annuity otherwise payable. Provisions are intended to preserve grandfathered Pre-409A status and conform to Treasury Regulations on limited cashouts (Treas. Reg. §§ 1.409A-3(j)(4)(v), 1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E)). No participant or spouse may elect whether to be cashed out.

- Coordination with Long-Term Disability (Section 4.10): For periods prior to April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a Normal, Early, Vested, or Disability Pension for any month they are eligible for and receiving employer long-term disability benefits. An Eligible Spouse’s entitlement to a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension or QJSA benefits is not negated by the participant’s receipt of long-term disability at death.

- Reemployment (Section 4.11): If a participant is reemployed and eligible to re-participate in the Salaried Plan after their Annuity Starting Date, payment of this plan’s pension is suspended if the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended. Payments recommence per Section 6.1, even if the Salaried Plan suspension ends earlier.

nodes.title: Coordination with Long Term Disability Plan
nodes.heading: 4.10 Coordination with Long T erm Disability Plan .
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of this section apply notwithstanding the preceding provisions of this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Lump-sum cashouts under Section 4.9 are paid in lieu of the pension otherwise payable and are intended to preserve the grandfathered status of Pre-409A pensions by conforming to the “limited cashout” rules under Treasury Regulations §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v) and §1.409A-6(a)(4)(i)(E); no participant or eligible spouse may elect whether the vested or pre-retirement spouse’s pension is cashed out.
- Coordination with Long-Term Disability: For periods prior to April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a normal, early, vested, or disability pension for any month they are eligible for and receiving employer long-term disability benefits; however, an eligible spouse remains eligible for a pre-retirement spouse’s pension or Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity benefits if the participant dies while receiving LTD.
- Reemployment rules: If a participant is reemployed after their annuity starting date and becomes eligible to re-participate in the Salaried Plan, their Pension payments are suspended to the extent the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended; payments then recommence at the time specified under Section 6.1, even if the Salaried Plan suspension ends earlier.

nodes.title: Reemployment of Certain Participants
nodes.heading: 4.11 Reemployment of Certain Participants .
nodes.start_phrase: In the case of a current or former Participant who is reemployed and is eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, payment of his Pension will be suspended if payment of his Salaried Plan pension is suspended (or would have been if it were already in pay status).
nodes.summary:
- Cashout rules (Section 4.9): Any lump-sum paid under this section replaces the pension otherwise payable to the participant or eligible spouse. The cashout features are intended to comply with Treasury Regulations on “limited cashouts” to preserve the grandfathered status of Pre‑409A pensions, and must be applied consistently with those rules. Participants and eligible spouses have no direct or indirect election over whether vested or pre‑retirement spouse’s pensions are cashed out.

- Coordination with Long-Term Disability (Section 4.10): Despite earlier provisions, for any period before April 14, 1991, a participant cannot receive a normal, early, vested, or disability pension for months when they are eligible for and receiving employer‑provided long‑term disability benefits. However, an eligible spouse remains eligible for a pre‑retirement spouse’s pension or QJSA benefits if the participant was on long‑term disability at death.

- Reemployment (Section 4.11): If a participant is reemployed after their annuity starting date and can reparticipate in the Salaried Plan, payment of their Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) benefit is suspended whenever the Salaried Plan pension is (or would be) suspended. Payments resume at the time specified under Section 6.1.

- Article V – Amount of Retirement Pension: The pension amount is determined under Sections 5.1–5.3, subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5.
  - Section 5.1 (PEP Pension):
    - Same form/time as Salaried Plan: PEP benefit equals Total Pension minus Salaried Plan Pension, both measured in the same form and commencement date.
    - Different form/time: PEP benefit equals the Total Pension in the PEP form/time multiplied by a fraction: (value of Total Pension minus value of Salaried Plan Pension) divided by value of Total Pension. Values are determined on a reasonable, consistent basis by the Plan Administrator for similarly situated employees.
    - Definitions for this section follow (not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.heading: ARTICLE V – Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase: When a Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Participant under this Plan, the amount of such Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1, 5.2 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4 and 5.5.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article V rules for determining the amount of a retirement pension when it becomes payable under the plan.
- States that the amount is determined under Sections 5.1–5.3 and may be adjusted under Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5.
- Details Section 5.1 (PEP Pension) calculation relative to the Salaried Plan:
  - If paid in the same form and at the same commencement time as the Salaried Plan pension, the PEP Pension equals the participant’s Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension, both expressed in that form/time.
  - If paid in a different form or at a different time, the PEP Pension equals the Total Pension in the applicable form/time multiplied by a fraction: (value of Total Pension – value of Salaried Plan Pension) ÷ (value of Total Pension), with values determined reasonably and consistently at the Plan Administrator’s discretion for similarly situated employees.
- Indicates that definitions for this section apply (not included in the excerpt).
- Identifies the plan as the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program.

nodes.title: PEP Pension
nodes.heading: 5.1 PEP Pension :
nodes.start_phrase: Same Form as Salaried Plan: If a Participant’ s Pension will be paid in the same form and will commence as of the same time as his pension under the Salaried Plan, then his Pension hereunder shall be the difference between:
nodes.summary:
- Article V sets out how a Participant’s retirement pension under the Plan is calculated, using Sections 5.1, 5.2, or 5.3, and subject to adjustments in Sections 4.6(b), 5.4, and 5.5.
- Section 5.1 (PEP Pension) defines how the Plan benefit coordinates with the Salaried Plan:
  - Same form/time as Salaried Plan: the Plan benefit equals Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension, both expressed in the same form and commencement date.
  - Different form/time: the Plan benefit equals the Total Pension in the Plan’s chosen form/time multiplied by a fraction: (value of Total Pension − value of Salaried Plan Pension) ÷ value of Total Pension. Values are determined on a reasonable and consistent basis by the Plan Administrator for similarly situated employees.
- Definitions for Section 5.1:
  - Total Pension is the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan benefit calculated without the Code section 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without the actuarial adjustment in Salaried Plan Part C §5.6(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2. Calculations match the specific form and timing; for lump sums, Actuarial Equivalent factors from Article II apply instead of those in the Salaried Plan.
  - Salaried Plan Pension means the benefit determined under the terms of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 5.2 (PEP Guarantee):
  - Applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings.
  - 1988 pensionable earnings are defined as remuneration for 1988 recognized for benefits under the then-effective Salaried Plan.
  - For ineligible Participants, the PEP Guarantee does not apply.

nodes.title: PEP Guarantee
nodes.heading: 5.2 PEP Guarantee :
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who is eligible under subsection (a) below shall be entitled to a PEP Guarantee benefit determined under subsection (b) below .
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Total Pension” as the greater of: (i) the pension under the Salaried Plan calculated without IRC 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without a specified actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee under Section 5.2; calculated based on the elected form and timing of payment, with specified actuarial equivalent (AE) factors for lump sums.
- Defines “Salaried Plan Pension” as the pension amount under the Salaried Plan.
- Establishes PEP Guarantee eligibility for Participants with at least $75,000 of 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer, using earnings recognized under the 1988 Salaried Plan and excluding periods with non-Employers.
- Details PEP Guarantee benefit formulas:
  - Default Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service (CS) plus 1% of HAME for CS over 10 years, minus 1-2/3% of Primary Social Security Amount (PSSA) times CS up to 30 years. For Vested Pensions, the benefit is projected to Normal Retirement Age (NRA) for CS, with HAME and PSSA at severance, then prorated by actual CS over projected CS.
  - For employees in eligible Salaried Plan classifications before July 1, 1975: greater of Formula A or Formula B, with a note that Formula B’s subparagraph (ii)(B) does not apply to Vested Pensions.
  - Formula B: greater of (A) 1.5% of HAME × CS − 50% of PSSA, or (B) 3% of HAME × CS up to 15 years − 50% of PSSA.
  - Disability Pension under either formula uses CS per Salaried Plan rules and HAME/PSSA at disability date.
- Special calculation rules for PEP Guarantee:
  - Surviving Eligible Spouse’s annuity: 50% of the Participant’s annuity, with no reduction to the Participant; reduced if spouse is more than 10 years younger (−0.8% per full year ages 11–20 younger; additional −0.4% per year beyond 20).
  - Reductions:
    - Early retirement: 3/12 of 1% per month before NRA.
    - Vested Pension: AE reduction if commencement before NRA; apply Salaried Plan pre-retirement spouse coverage reductions.
    - If elected form provides a larger spouse survivor benefit than the standard 50%, or a non-spouse survivor, or includes inflation protection, reduce to AE of the standard benefit (single life or non-inflation-protected, as applicable).
  - Lump sum conversion: lump sum equals the AE of the PEP Guarantee including survivor benefit value and any early retirement reductions.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (Section 5.3): payable amount equals the difference between the Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and the Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension; includes a definition of “Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension” (text continues beyond excerpt).

nodes.title: Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension
nodes.heading: 5.3 Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension :
nodes.start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
nodes.summary:
- Explains actuarial adjustments when optional annuity protections are elected, ensuring the total benefit value equals the actuarial equivalent of the elected annuity without such protection.
- Defines Lump Sum Conversion: a lump-sum distribution equals the actuarial equivalent of the participant’s PEP Guarantee, reflecting any survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
- Sets the formula for the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (PRSP): the monthly benefit to a surviving Eligible Spouse equals the Eligible Spouse’s Total PRSP minus the Salaried Plan PRSP.
- Clarifies “Total PRSP” as the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan PRSP calculated without Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and without a specific actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee PRSP; both measured at the applicable payment time.
- Details the PEP Guarantee PRSP:
  - Normal Rule: based on the survivor portion of a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity assuming separation at death (or severance date), commencement when spouse payments begin, and death immediately thereafter; includes early commencement reductions if before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Special Rule for active/disabled employees: minimum PRSP of 25% of the participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service and pay/Social Security figures determined as specified; no early commencement reduction.
- Provides “Certain Adjustments”:
  - Defines “specified plan” (the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans not based on pay deferrals, including the PepsiCo Prior Plan).
  - Requires recalculation for rehired participants whose Salaried Plan benefits are recomputed after their annuity start date; the Pre-409A Pension and PEP Guarantee are adjusted correspondingly for in‑service and prior distributions.

nodes.title: Certain Adjustments
nodes.heading: 5.4 Certain Adjustments :
nodes.start_phrase: Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to adjustment as provided in this section.
nodes.summary:
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension rules:
  - Standard early-commencement reductions apply to the Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity base.
  - Special rule for active or disabled employees: minimum spouse’s benefit equals 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2), with Credited Service determined per Salaried Plan rules; earnings/social security metrics fixed at date of death; no early-commencement reduction under this special rule.

- Pension adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or certain nonqualified plans sponsored by a PBG Organization member and not based on pay deferrals (includes the PepsiCo Prior Plan).
  - Rehired participants: if the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated after reemployment (post–Annuity Starting Date) for added Credited Service, the Pre-409A Pension and PEP Guarantee are also recalculated, adjusting for in-service and prior distributions and coordinating with benefits from this and any specified plans.
  - Increases under other plans: if a specified plan benefit rises after PEP benefits are set, PEP is recalculated; overpayments are recoverable; no duplication of payments across plans.

- Excludable employment (Section 5.5):
  - For employment on/after June 30, 1997, executives at level 22+ on limited-duration assignments do not earn a benefit or benefit increase tied to that assignment.

- Distribution options (Article VI; Section 6.1):
  - Governs form and timing of Pre-409A Pension distributions beginning on/after March 1, 1992; earlier distributions follow the Prior Plan.
  - All distributions subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9.
  - Introduces “No Advance Election” provisions for participants without an advance election in effect (text truncated).

nodes.title: Excludable Employment
nodes.heading: 5.5 Excludable Employment :
nodes.start_phrase: Effective for periods of employment on or after June 30, 1997, an executive classified as level 22 or above whose employment by an Employer is for a limited duration assignment shall not become entitled to a benefit or to any increase in benefits in connection with such employment.
nodes.summary:
- Coordination with other plans: Benefits are determined by considering this Plan and specified plans together to avoid duplication. If a participant’s benefit under a specified plan is increased after PEP benefits are set, the PEP benefit is recalculated and any overpayment may be recovered.
- Excludable Employment: Effective June 30, 1997, executives at level 22 or above on limited-duration assignments do not accrue benefits or increases from that employment.
- Distribution Options (Article VI): Establishes how benefits are distributed when a participant becomes entitled to a pension.
- Form and Timing of Distributions (Section 6.1): Governs distributions of Pre‑409A pensions beginning on or after March 1, 1992; earlier distributions follow the prior plan; all distributions are subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9.
- No Advance Election (Section 6.1(a)): Provides rules for participants without an Advance Election in effect (details truncated).

nodes.title: Distribution Options
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VI – Distribution Options
nodes.start_phrase: The terms of this Article govern the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to payment of a Pension under the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Coordination with other plans: Benefits are calculated with reference to the Salaried Plan while taking into account benefits provided under this Plan (the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan, Pre‑409A Program) and any specified plans, to avoid duplication.
- Adjustment for increases under other plans: If a participant’s benefit under a specified plan is increased after PEP benefits have been determined (e.g., by court order, plan administrator agreement, or otherwise), the PEP benefit will be recalculated. Any resulting overpayment may be recovered by the Plan Administrator. The intent is to prevent duplicate payments across plans.
- Excludable employment: For employment periods on or after June 30, 1997, executives at level 22 or above on limited‑duration assignments are not entitled to a benefit or to any increase in benefits attributable to that assignment.
- Distribution options (Article VI): Sets rules for how pensions are distributed once a participant becomes entitled to payment.
- Form and timing of distributions (Section 6.1): Governs distributions of Pre‑409A pensions beginning on or after March 1, 1992; earlier distributions follow the Prior Plan in effect at that time. All distributions are subject to the cashout rules in Section 4.9. Introduces a “No Advance Election” provision for participants without an advance election in effect, with details continuing beyond the excerpt.

nodes.title: Form and Timing of Distributions
nodes.heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions :
nodes.start_phrase: This section shall govern the form and timing of distributions of Pre-409A Pensions that begin on or after March 1, 1992.
nodes.summary:
- Coordination with other plans and overpayment recovery: If a participant’s benefit under a specified plan increases after PEP benefits are determined, the PEP benefit is recalculated to prevent duplication of payments, and any overpayment under the PEP may be recovered.  
- Excludable employment rule: Effective June 30, 1997, executives at level 22+ on limited-duration assignments do not earn PEP benefits or increases tied to that assignment.  
- Article VI scope: Governs how Pre-409A Pensions are distributed, applying to distributions starting on or after March 1, 1992, and subject to the Plan’s cashout rules.  
- Default distribution without an Advance Election: If no Advance Election is in place by the day before Retirement Date (or if employment ends before Retirement), the PEP benefit is paid in the same form and at the same time as the Salaried Plan benefit.  
- Special timing if still employed at Salaried Plan annuity start: If the Salaried Plan Annuity Starting Date occurs while the participant is still employed (due to Code section 401(a)(9)), PEP payments begin the first of the month after the Severance from Service Date, using the same form as the Salaried Plan.  
- Use of an Advance Election (for retirements after 1993): Must meet timing and procedural requirements; governs form and start date of PEP distributions.  
- Lump sum with Advance Election: If a Single Lump Sum is elected in advance, it is paid on the first of the month coincident with or following the Retirement Date.  
- Annuity with Advance Election: If an annuity is elected in advance, it begins on the first of the month coincident with or following the Retirement Date.  
- Determining annuity form when an annuity is elected:  
  - If there is a qualifying Salaried Plan election specifying an annuity (in effect as of the day before Retirement Date), the PEP annuity mirrors that form.  
  - If no qualifying Salaried Plan election, but a PEP Election exists, the PEP pays the annuity form chosen in the PEP Election.  
  - If neither election applies, default is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if married, or a Single Life Annuity if unmarried (marital status measured the day before Retirement Date).  
- Available forms reference: Section 6.2 notes that specified forms of payment are available to any participant entitled to a Retirement Pension (details follow beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Available Forms of Payment
nodes.heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment :
nodes.start_phrase: The forms of payment set forth in subsections (a) and (b) may be provided to any Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the hierarchy for determining a participant’s payout form:
  - If there is a qualifying Salaried Plan election in effect as of the day before Retirement Date and it specifies any annuity form (including when paired with a lump sum), the same annuity form applies.
  - If not, but a PEP Election is in effect as of the day before Retirement Date, the annuity form in that election applies.
  - If neither applies, the default is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity (QJSA) for married participants or a Single Life Annuity for unmarried participants; marital status is measured the day before Retirement Date.
- Lists available payment forms for Retirement Pensions (effective for Annuity Starting Dates after 1989; earlier distributions follow the Prior Plan):
  - Single Life Annuity (lifetime monthly payments ending at death).
  - Survivor annuities:
    - 100% Survivor Option (same reduced amount to beneficiary for life).
    - 75% Survivor Option (75% of reduced amount to beneficiary for life).
    - 50% Survivor Option (50% of reduced amount to beneficiary for life; counts as a QJSA if beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse).
