    - Ten Years Certain and Life (lifetime payments with at least 120 monthly payments guaranteed to beneficiary if death occurs earlier).
  - Single Lump Sum payment.
  - Combination Lump Sum/Monthly Benefit (permitted only if no Advance Election is in effect), with participant-designated whole-number percentages that total 100%; lump sum and monthly portions are each prorated by the elected percentages.
- Describes optional inflation protection (not available on lump sums):
  - Two levels: 5% or 7% thresholds. Monthly benefits are initially reduced, then increased each January 1 (starting the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date) by the amount prior-year inflation exceeds the elected threshold.
  - Inflation measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the method applicable to Social Security COLAs as of January 1, 1989.
  - Increases carry over to survivor benefits; elections are irrevocable by the participant and any surviving beneficiary.
- Specifies forms for vested (non-retirement) benefits:
  - Married participants: QJSA.
  - All participants: Single Life Annuity is available.
  - Specific form determined under Section 6.1(a).
- Outlines election procedures (Advance Elections and PEP Elections):
  - Must be made in writing on a Plan Administrator–designated form and signed by the participant (section continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Procedures for Elections
nodes.heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections :
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Advance Elections and PEP Elections.
nodes.summary:
- 7% inflation protection option: Monthly benefits are initially reduced but increase each January 1 if prior-year inflation exceeds 7%, by the amount over 7%. First increase occurs the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date. Inflation is measured over the 12 months ending September 30 using the Social Security COLA method in effect on January 1, 1989. Protection carries over to survivor benefits, and the election is irrevocable.
- Vested benefit forms: Married Participants receive a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity; a Single Life Annuity is available to both married and unmarried Participants, per Section 6.1(a).
- Election procedures (Section 6.3): Elections and revocations must be written, on Plan forms, and signed; no spousal consent required.
- Advance Election: 
  - Made on/after July 15, 1993; choose Annuity or Single Lump Sum.
  - Must be received before the start of the calendar year containing the Retirement Date and at least 6 months before the Retirement Date.
  - Remains effective until changed by a new timely election; revocable only if revocation meets the same timing; void if no entitlement to a Retirement Pension.
- PEP Election:
  - Available only if an Advance Election for an Annuity is in effect (advance receipt rule is deemed met if it will be by the proposed Retirement Date).
  - Participant selects an annuity form from Section 6.2 and may elect inflation protection; forms in 6.2(a)(3) and (4) are not available via PEP.
  - Must be received 90 days to the day before the Retirement Date; beneficiary age proof due by the day before the Retirement Date if required for reductions.
  - Can be changed by a new timely PEP Election; becomes effective at close of business the day before Retirement Date; void if no Advance Election in effect.
- Annuity Starting Date rules: Elections at an Annuity Starting Date apply to all unpaid accruals then due. If rehired after an initial Annuity Starting Date (with an annuity in pay or after a prior lump sum other than a small cashout), subsequent elections apply only to benefits accruing after rehire; prior accruals continue under prior elections.
- Receipt timing: An election is treated as received if postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator by close of business (as determined by the Administrator).
- Survivor options—effect of death around PEP Elections: If the Participant or beneficiary dies before a PEP Election (for forms under 6.2(a)(2)) becomes effective, the election is disregarded. If the Participant dies after the PEP Election is effective but before payments begin, the election is honored; survivor benefits start the first day of the month after death, with any back payments to the Participant’s estate.

nodes.title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
nodes.heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options :
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant makes a PEP Election for a form of payment described in Section 6.2(a)(2) and the Participant or his beneficiary (beneficiaries in the case of Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)) dies before the PEP Election becomes ef fective, the election shall be disregarded.
nodes.summary:
- Rehired participants after an initial Annuity Starting Date:
  - If already receiving an annuity in pay status upon rehire, or previously took a lump sum (other than a Section 4.9(a) cashout), any new Annuity Starting Date and related elections apply only to benefits accrued after rehire.
  - Prior accruals continue to be paid under the elections made at the initial Annuity Starting Date.
- Election timing:
  - An election is treated as received if postmarked that day or actually received by the Plan Administrator by close of business (as determined by the Administrator).
- Special rules for survivor options (Section 6.4):
  - Effect of certain deaths:
    - If the Participant or beneficiary dies before a PEP Election becomes effective, the election is disregarded.
    - If the Participant dies after the PEP Election becomes effective but before payments start, the elected form is honored; survivor benefits begin the first day of the month after death, and any back payments due to the Participant are paid to the estate.
    - For the option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv): if the Participant dies after the PEP Election is effective, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and before receiving 120 payments, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate. If a beneficiary had begun receiving payments and dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - Nonspouse beneficiary age limits:
    - 100% survivor option is not permitted if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant.
    - 75% survivor option is not permitted if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the Participant.
- Beneficiary designations (Section 6.5):
  - Required for forms with survivor options; made on a PEP Election Form or applicable Salaried Plan form.
  - For the Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv) option, both a primary and contingent beneficiary may be named.
  - Participants may change or revoke beneficiary designations any time before the election is finally effective, subject to Plan Administrator rules.
  - A designation (or change/revocation) is not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.heading: 6.5 Designation of Beneficiary :
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who has elected to receive all or part of his pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies payment continuation rules: if a participant dies without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary and before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the participant’s estate; if a beneficiary dies after payments have begun but before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Sets limits for nonspouse beneficiaries: the 100% survivor option is not allowed if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the participant; the 75% survivor option is not allowed if the nonspouse beneficiary is more than 19 years younger.
- Establishes beneficiary designation procedures: participants electing a survivor option must designate beneficiaries on the PEP Election Form or approved Salaried Plan form; for the option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv), both primary and contingent beneficiaries may be named; designations can be changed or revoked before the election is final; designations are effective only when filed with the Plan Administrator (or Prior Plan Administrator for pre-effective-date periods); if no beneficiary is properly designated, the survivor option election under Section 6.2(a)(2) is not effective.
- Introduces an Appendix to Article PBG: states that the appendix provides additional provisions for specified individuals and will govern in the event of any conflict with the main plan text.

nodes.title: Foreward
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX T O AR TICLE PBG
FOREW ARD
nodes.start_phrase: This Appendix sets forth additional provisions applicable to individuals specified in the Articles of this Appendix.
nodes.summary: Foreword to an appendix of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program stating that the appendix contains additional provisions applicable to certain individuals identified within its articles, and establishing that, in the event of any conflict with the main plan text, the appendix will govern.

nodes.title: 1993 Accruals
nodes.heading: ARTICLE A – 1993 Accruals
nodes.start_phrase: This Article A of the Appendix shall be ef fective on the date the Plan is adopted.
nodes.summary:
- Article A – 1993 Accruals: Effective upon plan adoption; establishes who qualifies for special 1993 accrual treatment and how benefits are calculated.
  - Eligibility: Salaried Plan Participants employed on December 31, 1993, vested in 1993 (or would vest in 1994 with assumed continued service), and whose minimum 1993 Pension is not derived solely from the portion described in Article X(c) of the main plan.
  - Minimum 1993 Pension: Accrued as of December 31, 1993, using assumptions that:
    - Service and Credited Service continue through December 31, 1994, unless HR records show a scheduled 1994 termination, in which case only through that date.
    - Highest Average Monthly Earnings are projected to end of 1994 using the plan’s actuarial salary scale; a higher “Special PEP Salary Scale” is used if it projects higher 1994 earnings; if service is assumed to end during 1994, earnings after termination are excluded.
    - Attained age is assumed as of the end of the assumed continued service period.
  - Vesting: Any covered individual not otherwise vested becomes vested as of December 31, 1993 in both the regular Pension and the minimum 1993 Pension.
  - Limits: Code section 401(a)(17) applies for 1993 as amended by OBRA 1993.
  - Later Accruals: For participants with a minimum 1993 Pension, any Pre‑409A Pension accrued after 1993 is only the amount exceeding that minimum.

- Article P98 – PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit: Supplements the main plan for certain employees effective February 1, 1998.
  - Defines key terms:
    - Covered Employee: An employee who fails to meet Salaried Plan Early Retirement eligibility solely because they are a highly compensated employee, as defined in Article S and Section S.3(a)(4) of the Appendix to the Legacy PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (Part C).
    - Effective Date: February 1, 1998.
    - Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit: As referenced in Section S.3(b) of the same Appendix.
    - Severance Date: The qualifying involuntary termination under Section S.2(b)(1) that establishes Covered Employee status.

nodes.title: PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit
nodes.heading: ARTICLE P98 – PepsiCo Special Early Retirement Benefit
nodes.start_phrase: This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and benefits of Covered Employees on and after the Ef fective Date.
nodes.summary:
- Article P98 establishes a Special Early Retirement Benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre‑409A Program for certain “Covered Employees” effective February 1, 1998.
- Covered Employee is defined as an employee ineligible for the Salaried Plan Early Retirement Benefit solely due to highly compensated status under the Legacy PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan provisions; other key definitions include Effective Date, Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit, and Severance Date (an eligible involuntary termination).
- Benefit amount and form: A Covered Employee receives a single lump-sum payment, as soon as administratively practicable after the Severance Date, in lieu of any other benefits under the Plan. The lump sum equals:
  - The actuarial present value of the Total Pension as of the Severance Date, assuming eligibility for the Salaried Plan Special Early Retirement Benefit and commencement on the Severance Date,
  - Minus the actuarial present value of the Salaried Plan Pension as of the Severance Date, determined without this Appendix and assuming commencement at Normal Retirement Date.
- Calculations use actuarial equivalence factors in effect on the Severance Date for lump-sum conversions, assume a Single Life Annuity form, and, if applicable, substitute more favorable PEP Guarantee early commencement reduction factors (Section 5.2) for the Salaried Plan’s early reduction factors in determining the Total Pension component.
- Article IPO covers Transferred and Transition Individuals following the spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan, relying on definitions and terms in the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.
- Rights preserved: Transferred Individuals participating in the PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately before the Effective Date become Participants in this Plan as of the Effective Date; the spin-off causes no break in Service or Credited Service for Transferred or Transition Individuals; service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations are preserved per the Agreement as of the Close of the Distribution Date.

nodes.title: Transferred and Transition Individuals
nodes.heading: Article IPO – T ransferred and T ransition Individuals
nodes.start_phrase: This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and benefits of T ransferred and T ransition Individuals following the spinof f of this Plan from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Article IPO addresses how the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – Pre-409A Program treats Transferred and Transition Individuals after the plan’s spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
- It defines key terms by reference to the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement (Agreement): Agreement, Close of the Distribution Date, Transferred Individual, and Transition Individual.
- All Transferred Individuals who participated in the PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately before the Effective Date automatically become Participants in this Plan as of the Effective Date.
- The spin-off does not cause a break in Service or Credited Service for Transferred or Transition Individuals.
- Service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations recognized under the PepsiCo Prior Plan through the Close of the Distribution Date receive full recognition under this Plan as of the Effective Date, avoiding duplication of benefits.
- Benefits for Transition Individuals are determined per section 8.02 of the Agreement.

- Article PAC sets guiding principles for appointing members to the Plan Administration Committee (PAC).
- Membership requirements include being a PepsiCo Organization employee at Band 1 or above, the ability to devote adequate time, and fiduciary character to act prudently in participants’ best interests.
- Additional guidelines emphasize experience in benefit plan/ERISA administration, collective expertise across health, welfare, and retirement plans, and the ability to evaluate plan expenses.
- The PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified committee candidates.

nodes.title: Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.start_phrase: This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to the appointment of the members of the P AC.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes guiding principles for appointing members to PepsiCo’s Pension Administrative Committee (PAC) under the Pension Equalization Plan.
- Eligibility criteria: must be a PepsiCo employee at Band 1 or above, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character and temperament to act prudently and solely in the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries.
- Additional membership guidelines: prior benefit plan administration or transferable ERISA-related experience; the committee collectively should have expertise across ERISA health, welfare, and retirement plans; each member must be able to evaluate the reasonableness of plan expenses.
- The PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified candidates.
- These guidelines are advisory to the Chair and do not alter ERISA’s legal standards.
- The excerpt also indicates a transition to the Section 409A Program Plan Document (January 1, 2022 Restatement).

structure.title: PEPSICO PENSION EQUALIZATION PLAN (PEP) Plan Document for the Section 409A Program January 1, 2022 Restatement
structure.heading:
Exhibit 10.10
PEPSICO
PENSION EQUALIZA TION PLAN
(PEP)
Plan Document for the Section 409A Program
January 1, 2022 Restatement
structure.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
structure.summary:
- Identity and purpose: Restated January 1, 2022 Plan Document for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) Section 409A Program. Provides nonqualified supplemental pension benefits to salaried employees participating in the qualified Salaried Plan whose qualified benefits are limited by Internal Revenue Code caps, and preserves certain pre‑1989 Salaried Plan formula benefits for eligible employees.
- History and scope: 1989 restatement; comprehensive 2005 restatement to address Section 409A for post‑2004 accruals or materially modified benefits; subsequent amendments incorporating a plan merger with the PBG Pension Equalization Plan effective December 31, 2011. The PBG plan’s 409A terms are preserved in an appendix, with administrative provisions aligned to this document. No change to time or form of 409A payments.
- Core definitions and construction: Extensive defined terms governing calculations and administration (e.g., Accrued Benefit, Actuarial Equivalent, Annuity/Starting Date, Cashout Limit, Covered Compensation, Credited Service, various 409A retirement pensions, Disability, Key Employee, Separation from Service, Single Lump Sum, Vested Pension, Plan Administrator, Plan Year), plus construction rules.
- Participation and service: Who participates, how service is measured (Elapsed Time and other rules), and how Credited Service is determined.
- Benefit eligibility requirements: Conditions for Normal, Early, Late 409A Retirement Pensions; 409A Disability Pension; 409A Vested Pension; Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s and Domestic Partner’s 409A Pensions; vesting rules; timing of payments; cashout distributions; reemployment effects; forfeiture provisions.
- Benefit calculations: Methods for determining a Participant’s 409A pension; PEP Guarantee; spousal and domestic partner death benefits; adjustments; offsets; treatment of excludable employment; coordination with pre‑409A pension amounts.
- Distributions: Available forms and timing (including annuities and lump sums); election procedures; survivor options; beneficiary designations; required six‑month delay for Key Employees under Section 409A; FICA and related tax withholding timing.
- Administration: Authority and responsibilities to administer; facility of payment; detailed claims and appeals procedures; requirement to exhaust plan remedies before litigation; limitations periods; venue restrictions; effect of specific references.
- Miscellaneous legal provisions: No guarantee of employment; anti‑alienation; unfunded status; corporate action and indemnification provisions; compliance with Sections 409A and 457A; authorized transfers.
- Amendment and termination: Continuation, amendment, and termination mechanics; provisions addressing change in control.
- ERISA structure, applicable law, and signature.
- Appendices covering special rules and populations, including: transition provisions; earnings/service during severance windows; international and PIRP transfers; Band 4+ rehired Yum participants; severance‑window payment timing; U.K. supplement for U.S. service; delay elections for certain pre‑2018 terminees; historic domestic partner definitions; 409A makeup for certain pre‑409A benefits; certain international employees who are U.S. persons; a comprehensive PBG appendix (history, definitions, participation, benefits, death benefits, distributions); and guiding principles for Benefit Plan Fiduciary Committee (PAC) appointments.

nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE I
Foreword
nodes.start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) provides supplemental pension benefits to salaried employees who participate in the Salaried Plan, making up for benefits limited by Internal Revenue Code caps, and also includes certain benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula for eligible employees.

- Restatement history: The Plan was restated in 1989, then comprehensively restated effective January 1, 2005 to establish the Section 409A program terms. Subsequent restatements occurred effective January 1 of 2017, 2019, 2021, and 2022 (the current restatement).

- Section 409A coverage: The 2005 restatement governs benefits subject to Section 409A (generally amounts earned or vested after December 31, 2004 or materially modified under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-6(a)(4)).

- Merger with PBG PEP: Effective December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan merged into this Plan. The 409A PBG PEP document (as of April 1, 2009, amended through January 1, 2011) is attached as an appendix and continues to govern pre-merger PBG PEP 409A benefits, with certain administrative provisions now governed by the main 409A PepsiCo PEP document. The merger and updates did not change the time or form of payment for 409A benefits.

- Interplay of 409A and pre-409A programs: Benefits not subject to the 409A Program (generally earned or vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially modified) are governed by the Pre-409A Program document. Both documents together describe a single plan, but 409A and pre-409A amounts are tracked separately to preserve grandfathered, 409A-exempt status.

- Linkage to the Salaried Plan and 2025 freeze: PEP accruals and eligibility to “grow into” benefit enhancements generally mirror those under the Salaried Plan. Special provisions (including the “PEP Guarantee” in Section 5.2 and certain appendix provisions) may provide accruals beyond strict make-up for Code limits for some participants. The freeze of the Salaried Plan effective end of day December 31, 2025 also freezes all PEP accruals as of that time, and post-freeze grow-in rules follow the Salaried Plan’s operational rules.

- Definitions section begins: Article II introduces defined terms used throughout the document.

- Key defined terms excerpted:
  - Accrued Benefit: The pension payable at Normal Retirement Date per Article V, based on Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service at the determination date.
  - Actuarial Equivalent: A benefit of equal value determined using specified actuarial factors applied uniformly; new rights/features/benefits use these factors only if expressly adopted. For annuity forms (e.g., qualified joint and survivor, survivor annuities, inflation-protected annuities, period certain and life), the Plan Administrator selects the factors; effective January 1, 2009, factors are in Schedule 1 (prior factors in the appendix).

nodes.title: Definitions and Construction
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE II
Definitions and Construction
nodes.start_phrase: This section provides definitions for certain words and phrases listed below .
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article II (Definitions and Construction) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program and the start of Article III (Participation and Service).
- Actuarial Equivalent and payment factors: sets Plan Administrator authority over actuarial factors; includes Schedule 1 mortality tables and interest rates (GAR 94 through 12/31/2018; 2019 mortality table thereafter; distinct factors for 5% and 7% inflation protection); allows retroactive application with a floor tied to 2019 Salaried Plan factors; lump sums use Salaried Plan lump-sum factors; other adjustments follow Salaried Plan (including 2019 updates).
- Core plan definitions: Accrued Benefit, Annuity, Annuity Starting Date, Cashout Limit, Code, Company, Covered Compensation, Credited Service, Disability/Normal/Early/Late/ Vested 409A Pensions, Elapsed Time Service, Employee/Employer, ERISA, FICA Amount, 409A Program, Highest Average Monthly Earnings (without 401(a)(17) cap), Participant, Pension (409A vs. Pre-409A), Plan/Plan Year/Pre-409A Program, Salaried Plan, Section 409A, Service, Social Security Act, Taxable Wage Base.
- Spouse and partner eligibility: detailed post-1/1/2019 definition of Eligible Domestic Partner (civil union, health plan enrollment, or other written criteria; one partner maximum; cannot have both spouse and partner); Eligible Spouse defined under federal tax law.
- Governance: PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) composition, chair designation, appointment principles, expertise requirements, and semiannual activity reports; reference to Guiding Principles for appointments.
- Key Employee rules: identification under Code §§416/409A with officer/owner thresholds; administrative convenience adding Leadership Group 6+ (capped at 200); historical transition rules (2010–2018) across PepsiCo/PBG/PAS; timing of annual identification and effectiveness periods; compensation definition per Treas. Reg. §1.415(c)-2.
- Social Security coordination: Primary Social Security Amount assumptions for retirement/survivor and disability calculations (age-65 estimate rules, exclusions, law as of separation).
- Conduct restrictions: Prohibited Misconduct (competition in Covered Products, non-solicit, confidentiality breaches, code/securities violations, fraud) with DTSA and government reporting protections; broad “Participation” and detailed “Covered Products” definitions.
- Benefit forms and options: Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Single Lump Sum; survivor/period-certain and inflation-protection adjustments per schedules; pre-retirement spouse’s and domestic partner’s pensions.
- Separation from Service: 409A-compliant standards (20% service threshold; leave-of-absence rules including 6-month and 29-month disability substitutions; director services disregarded; certain transfers to 20%+ owned entities not separations); Final Separation from Service concept.
- Construction rules: grammar/number conventions; “hereof/hereunder” usage; “including” read as without limitation; document hierarchy and cross-reference conventions.
- Participation and Service (Article III start): who qualifies as a Participant (currently entitled or but for vesting; status may later cease); eligibility exclusions mirror the Salaried Plan; entitlement and pre-retirement survivor benefits based on Service determined under the Salaried Plan (noting an exception for certain inpats).

nodes.title: Participation and Service
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE III
Participation and Service
nodes.start_phrase: 3.1 Participation : An Employee shall be a Participant in the Plan during the period:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Excerpts from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program covering Article III (Participation and Service) and part of Article IV (Requirements for Benefits).

- Participation (Art. III, Sec. 3.1):
  - An employee is a Participant during any period when they would currently be entitled to a Pension under the Plan, or would be but for the vesting requirement in Section 4.7.
  - Entitlement can later cease.
  - All eligibility exclusions from the Salaried Plan apply.

- Service rules (Sec. 3.2):
  - Eligibility for a Pension or, if death occurs before benefits start, a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pension, is based on Service as defined in Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Inpats: Provisions that disregard pre-transfer Service for certain inbound transfers to the U.S. do not apply to this Plan before Jan 1, 2015, unless needed to prevent benefit duplication.
  - Leaves of absence: If Service would extend past Separation due to a leave, the Plan Administrator may project benefits at Separation as if such Service were included.

- Credited Service (Sec. 3.3):
  - Pension and pre-retirement survivor benefits are based on Credited Service per Article III of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Inpats: Rules that disregard pre-transfer Credited Service do not apply to individuals transferring before Oct 1, 2014, unless needed to avoid duplication with the Salaried Plan.
  - Leaves of absence: Similar projection authority at Separation for Credited Service.

- Requirements for Benefits (Art. IV):
  - General: Participants may receive a Pension; eligible surviving spouses or domestic partners may receive survivor benefits, with amounts determined under Article V.
  - Normal 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.1): Separation after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
  - Early 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.2): Separation before Normal Retirement Age, with at least age 55 and 10+ years of Elapsed Time Service.
  - 409A Vested Pension (Sec. 4.3): Available if vested under Section 4.7 and Separation occurs before Normal/Early eligibility; no benefit if vesting is not met.
  - Late 409A Retirement Pension (Sec. 4.4): No payments until Late Retirement Date for those working past Normal Retirement Age; amount determined under Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title: Requirements for Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IV
Requirements for Benefits
nodes.start_phrase:
A Participant shall be eligible to receive a Pension and a surviving Eligible Spouse or surviving Eligible
Domestic Partner , as applicable, shall be eligible for certain survivor benefits as provided in this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article IV (Requirements for Benefits) and the start of Article V (Amount of Retirement Pension) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

- Eligibility for pensions:
  - Normal 409A Retirement Pension: payable upon separation from service at or after Normal Retirement Age.
  - Early 409A Retirement Pension: payable upon separation before Normal Retirement Age after at least age 55 and 10+ years of Elapsed Time Service.
  - 409A Vested Pension: payable if vested under Section 4.7 and separated before qualifying for Normal/Early; no benefit if vesting not met.
  - Late 409A Retirement Pension: for those working past Normal Retirement Age; payments begin at Late Retirement Date and are determined by Part B of the Salaried Plan with specified exceptions.
  - 409A Disability Pension: available if the Salaried Plan disability criteria are met; split into Pre-Separation Accruals and Post-LTD Accruals (to the earlier of age 65, Salaried Plan benefit commencement, or recovery).

- Survivor benefits before retirement:
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: payable if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date; starts the month after the later of death or the date the participant would have turned 55; amount determined under Section 5.3 (after applying Section 5.6). For vested terminated employees, the participant’s benefit is reduced by an age-based annual charge for each year spouse coverage is in effect; no reduction for coverage within 90 days after termination.
  - Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: similar structure and commencement; amounts under Section 5.8 (after Section 5.6). For vested terminated employees, participant’s benefit is reduced by an age-based annual charge; no reduction for coverage within 180 days after termination.

- Vesting: Full vesting in the 409A Accrued Benefit occurs when fully vested under Part B of the Salaried Plan (subject to Section 8.7 related to Code section 457A).

- Time of payment and interest: 409A Pension distributions commence per Section 6.1 (subject to Section 6.6). Any interest due to delayed payment (per Salaried Plan rules) accrues under the 409A Program and is paid with the 409A Pension, but no interest is paid if the delay is participant-caused or prohibited by IRS 409A correction guidance.

- Small-balance cashouts (limited cashouts under Treas. Reg. 1.409A-3(j)(4)(v)):
  - Participant, spouse, and domestic partner 409A pensions may be automatically cashed out in a lump sum if the actuarial present value is at or below the Plan’s Cashout Limit (historically $15,000 before December 1, 2012).
  - Special discretionary cashouts of 409A Vested Pensions may be made by the Plan Administrator on specified dates (e.g., December 1, 2012, and later designated months), with written lists documenting selections.
  - All 409A nonaccount balance benefits across applicable plans must be cashed out together if the limit is met; cashouts respect any required six-month delay; no participant or survivor election is permitted.
  - Cashouts are not available effective January 1, 2018, for participants eligible for certain “Kicker” benefits under a Severance Program (as defined in Appendix Article E).

- Reemployment: If a retiree receiving an annuity is rehired and re-eligible under the Salaried Plan, existing annuity payments continue unchanged; any new 409A accruals are paid after the subsequent separation.

- Forfeiture for misconduct: Post-2008 Accruals are forfeited (and recoverable if already paid) if the participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of separation.

- Article V—Amount of Retirement Pension (overview and formula):
  - When payable, the 409A Pension is determined under Sections 5.1 or 5.3, subject to adjustments (e.g., 4.6(b), 5.4) and the Plan freeze in Article I.
  - Section 5.1 formula: 409A Pension equals Total Pension minus the Salaried Plan Pension minus the Pre-409A Pension (not below zero), calculated with appropriate early/late commencement adjustments, relative value of forms, actuarial equivalence, and anti-duplication rules as administered by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE V
Amount of Retirement Pension
nodes.start_phrase:
When a 409A Pension becomes payable to or on behalf of a Participant under this Plan, the amount of
such 409A Pension shall be determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3 (whichever is applicable), subject to any
adjustments required under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4 and subject to the freeze of the Plan described in Article I.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article V sets how 409A retirement and pre-retirement survivor pensions are calculated under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) – 409A Program, including definitions, coordination with the Salaried Plan and Pre‑409A Program, the PEP Guarantee, adjustments, offsets, and exclusions. Article VI begins the rules for distribution timing and form.

- Core 409A Pension calculation (Section 5.1):
  - Participant’s 409A Pension = Total Pension − Salaried Plan Pension − Pre‑409A Pension (not below zero).
  - Determined with early/late commencement adjustments as of the Annuity Starting Date, relative value of elected forms of payment, actuarial equivalence, and rules to prevent duplication considering prior payments.
  - For Annuity Starting Dates after 12/31/2018, may “make up” harsher early retirement reductions applied to the Pre‑409A Pension compared to 2019 Salaried Plan Factors.
  - Total Pension = greater of (i) Part B Salaried Plan pension ignoring Code 401(a)(17)/415 limits and the post‑NRD actuarial increase under Part B §5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee; comparisons reflect relative value of forms.

- PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2):
  - Eligibility: 1988 pensionable earnings with an Employer ≥ $75,000 (as defined under the 1988 Salaried Plan; excludes earnings from non‑Employer entities at the time).
  - Benefit formulas:
    - Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service (CS) + 1% of HAME for CS >10 − 1⅔% of Primary Social Security Amount (PSSA) × CS (max 30). Vested Pension is prorated based on actual vs. projected CS to Normal Retirement Age (NRA).
    - Formula B (for classifications eligible before 7/1/1975): greater of (A) 1½% of HAME × CS − 50% of PSSA, or (B) 3% of HAME × CS up to 15 − 50% of PSSA. Disability pensions use CS and pay bases at disability per Salaried Plan.
  - Survivor benefit for Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner: 50% of Participant’s annuity with no reduction to the Participant; if survivor is >10 years younger, reduce 0.8% per year for years 11–20 younger and 0.4% per year thereafter.
  - Additional reductions/adjustments:
    - Early retirement: 0.25% (3/12 of 1%) per month before NRA.
    - Vested Pension commencing before NRA: actuarial equivalent; apply pre‑retirement spouse/domestic partner coverage reductions.
    - If elected form provides greater survivor benefit, or a non‑spouse survivor, or includes inflation protection, reduce to actuarial equivalence of the standard benchmark form.
  - Lump sum: actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, including survivor and early‑retirement adjustments; actuarial equivalence preserves pre‑1989 plan value and complies with Section 409A’s annuity equivalence rules.

- Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension (Section 5.3):
  - Amount = Total PR Spouse’s Pension − Salaried Plan PR Spouse’s Pension − PR Spouse’s Pension from Pre‑409A Program (not below zero).
  - Uses early/late commencement adjustments and actuarial equivalence; considers timing/form of any prior payments.
  - Total PR Spouse’s Pension = greater of the Salaried Plan amount ignoring Code limits and Part B §5.7(d), or the PEP Guarantee PR Spouse’s Pension; comparison done at Participant’s NRA and then adjusted for actual commencement.
  - PEP Guarantee PR Spouse’s Pension: equal to survivor benefit under a QJSA assuming separation and commencement aligned with survivor benefit start, and death the day after; special minimum for active/disabled Participants = 25% of PEP Guarantee, with CS and pay bases as of death; no early commencement reduction. Applies principles parallel to §5.1(b) and the actuarial‑equivalence sentence in §5.2(b)(2).

- Certain adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Rehired Participants: if Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated for added CS, recalculate PEP benefits to the extent permitted under Section 409A; adjust PEP Guarantee for in‑service/prior distributions consistent with Salaried Plan, considering this Plan and any “specified plans.”
  - Increases under other specified plans: if a court/administrator/other increases a related plan benefit after PEP is determined, recalculate PEP (subject to 409A) and recover any overpayment; avoid duplication with Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans.
  - No offsets that violate Section 409A: apply Salaried Plan non‑duplication/transfer rules to Total Pension only if they do not change 409A time/form; Company will seek compliant special arrangements under the other plan to avoid prohibited changes.

- Excludable employment (Section 5.5): Executives who sign agreements waiving eligibility or participation will not accrue or increase benefits for that employment; applies to agreements on/after 1/1/2009, whether signed before or after eligibility/participation.

- Pre‑409A Pension (Section 5.6): The grandfathered portion under Treas. Reg. §1.409A‑6(a)(3)(i),(iv); determined using principles akin to §5.1(b) and the actuarial‑equivalence standard in §5.2(b)(2).

- Offsets (Section 5.7):
  - Company may offset benefits by amounts the Participant owes the Company (incurred during employment), within 409A annual limits, and at the same time/amount as the debt would be due.
  - When a Prior 409A Benefit exists, compute any additional 409A Benefit net of an actuarially equivalent offset reflecting early/late commencement and form values; example: Post‑Disability Accruals offset by Pre‑Separation Accruals.

- Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 5.8):
  - Structure mirrors the spouse provisions: Amount = Total PR Domestic Partner’s Pension − Salaried Plan PR Domestic Partner’s Pension − Pre‑409A Program portion (not below zero); apply early/late and actuarial equivalence.
  - Total PR Domestic Partner’s Pension: greater of Salaried Plan amount ignoring Code limits and Part B §5.7(d), or PEP Guarantee PR Domestic Partner’s amount; compare at Participant’s NRA then adjust for commencement.
  - PEP Guarantee PR Domestic Partner’s Pension: QJSA‑based survivor model; special minimum for active/disabled = 25% of PEP Guarantee; no early commencement reduction; same actuarial‑equivalence principles apply.

- Distributions (Article VI introduction and §6.1 start):
  - Article VI governs distribution of 409A Pensions to Participants and any beneficiary continuation; Pre‑Retirement Spouse/Domestic Partner pensions are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules in §4.9); Pre‑409A Pension distributions follow Pre‑409A Program terms.
  - 409A Retirement Pension form/timing (§6.1):
    - Default: Single lump sum on the first day of the month on/after the Retirement Date, subject to key‑employee delay (§6.6).
    - Prior elections: If a compliant election was made by 12/31/2007 at least six months before and in a calendar year prior to the Annuity Starting Date, distributions follow that election.

nodes.title: Distribution of Benefits
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VI
Distribution of Benefits
nodes.start_phrase:
The terms of this Article govern (i) the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to a
409A Pension, and (ii) the continuation of benefits (if any) to such Participant’ s beneficiary following the Participant’ s
death.
nodes.summary:
- Article VI sets rules for distributing 409A Pension benefits to participants and for continuing benefits to beneficiaries after a participant’s death.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Domestic Partner’s Pensions from the 409A Program are paid as lifetime annuities to the eligible spouse or domestic partner, subject to Section 4.9 cashout provisions. Pre-409A Pensions are governed by the Pre-409A Program.
- Section 6.1 (Form and Timing):
  - Default rule: A participant’s 409A Retirement Pension is paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following the retirement date, subject to delay rules for Key Employees (Section 6.6).
  - Prior payment elections: If a participant made a valid election by December 31, 2007, and at least six months before and in a calendar year prior to the annuity starting date, payment will follow that election (options referenced but text is truncated).

nodes.title: Form and Timing of Distributions
nodes.heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions :
nodes.start_phrase: Benefits under the 409A Program shall be distributed as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Article VI governs distribution of benefits under the 409A Program when a participant becomes entitled to a pension and outlines continuation of benefits to beneficiaries after a participant’s death. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s pensions are paid as lifetime annuities (subject to cashout rules). Pre‑409A benefits are governed by the Pre‑409A Program.
- 409A Retirement Pension (Form and Timing):
  - Default: Single lump sum payable on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Retirement Date, subject to a delay for Key Employees (Section 6.6).
  - Prior payment elections: If made by December 31, 2007 and at least six months earlier in a prior calendar year than the Annuity Starting Date, the election controls. Elections could (i) choose an annuity form, (ii) change commencement timing, or both. Elections by participants eligible only for a Vested Pension at separation are disregarded.
  - Default annuity forms when an annuity is elected: Qualified Joint & Survivor Annuity (QJSA) if married; Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless an optional form is elected under Section 6.2 following procedures in Section 6.3(a). Marital status is determined on the Annuity Starting Date.
  - If commencement is delayed by election, the benefit is increased for interest at the plan’s actuarial lump-sum rate through the payment processing date; interest is paid at the participant’s elected time.
- 409A Vested Pension (Form and Timing), subject to cashouts (Section 4.9), key employee delay (Section 6.6), and Disability rules (6.1(c)):
  - Separation before age 55 with at least 5 years of Service: Annuity commences on/after age 55 (first day of the coincident/next month). Default form is QJSA if married; Single Life if unmarried. An unmarried participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% or 75% Survivor Annuity for the partner (per Section 6.2). Marital/partner status determined at the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Separation at ages 55–64 with at least 5 but less than 10 years of Service: Annuity commences the first of the month following Separation from Service, with forms as above and optional forms available under Section 6.2 via Section 6.3(a) procedures.
- 409A Disability Pension:
  - Pre‑Separation Accruals: Paid the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; forms available are those for Vested or Retirement Pensions under Section 6.2 (varying by marital/domestic partner status).
  - Post‑LTD Accruals: Paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Available Forms of Payment (Section 6.2):
  - Applies to participants entitled to a Retirement Pension under 6.1(a)(2) or a Vested Pension under 6.1(b).
  - Retirement Pension: Participant may choose among optional forms by valid election under Section 6.3(a).
  - Vested Pension:
    - If married on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect only certain specified optional forms (referenced as paragraphs (1), (2)(ii), (2)(iii)) with the Eligible Spouse as beneficiary.
    - If unmarried with an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect designated survivor annuity options for the partner (text continues beyond the excerpt).
- Cross-references and conditions: Cashout distributions (Section 4.9), election procedures (Section 6.3(a)), key employee payment delay (Section 6.6), and definitions including Pre‑Separation Accruals and Post‑LTD Accruals (Section 4.5).

nodes.title: Available Forms of Payment
nodes.heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment :
nodes.start_phrase:
This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension
under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) above or a V ested Pension under subsection 6.1(b) above.
nodes.summary:
- Defines Disability Pension payment timing under the 409A Program:
  - Pre-Separation Accruals are paid on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service, using the same payment forms available for Vested or Retirement Pensions (including marital/domestic partner distinctions).
  - Post-Long-Term-Disability (Post-LTD) Accruals are paid in a lump sum on the first day of the month after the Participant turns 65.
- Sets out available annuity forms for Participants entitled to a Retirement Pension or a Vested Pension:
  - Retirement Pension: may elect from the full menu of options via proper election.
  - Vested Pension:
    - If married on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect Single Life Annuity, 75% Survivor, or 50% Survivor with Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; no other forms permitted.
    - If not married but has an Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date: may elect 75% Survivor or 50% Survivor with Eligible Domestic Partner as beneficiary; no other forms permitted.
    - If not married and no Eligible Domestic Partner: must receive a Single Life Annuity.
  - Optional annuity forms (each actuarially equivalent to a Single Life Annuity):
    - Single Life Annuity.
    - Survivor Options: 100%, 75%, or 50% (50% is a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if beneficiary is an Eligible Spouse).
    - Ten Years Certain and Life.
- Provides optional inflation protection for annuity payments:
  - 5% or 7% protection: initial reduction to monthly benefit, with increases each year to the extent prior-year inflation exceeds the chosen threshold.
  - Adjustments apply each January 1, starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date, based on inflation for the 12 months ending September 30, measured like Social Security COLAs.
  - Chosen inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits and is irrevocable.
- Establishes procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.2), including special rules when there are multiple Annuity Starting Dates; defines the date an election is “received” as the postmark date or the actual receipt date by the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Procedures for Elections
nodes.heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections :
nodes.start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections ( i.e., elections under Section 6.2).
nodes.summary:
- Describes two optional inflation-protection features for monthly annuity benefits:
  - 5% Inflation Protection: benefit is initially reduced; thereafter increased each January 1 by the excess of prior-year inflation over 5%.
  - 7% Inflation Protection: same mechanics, with a 7% threshold.
- Inflation adjustments begin on the second January 1 following the Participant’s Annuity Starting Date, based on inflation for the 12 months ending September 30, measured using the Social Security cost-of-living adjustment methodology in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
- Elected inflation protection is irrevocable and carries over to increase any survivor benefit.

- Sets procedures for Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.3):
  - An election is deemed received if postmarked that day or actually received by close of business that day; spousal consent is not required.
  - Election of an optional annuity form (for a 409A Retirement Pension with a proper prior election or a 409A Vested Terminated Pension) must be in writing, signed, received at least one day before the Annuity Starting Date, specify an available optional form, and designate a beneficiary if applicable. Electronic elections/affirmations may be permitted.
  - For Participants with multiple Annuity Starting Dates (e.g., after rehire): initial elections continue to govern prior accruals; new elections at the subsequent Annuity Starting Date apply only to benefits accrued after rehire.
  - Marital status determination (effective Jan 1, 2014): default assumption is unmarried unless the Participant provides satisfactory notice before the Annuity Starting Date; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.

- Introduces special rules for survivor options (Section 6.4), including effects of certain deaths when an optional annuity with a survivor benefit has been elected (details partially shown).

nodes.title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
nodes.heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options :
nodes.start_phrase: The following special rules shall apply for the survivor options available under Section 6.2.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses how elections at a subsequent Annuity Starting Date (after a rehire and subsequent Separation from Service) apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; prior unpaid accruals continue under the initial Annuity Starting Date elections.
- Establishes marital status determination rules (effective January 1, 2014): the Plan assumes a Participant is unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless the Participant provides satisfactory notice of marriage before that date; notice is given with the payment election or via Plan Administrator procedures; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Sets special survivor option rules:
  - If a Participant or designated beneficiary dies before the Annuity Starting Date, any prior survivor annuity election is disregarded.
  - If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date but before payments actually commence, the survivor election stands; survivor payments to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month after death; any owed back payments go to the Participant’s estate.
  - For the 120-payment certain option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): if the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate; if a beneficiary receiving payments dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Imposes age-difference limits when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner:
  - 100% survivor option unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant.
  - 75% survivor option unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger than the Participant.
- Introduces the next section on designation of beneficiary for forms of payment that include a survivor benefit.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.heading: 6.5 Designation of Beneficiary :
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant who has elected under Section 6.2 to receive all or part of his Retirement Pension in a form of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Treatment of benefit elections upon death relative to the Annuity Starting Date: elections under certain options are disregarded if death occurs before the Annuity Starting Date; if death occurs after the Annuity Starting Date but before 409A Retirement Pension payments begin, the elected survivor form is honored, benefits start the first day of the month following death, and any back payments due go to the participant’s estate.
- Rules for the 120-payments-certain option (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): if the participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary before 120 payments are made, the remaining payments go to the participant’s estate; if a beneficiary was receiving payments and dies before completion, the remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Restrictions when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner: the 100% survivor option is not permitted if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger; the 75% survivor option is not permitted if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger.
- Beneficiary designation rules for survivor options: beneficiaries must be designated on approved forms; for the 120-payments-certain option, both primary and contingent beneficiaries may be named; designations can be changed or revoked before the Annuity Starting Date and are effective only when filed with the Plan Administrator; if no beneficiary is properly designated for a survivor option, the default is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner; participants entitled only to a Vested Pension generally cannot name a beneficiary unless an optional form is elected, in which case the spouse/domestic partner is the beneficiary on the Annuity Starting Date.
- Required delay for Key Employees under Section 409A: for Key Employees, 409A Retirement Pension distributions begin on the earliest first day of a month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon death.

nodes.title: Required Delay for Key Employees
nodes.heading: 6.6 Required Delay for Key Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 6.1 above, if a Participant is classified as a Key Employee upon his Separation from Service (or at such other time for determining Key Employee status as may apply under Section 409A), then distributions to the Participant shall commence as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Beneficiary designations: Participants selecting an optional form of payment must designate a beneficiary on the election form (or approved Salaried Plan form). For the survivor option in Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv), both a primary and contingent beneficiary may be named. Participants can change or revoke designations any time before the Annuity Starting Date, subject to Plan Administrator rules, and designations are effective only when filed with the Plan Administrator.
- Default beneficiary rules: If no beneficiary is properly designated and a survivor option under Section 6.2(a)(2) is elected, the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner is the beneficiary. Participants entitled only to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if they may elect an optional form under Section 6.2, the beneficiary on the Annuity Starting Date is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
- Required delay for Key Employees (Section 6.6, Section 409A compliance): 
  - 409A Retirement Pension: Payments begin on the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon death. For periods before 2009, no delay applies if payments begin simultaneously with the Salaried Plan under Section 6.1(b)(3)(i).
  - 409A Vested Pension: Payments begin per Section 6.1(b) or, if later, on the earliest first of the month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon death. The same pre-2009 exception applies.
  - Interest on delayed payments: Any delayed amounts are increased by interest at the plan’s Actuarial Equivalent lump-sum rate through the check preparation date and paid as a lump sum when distributions commence. If the participant dies, the beneficiary or estate receives any delayed amounts with interest as provided by the plan.

nodes.title: Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes
nodes.heading: 6.7 Payment of FICA and Related Income T axes :
nodes.start_phrase: As provided in subsections (a) through (c) below , a portion of a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) in satisfaction of the Participant’ s FICA Amount and the related withholding of income tax at source on wages (imposed under Code Section 3401 or the corresponding withholding provisions of the applicable state, local or foreign tax laws as a result of the payment of the FICA Amount) and the additional withholding of income tax at source on wages that is attributable to the pyramiding of wages and taxes.
nodes.summary:
- Describes how a portion of a participant’s 409A Pension will be paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to tax authorities to cover the participant’s FICA tax, required income tax withholding tied to that FICA payment, and additional withholding due to wage/tax pyramiding.
- Specifies timing: on the date FICA and related withholdings are due for deposit, the lump sum equal to those amounts is paid from the participant’s 409A Pension and remitted to the IRS (or applicable authority). Key Employee status does not affect this lump-sum payment timing.
- Explains pension reduction: the participant’s 409A Pension is reduced, effective as of the lump-sum payment date, by the Actuarial Equivalent of the amount used to satisfy FICA and related tax withholding. This reduction may occur even after pension payments have begun.
- Clarifies no impact on pension commencement: the lump-sum tax payment does not alter the commencement timing of the participant’s actuarially reduced 409A Pension, including any required delay for Key Employees.
- Outlines plan administration: the Plan Administrator has authority to interpret the plan, issue regulations, maintain records, and calculate benefits; may rely on participant-provided information (address, age, marital status); and its determinations are final and binding.
- States that neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary of the plan, and ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply under this plan.
- Provides facility of payment rules: if a payee is under legal disability or otherwise unable to manage finances, the Plan Administrator may direct payments to the person, their legal representative, or apply payments for their benefit, fully discharging liability.
- Notes claims procedure authority: the Plan Administrator (or its designee) has exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the plan (section text continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VII
Administration
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
nodes.summary:
- Administration and authority:
  - The Plan Administrator has sole, absolute discretion to interpret the plan, issue regulations, keep records, and calculate benefits; its decisions are final and binding.
  - The Administrator may rely on participant-provided information (address, age, marital status).
  - Neither the Company nor the Administrator is a fiduciary; ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply.

- Facility of payment:
  - If a payee is incapacitated, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit; such payments fully discharge liability.

- Claims and appeals process:
  - The Administrator has exclusive authority over eligibility and benefit determinations; court review is under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard and limited to the administrative record.
  - Denial notices within 90 days (extendable to 180) must state reasons, cite plan provisions, list needed additional information, and describe review rights (including ERISA civil action).
  - Claimants have 60 days to seek review; decisions on review within 60 days (extendable to 120) with access to relevant documents at no charge.
  - Specific references to discretion do not limit the Administrator’s broader discretion.

- Mandatory exhaustion of remedies:
  - Claimants must fully exhaust plan claims procedures before filing in court; this requirement is intended to apply as broadly as possible.
  - Post-exhaustion litigation is limited to the administrative record.
  - The Administrator may establish special procedures (e.g., class claims) to facilitate exhaustion.
  - Definitions provided for Dispute, Claim (including interpretation, validity, administration, ERISA violations, benefit recovery, fiduciary breach, and related matters), and Claimant.
  - Examples clarify when exhaustion is not excused (e.g., inadequate claim submission or document requests).

- Limitations period and venue:
  - Two-year statute of limitations for claims, ERISA interference, and other actions, with accrual defined by earliest of specified events (e.g., receipt of calculation, identified payment date, knowledge of facts, first payment/denial).
  - Appeals correspondence does not toll the limitations period.
  - Exclusive venue: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for claims filed on/after January 1, 2011.

- Miscellaneous:
  - No guarantee of employment; employers retain at-will termination rights.
  - Anti-alienation: benefits may not be assigned, pledged, garnished, or transferred (including in divorce/child support contexts); attempts are void and not binding on the Company.
  - Unfunded status: obligations are payable from the Company’s general assets; participants are unsecured general creditors.
  - Company action under the plan may be taken by the Board of Directors or the Compensation Committee (section truncated).

nodes.title: Miscellaneous
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE VIII
Miscellaneous
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing contained in this Plan shall be construed as a contract of employment between an Employer and any Employee, or as a right of any Employee to be continued in the employment of an Employer , or as a limitation of the right of an Employer to discharge any of its Employees, with or without cause.
nodes.summary:
- Employment not guaranteed: The Plan does not create a contract of employment or restrict an employer’s right to terminate employment with or without cause.
- Anti‑alienation of benefits: Plan benefits cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, garnished, or otherwise encumbered, including in divorce or child-support matters; the Company is not liable for beneficiaries’ debts.
- Unfunded status: Obligations are paid from the Company’s general assets; participants are unsecured general creditors.
- Corporate authority: Plan actions may be taken by the Board, its Compensation Committee, or duly authorized designees, with reporting to the Board.
- Indemnification: Employees administering the Plan in good faith are indemnified to the fullest extent permitted by law unless the Board decides otherwise.
- Section 409A compliance: The Plan is intended to comply with 409A; good‑faith actions to comply do not create liability. Explicit anti‑duplication rules ensure no double counting of benefit elements (e.g., earnings or service), with specific provisions controlling over general ones and integration rules with the Salaried Plan.
- Section 457A measures for expatriates: For Covered Transfers to certain non‑U.S. entities, participants vest immediately before transfer (unless the Company issues a contrary communication); post‑transfer benefit enhancements tied to service or age are credited only at plan year‑end and only if permissible; no right to enhancements that would be taxable under 457A; these rules cease upon return to qualifying U.S. entities or as specified by Company communication.
- Authorized transfers outside PepsiCo: If a participant moves to a non‑PepsiCo entity, liability for accrued benefits remains with the Company unless otherwise agreed.
- Electronic signatures: Electronic signatures and records are fully valid and enforceable to the extent permitted by law.
- Amendment and termination (Article IX overview): The Company retains broad rights, subject to 409A, to amend (including retroactively) or terminate the Plan at any time; continuation is not guaranteed. Amendments/termination cannot reduce the benefit amount already earned under Article IV as of the action date unless an equal amount is provided under another plan or as necessary to comply with 409A; specific payment forms are not protected. Only the Company may amend. The termination provision begins to outline options to terminate the Plan as to the Company or specific employers/groups.

nodes.title: Amendment and Termination
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE IX
Amendment and T ermination
nodes.start_phrase: This Article governs the Company’ s right to amend and or terminate the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Article IX outlines the Company’s authority to amend or terminate the Plan, subject at all times to Internal Revenue Code Section 409A. The Company’s powers are as broad as allowed by law.
- Continuation: Although intended to continue indefinitely, the Plan may be amended, terminated, or partially terminated at the Company’s discretion. Amendments or terminations cannot reduce a participant’s accrued benefit under Article IV as of the action date unless an equal benefit is provided under another plan or as necessary to comply with Section 409A. Specific payment forms are not protected.
- Amendments: The Company alone may amend the Plan, including retroactively, to ensure continued 409A compliance. Other Employers have no amendment rights.
- Termination: The Company may terminate the Plan in whole or for specific Employers, for a group experiencing a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), or as otherwise permitted by Section 409A. If not all Employers are terminated, the Plan continues for remaining Employers. Distributions upon termination must follow 409A restrictions.
- Change in Control: The Company retains maximum discretionary authority permitted by 409A to terminate and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (as defined in 409A). These are the exclusive terms for any Change in Control distribution of 409A Program-derived benefits.
- Article X (ERISA Plan Structure): Together with the Pre-409A Program documents, the Plan consists of three separate ERISA plans (effective July 1, 1996):
  - Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): Provides benefits above Internal Revenue Code §415 limits for Salaried Plan participants.
  - Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits above Code §401(a)(17) limits (after accounting for the Excess Benefit Plan); for ERISA reporting, referred to as PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
  - Preservation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees that preserves certain benefits for Salaried Plan participants (description truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: ERISA Plan Structure
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE X
ERISA Plan Structure
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan document in conjunction with the plan document(s) for the Pre-409A Program encompasses three separate plans within the meaning of ERISA, as are set forth in subsections (a), (b) and (c).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes the ERISA plan structure for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program), which, together with Pre-409A plan documents, comprises three separate ERISA plans effective July 1, 1996 (with plans (b) and (c) previously a single plan).
- Defines three components:
  - Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): provides benefits exceeding Internal Revenue Code §415 limits for Salaried Plan participants.
  - Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees, providing benefits above the §401(a)(17) compensation cap under the Salaried Plan (after the Excess Benefit Plan); ERISA reporting name: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
  - Preservation Top Hat Plan: a “top hat” plan preserving pre-1989 accrual levels for certain participants described in §5.2(a), after taking into account the other two plans; ERISA reporting name: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan II.
- Specifies benefit allocation order: first to the Excess Benefit Plan; then to the Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan; then to the Preservation Top Hat Plan. Confirms the three plans are severable for all purposes.
- Clarifies that lump-sum termination benefits paid in connection with Special Early Retirement under a temporary company severance program are treated as part of an unfunded severance (welfare) plan under ERISA §3(1), exist only for the program’s duration and purpose, and are not subject to top hat reporting or pension-plan ERISA requirements.
- Sets governing law: ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; New York law applies where not preempted by ERISA.
- Includes a severability clause: invalidity of any provision does not affect the remainder of the Plan.

nodes.title: Applicable Law
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE XI
Applicable Law
nodes.start_phrase: The provisions of this Plan shall be construed and administered according to, and its validity and enforceability shall be governed by , enforced in accordance with, and determined under (1) ERISA and any other applicable federal law as would be applied in cases that arise in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New Y ork, and (2) to the extent ERISA does not preempt state law , the internal laws of the state of New York.
nodes.summary:
- Governing law: The plan is to be construed, administered, and enforced under ERISA and applicable federal law as applied in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York; where ERISA does not preempt, New York state internal law applies.
- Severability: If any provision is found void, invalid, or unlawful, the remainder of the plan remains in effect.
- Adoption and effective date: The amended and restated PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program is adopted on December 20, 2021, effective January 1, 2022 (or as otherwise stated).
- Execution: Signed by Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer; approvals by Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel (Law Department), and Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel (Tax Department).

nodes.title: Signature
nodes.heading:
ARTICLE XII
Signature
nodes.start_phrase: The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan, 409A Program, as amended and restated, is hereby adopted as of this 20th day of December , 2021, to be ef fective as of January 1, 2022 or as otherwise stated herein.
nodes.summary: Execution and approval page (Article XII – Signature) of the amended and restated PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, confirming adoption on December 20, 2021 with an effective date of January 1, 2022 (unless otherwise stated). It includes the executing officer’s signature (Ronald Schellekens, Executive Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer) and approvals from Legal (Jeffrey Arnold, Legal Director, Employee Benefits Counsel) and Tax (Christine Griff, Vice President, Tax Counsel), along with the plan title and page reference.

nodes.title: APPENDIX
nodes.heading: APPENDIX
nodes.start_phrase: The following Appendix articles modify particular terms of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program that modifies specific plan terms and governs in case of conflict with the main plan; otherwise, the main plan provisions apply to participants, beneficiaries, and related claimants.
- Appendix Article A: Transition Provisions covering rules effective at some point between January 1, 2005 and December 31, 2008, with each provision specifying its own effective period.
- Transition rules affecting Article II (Definitions):
  - Actuarial Equivalent: During the Transition Period, for pensions paid as a Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity, other survivor annuity options, annuities with inflation protection, or as a Single Life Annuity, the Plan Administrator used actuarial factors from the Salaried Plan.
  - Key Employee: Additional operating rules applied by time period; for the 2005 plan year, to avoid missing anyone, all participants (and former participants) classified or grandfathered as Band IV and above at any time in 2005 were treated as Key Employees for Separation from Service distributions.

nodes.title: Transition Provisions
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE A - 
Transition Provisions
nodes.start_phrase: This Article A provides the transition rules for the Plan that were ef fective at some time during the period beginning January 1, 2005 and ending December 31, 2008 (the “T ransition Period”).
nodes.summary:
- Scope and timing: Establishes transition rules for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program effective during January 1, 2005–December 31, 2008, specifying when each provision applied.

- Definitions adjustments (Article II):
  - Actuarial Equivalent: During the transition, annuity conversions for certain forms (QJSA, survivor annuities with inflation protection, Single Life Annuity) used Salaried Plan actuarial factors.
  - Key Employee identification: Special interim rules for 2005–2007, broadly treating Band IV+ (and grandfathered equivalents) as Key Employees and setting compensation-based lookbacks (under Code §415(c)(3)) by calendar quarter to determine Key status.

- Distributions (Article VI): 409A Pensions that otherwise would have been paid during the transition were instead paid on March 1, 2009.

- Administration (Article VII): Replaced Section 8.6(a) to mandate compliance with Code §409A and preservation of grandfathered (Pre-409A) deferrals; voids actions/provisions that would violate §409A or harm grandfathering; deems required §409A provisions included.

- Severance benefits transition rules:
  - Defines Special Early Retirement (age 50–<55 with 10 years of Elapsed Time Service; for 2008 severance, age/service rounded up).
  - 2005 severance: Sets payment timing/form for non-retirement-eligible (paid as Vested Pension; coordination with Salaried Plan timing; special 2007 payment timing for some) and for retirement-eligible or Special Early Retirement participants (generally lump sum first of month after separation).
  - 2007 severance: Distinguishes non-retirement-eligible (Vested Pension forms), retirement-eligible (lump sum unless valid prior payment election), those becoming retirement-eligible during paid leave, Special Early Retirement eligible or becoming eligible during leave; specifies “PEP Kicker” lump sum timing and interaction with prior payment elections.
  - 2008 severance: Parallel structure to 2007 with timing/forms, inclusion of Special Early Retirement rules (with rounding), and PEP Kicker handling.
  - Key Employee delay: If a payment is due on account of Separation from Service and the participant is a Key Employee, applies the payment delay under Section 6.6.
  - Compliance: Confirms company elections and payments complied with Notice 2005-1 and Code §409A (including 19(c)) and were scheduled in the termination year as specified.

- Special participant rules:
  - For 2005 Band VI limited-duration assignments (<5 years): Deems 5 years of PEP Credited Service and vesting.
  - For a participant with a 11/1/2007 Salaried Plan lump-sum Annuity Starting Date (selected 10/9/2007): Non-409A portion of Plan benefit paid as a lump sum six months after that date.
  - For a participant who fixed a 2/1/2005 payment date (selected 9/3/2004): Confirms that as the commencement date and includes service during post-payment consulting in benefit calculation.

- 409A Disability Pension (Pre-Separation Accruals):
  - Distributions start March 1, 2009, using Vested Pension forms (married/unmarried differences apply).
  - Additional death benefit: If death occurs before expected mortality date, beneficiary receives a lump sum actuarial equivalent of remaining expected payments; sets beneficiary designation hierarchy.

- Appendix B (Severance window earnings/service computation):
  - Defines Severance Program and Eligible Bonus.
  - Allows salary continuation and Eligible Bonus earned in the first 12 months of a qualifying severance leave to be included in Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if paid later, with references to recognizing Service and Credited Service under Sections B.3 and B.4.

nodes.title: Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance Windows
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE B - 
Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance W indows
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases, in boldface and underlined, appear in this Appendix B with initial capitals they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary:
