- The excerpt is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program and covers Appendix Article B (Computation of Earnings and Service During Certain Severance Windows) and the start of Appendix Article C (International and PIRP Transfer Participants).

- Article B defines key terms:
  - Severance Program: A severance benefit program that the Plan Administrator deems eligible for recognizing Service and Credited Service under this appendix.
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive under the Severance Program that can be included in Highest Average Monthly Earnings.

- Article B outlines how severance-related pay and time can be credited:
  - Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus (B.2): Salary continuation and Eligible Bonus for the first 12 months of a severance leave can be counted toward Highest Average Monthly Earnings, even if paid after Separation from Service; projected amounts may be used if pension benefits commence before all payments are made.
  - Inclusion of Credited Service (B.3): The first 12 months of severance can count as Credited Service for calculating the Participant’s Pension and pre-retirement spouse/eligible domestic partner benefits, even if this period is after Separation from Service.
  - Inclusion of Service (B.4): Similarly, the first 12 months of severance can count as Service for these benefits, even if after Separation from Service.
  - Reduction to Reflect Early Payment (B.5): If pension calculations include projected service or earnings before they are actually performed or paid, the benefit is actuarially adjusted using the Salaried Plan’s early payment rate to account for the early inclusion.

- Article C introduces special calculation rules for certain transfers:
  - Scope (C.1): Establishes special benefit rules for International Transfer Participants and PIRP Transfer Participants; benefits are paid under normal plan terms and are subject to Code section 409A (including amounts accrued before 1/1/2005). Effective dates: International Transfer rules effective 4/1/2007; PIRP Transfer rules effective 1/1/2016 (with possible pre-2016 service recognition).
  - International Transfer Participants (C.2): Begins defining who qualifies, referencing transfers to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary” and specific employee status criteria under the Salaried Plan; full definition continues beyond the excerpt.

nodes.title: International and PIRP Transfer Participants
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE C
International and PIRP T ransfer Participants
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of an individual who is either an “International Transfer Participant” under Section C.2 below or a “PIRP T ransfer Participant” under Section C.4 below .
nodes.summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes special rules for calculating benefits for “International Transfer Participants” (ITPs) and “PIRP Transfer Participants,” specifying that ITP benefits are determined under Section C.3 (subject to C.6) and PIRP benefits under Section C.5. All benefits are paid under the Plan’s normal terms and are subject to Code section 409A (including amounts accrued before January 1, 2005). Effective dates: ITP provisions effective April 1, 2007; PIRP provisions effective January 1, 2016 (may consider pre‑2016 years).

- Definition of International Transfer Participant (C.2):
  - General rule: An individual who, after transfer to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary,” would meet the Salaried Plan’s Employee definition at Section 2.1 Part B, paragraph (2)(vi) (U.S. citizen or resident alien on a qualifying temporary international assignment) but for being in a Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher role.
  - Special rule for certain permanent assignments to Mexico: Also includes individuals transferred to an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary in Mexico who (1) are in Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher, (2) have Mexico as home country per Expat Centre for Excellence records, and (3) are on assignments not limited to 5 years or less.
  - Grandfathering: Individuals transferred before April 1, 2007 can qualify if they met the above conditions at the time of transfer.

- Benefit formula for ITPs (C.3):
  - Methodology: Generally mirrors Section 5.1 of the Plan.
  - Total Pension (per Section 5.1(c)(1)): Calculated as if the participant continued to accrue Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan while working for the foreign subsidiary after U.S.-based employment ended, disregarding the actual cessation date of such accruals. For transfers before 1992, service and earnings with the foreign subsidiary prior to 1992 are excluded.
  - Final Plan benefit: Total Pension (as a lump sum at benefit commencement) reduced by (1) the actual Salaried Plan benefit (as a lump sum at benefit commencement) and (2) any amounts paid from a “qualifying plan” (as defined in Section 3.5(c)(4) of Part B of the Salaried Plan) related to the foreign assignment (also expressed as a lump sum at benefit commencement).

- PIRP Transfer Participants (C.4 heading introduced): Indicates forthcoming definitions related to PIRP Transfer Participants; detailed content not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Definitions Related to PIRP Transfer Participants
nodes.heading: C.4 Definitions Related to PIRP T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: The following definitions apply for purposes of Sections C.1, C.4 and C.5 of this Article.
nodes.summary:
- Coverage of International Transfer Participants: For employees who transferred from a U.S.-based Employer to an “April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary,” Total Pension is calculated as if they continued to earn Credited Service and Earnings under the Salaried Plan during the foreign assignment. For transfers that occurred before 1992, service and earnings with the foreign subsidiary prior to 1992 are excluded.
- Offset-based benefit calculation for International Transfers: The Plan benefit equals the participant’s Total Pension (as a lump sum at benefit commencement) reduced by (1) the actual Salaried Plan benefit (lump sum at commencement) and (2) any amounts received from a qualifying plan related to the foreign assignment (also valued as a lump sum at commencement), preventing duplication.
- PIRP Transfer Participants definitions (Section C.4): Establishes key terms, including Accrued Benefit (single-life annuity at age 65), PIRP-DB (defined benefit portion of the PepsiCo International Retirement Program), PIRP-DB Employer, PIRP-DB Pensionable Service, PIRP-DB Salary, PIRP-DB Vice President, U.S. Person, and Year of Transfer.
- Incoming and Outgoing PIRP Transfer Participants: Defines who qualifies when moving between PIRP-DB-eligible positions and Salaried Plan-eligible positions within a year, where PIRP-DB accruals are blocked by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB; requires that the individual would otherwise receive a PIRP-DB benefit enhancement for the Year of Transfer and that PIRP-DB benefits were not paid out by December 1, 2016 (with limited VP discretion to treat certain payouts as unpaid).
- PIRP Transfer Participants’ benefit methodology (Section C.5): Generally follows Section 5.1 of the Plan, with special rules for “Total Pension.”
- Total Pension for PIRP Transfers: Calculated as if the participant were eligible under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer, recognizing actual Salaried Plan Credited Service and Earnings plus additional compensation and service that would have been PIRP-DB Salary and PIRP-DB Pensionable Service absent PIRP-DB Section 9.14.
- Additional PIRP-DB Salary/Service adjustments: If, in a year the participant is accruing under this Plan, PIRP-DB Salary is blocked by Section 9.14 and tied to PIRP-DB Pensionable Service not recognized here, the formula provides for an increase to account for that unrecognized salary/service (text truncates before completing the provision).
- Overall intent: Coordinate and equalize pension benefits for employees transferring between U.S. and international plans, ensure recognition of service and compensation despite accrual blocks, and avoid benefit duplication through specified offsets.

nodes.title: Benefit Formula for PIRP Transfer Participants
nodes.heading: C.5 Benefit Formula for PIRP T ransfer Participants :
nodes.start_phrase: Except as provided in this Section C.5, a PIRP T ransfer Participant’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined using a calculation methodology that is substantially similar to that which applies under Section 5.1 of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Year of Transfer” as the year in which a transfer described in subsection (f) occurs.
- Outlines the benefit formula for PIRP Transfer Participants, generally aligning with Plan Section 5.1 but with special rules for calculating “Total Pension.”
- Total Pension calculation:
  - Computed as if the participant were an eligible employee under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer, using actual Salaried Plan credited service/earnings plus any PIRP-DB salary and pensionable service that would have been recognized absent PIRP-DB Section 9.14.
  - If PIRP-DB salary/service during a year cannot be recognized due to Section 9.14 and relates to service not recognized under this Plan, the blocked increase in the PIRP accrued benefit is added to the participant’s accrued benefit under this Plan; for separations on/after January 1, 2017, this yields an appropriate, company‑determined increase to Total Pension.
  - Prevents double counting: no compensation or service is counted more than once, and benefits are coordinated to avoid duplication with PIRP-DB (as limited by Section 9.14) or other company plans, while preserving Code Section 409A compliance.
- Benefit payable under this Plan is determined by applying normal Article V reductions to the Total Pension.
- For separations on/after January 1, 2017, if early retirement eligibility under PIRP-DB (but for Section 9.14) would have increased the PIRP-DB benefit, an appropriate, company‑determined increase is added to this Plan’s benefit, net of any expected early retirement increase under this Plan, again avoiding duplication and maintaining 409A compliance.
- Permits alternative arrangements: the Company and an International Transfer Participant may agree in writing to disregard this Article in favor of another mutually agreed, Code Section 409A‑compliant benefit arrangement.

nodes.title: Alternative Arrangements Permitted
nodes.heading: C.6 Alternative Arrangements Permitted :
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Article or the Plan to the contrary , the Company and a Participant who would qualify as an International T ransfer Participant under Section C.2 above may agree in writing to disregard the provisions of this Article in favor of another mutually agreed upon benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A, in which case this Article shall not apply .
nodes.summary:
- Adjustment of benefits for PIRP Transfer Participants: If a projected increase in the PIRP-DB benefit at retirement is blocked by PIRP-DB Section 9.14, the Company may grant a discretionary, “appropriate increase” to the Participant’s benefit under this Plan, payable at the time and in the form provided by this Plan.
- Netting and anti-duplication rules: The increase will be reduced for any expected boost from Early Retirement eligibility under this Plan and structured to avoid duplicating benefits available under PIRP-DB (after Section 9.14 is applied) or any other Company/affiliate plan, without using any offset that would violate Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.
- Alternative arrangements: For Participants who would qualify as International Transfer Participants, the Company and the Participant may agree in writing to disregard the applicable Article and adopt another mutually agreed benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A; in such cases, the Article does not apply.
- Appendix Article D (Band 4 or higher rehired Yum participants): Effective May 1, 2009, special rules apply to certain rehired employees in Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher whose transfers would otherwise be Eligible Transfers under the Salaried Plan. For purposes of calculating Total Pension under Section 5.1(c)(1) (but not Salaried Plan Pension under Section 5.1(c)(2)), their reemployment position is deemed below Band 4 so the transfer qualifies as an Eligible Transfer and the Participant receives imputed service under TRI.4(b) and (c).
- Administration and compliance: Benefits under Article D remain subject to the Plan’s usual conditions and payment terms, and all such benefits are subject to Code Section 409A.

nodes.title: Band 4 or Higher Rehired Yum Participants
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE D Band 4 or Higher Rehired Y um Participants
nodes.start_phrase: Effective May 1, 2009, this Article provides special rules for calculating the benefit of a transferred Participant whose transfer would be an Eligible T ransfer under Section TRI.2(e) of the Part B of the Salaried Plan but for the fact that such individual is reemployed by the Company on or after May 1, 2009, into a position that is classified as Band 4 (or its equivalent) or higher .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article D outlines special rules for rehired Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher “Yum” participants reemployed on or after May 1, 2009. For Total Pension calculations (Section 5.1(c)(1))—but not for Salaried Plan Pension (Section 5.1(c)(2))—their reemployment position is deemed below Band 4 so the transfer qualifies as an Eligible Transfer under Section TRI.2(e) and they can receive imputed service under Sections TRI.4(b) and (c). All other standard plan conditions apply, and benefits are subject to IRC Section 409A.
- Appendix Article E sets the time and form of payment rules for benefits paid during severance windows to “Covered Participants,” effective for terminations on or after January 1, 2009 (or January 1, 2012 for participants covered by Appendix Article PBG). It defines “Applicable Summary Plan Description” and “Covered Participant” (those terminated and eligible for Special Early Retirement under a Severance Program or an Individual Severance Agreement) and clarifies that severance-related additional benefits are not permanent plan features.

nodes.title: Time and Form of Payment for Benefits Paid During Severance Windows
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE E - Time and Form of Payment for Benefits Paid During Severance W indows
nodes.start_phrase: This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes timing and form of payment rules for benefits paid during severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Applies to “Covered Participants” whose employment terminates and who qualify for Special Early Retirement either under a Severance Program (as detailed in the Applicable Summary Plan Description) or via an Individual Severance Agreement.
- Effective for terminations on or after January 1, 2009, with a separate effective date of January 1, 2012 for Participants covered by Appendix Article PBG.
- States that any additional severance-related benefits provided are not permanent features of the Plan.
- Provides definitions for key terms, including “Applicable Summary Plan Description” and “Covered Participant,” and defers to the main Plan for other capitalized terms unless context dictates otherwise.

nodes.title: Scope
nodes.heading: E.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase: This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article E governs the timing and form of pension benefit payments made during severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope: Applies to “Covered Participants” terminated in a Severance Program or under an Individual Severance Agreement on or after January 1, 2009 (or January 1, 2012 for those under Appendix Article PBG). It clarifies that any additional severance-related benefits are not permanent Plan features.
- Definitions: Establishes key terms used in this Article, including:
  - “Applicable Summary Plan Description” (the SPD describing a specific Severance Program).
  - “Covered Participant” (a participant whose employment is terminated and who qualifies for Special Early Retirement either under a Severance Program per the SPD or via an Individual Severance Agreement).
- Interpretation: Capitalized terms not defined in this Article E have the meanings given in the main Plan unless context requires otherwise.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: E.2 Definitions :
nodes.start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix E with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines Appendix Article E of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, governing when and how benefits are paid during severance windows.

Key points:
- Scope and effective dates: Applies to participants terminated under a Severance Program or qualifying Individual Severance Agreement on/after Jan 1, 2009 (or Jan 1, 2012 for those under Appendix Article PBG). Clarifies that severance-related enhancements are not permanent plan features.
- Defined terms:
  - Applicable Summary Plan Description: Governs a specific Severance Program.
  - Covered Participant: A participant whose employment ends and who qualifies for Special Early Retirement via a Severance Program or Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Individual Severance Agreement: An agreement that sets termination terms and explicitly qualifies the participant for Special Early Retirement under PEP.
  - Kicker: The Special Early Retirement benefit equal to the difference between the Early Retirement Pension and the Vested Pension across the Salaried Plan and this Plan, split into:
    - PEP Kicker (nonqualified plan replacement benefits), and
    - Qualified Kicker (qualified plan replacement benefits).
    Early retirement reduction factors before age 55 generally use the 56-to-55 rate unless a Severance Program or Individual Severance Agreement specifies otherwise.
  - Severance Program: As defined in the Salaried Plan (cross-referenced).
  - Special Early Retirement: Meets SPD conditions or is expressly recognized in an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Termination Date: The later of Separation from Service or the projected end of any severance leave; fixed based on formulas in effect when the right to special early retirement arises and does not change due to later events.
- Payment timing/form for 409A Pension (excluding the Kicker):
  - If not retirement-eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with forms under Section 6.2.
  - If retirement-eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior election under Section 6.1(a)(2).

nodes.title: Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension
nodes.heading: E.3 Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered Participant’ s 409A Pension (calculated without regard to the Kicker for purposes of this Section E.3) shall be paid as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how a Participant’s Termination Date is determined at Separation from Service, using severance leave-of-absence formulas in the applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement when special early retirement rights arise; once set, the Termination Date does not change due to later events.
- Defines time and form of payment for the 409A Pension (excluding any Kicker in the calculation for this section):
  - Non-retirement eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2).
  - Becomes Normal/Early retirement eligible after Separation (including during paid leave): paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at Separation or becomes eligible during paid leave: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) with form options under Section 6.2.
- Specifies time and form of Kicker benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s 55th birthday or Separation from Service; a valid prior election under Section 6.1(a)(2) governs even if the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under E.3(b)(2). If the Participant dies after qualifying but before payment, the PEP Kicker is paid in a lump sum to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner.
- Applies to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, referencing Sections 6.1(a)(1), 6.1(a)(2), 6.1(b), 6.2, and Article IV.

nodes.title: Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits
nodes.heading: E.4 Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered Participant’ s PEP Kicker and Qualified Kicker shall be paid as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Defines how a 409A Pension is paid if a participant becomes eligible for Normal, Early, or Special Early Retirement after Separation from Service (including during any paid leave period): it is treated and paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
- Specifies timing and form of payment for “kicker” benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) controls even if the 409A Pension is paid differently. If the participant dies after qualifying but before payment, it is paid in a lump sum within 60 days to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or otherwise to the estate.
  - Qualified Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the Termination Date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time or form; death benefits follow the same 60-day spouse/partner-then-estate rule.
- Establishes a payment delay requirement for Key Employees: any payment triggered by Separation from Service is delayed per Section 6.6, unless an exemption from Section 409A applies.

nodes.title: Delay for Key Employees
nodes.heading: E.5 Delay for Key Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Appendix E to the contrary , if a Participant is determined to be a Key Employee, any payment under this Article E that is made on account of his Separation from Service shall be subject to the required delay in payment for Key Employees under Section 6.6, except to the extent that the payment qualifies for an exemption from the application of Section 409A.
nodes.summary:
- Sets payment rules for a “Qualified Kicker” benefit: generally paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the participant’s termination date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description (SPD) or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time or form, in which case that document governs.
- Establishes death payment provisions: if a participant qualifies for a benefit (including the Qualified Kicker) but dies before payment, the benefit is paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the surviving spouse or eligible domestic partner, or to the estate if none.
- Imposes a Section 409A “Key Employee” delay: if the participant is a Key Employee, any payment triggered by separation from service under Article E is delayed in accordance with Section 6.6, except where a 409A exemption applies.
- Introduces Appendix F (U.K. Supplementary Appendix for Participants with U.S. Service):
  - Scope: applies to “Covered U.K. Employees”; benefits are determined under Section F.3, paid under the plan’s normal time and form rules, and are subject to Code section 409A; Appendix restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011 for pre-2016 service).
  - Defines “Covered U.K. Employee” criteria: a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who (i) becomes subject to U.S. income taxes by engaging in U.S. service, (ii) continues accruing benefits under the U.K. plan during U.S. service, (iii) would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix but for its unavailability during U.S. service, (iv) later is either localized in the U.S. or terminates employment before starting an assignment outside the U.S., and (v) after satisfying those conditions, is designated as covered (designation details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: U.K. Supplementary Appendix Participants with U.S. Service
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE F - U.K. Supplementary Appendix Participants with U.S. Service
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below .
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines Appendix Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, a U.K. Supplementary Appendix for U.K. plan participants who perform U.S. service. It specifies scope and states that benefits for eligible individuals (“Covered U.K. Employees”) are determined under Section F.3 and paid under the Plan’s normal timing and form, with all benefits subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A. It records effective dates (originally effective January 1, 2011; restated January 1, 2016) and describes detailed eligibility criteria for a “Covered U.K. Employee,” including: becoming subject to U.S. income tax due to U.S. service, continuing to accrue under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan during that U.S. service, being the type who would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix but for the suspension of such accruals during U.S. service, subsequently either becoming localized in the U.S. or terminating employment before starting an assignment outside the U.S., and then being specifically designated as covered.

nodes.title: Scope
nodes.heading: F.1 Scope:
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below .

nodes.title: “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined
nodes.heading: F.2 “Covered U.K. Employee” Defined :
nodes.start_phrase: A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan (“U.K. Participant”) who – (i) becomes subject to United States income taxes, e.g., by transferring to a position with the Company in the United States or otherwise
nodes.summary:
- Establishes Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for U.K. employees who perform U.S. service, restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011), with all benefits subject to Code section 409A and paid under the Plan’s standard timing and form rules.
- Defines “Covered U.K. Employee” as a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who: (i) becomes subject to U.S. income taxes (Engages in U.S. Service); (ii) continues accruing under the U.K. Pension Plan during U.S. Service; (iii) would have accrued under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix for that period but for its unavailability during U.S. Service; (iv) is later either localized in the U.S. or terminates employment before starting a non-U.S. assignment; and (v) after meeting all prior conditions, is designated by the Company in its sole discretion, creating a binding right to Article F benefits. The U.S. Service period runs from the U.S. Commencement Date (first subject to U.S. tax) to the U.S. Cessation Date (no longer subject to U.S. tax or earlier if Article F benefits commence).
- Describes benefit determination for Covered U.K. Employees as the Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit minus the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit, measured as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date.
  - Modified U.S. Cessation Date is the earliest of: ceasing U.S. tax status; first satisfying localization/termination condition; starting an assignment outside the U.S.; or Article F benefit commencement.
  - Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit equals the benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix based on all service and compensation through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date that is (or would be but for U.K. legal limits) counted under the U.K. Pension Plan, expressed as a single lump sum payable when Article F benefits commence.
- Notes that the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is subtracted in the formula, though its definition appears beyond the provided excerpt.

nodes.title: Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees
nodes.heading: F.3 Benefit for Covered U.K. Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating, as of his Modified U.S. Cessation Date, his “T otal U.K. Supplementary Benefit” and then subtracting from this amount his “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit.”
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Company, in its sole discretion, may designate certain individuals as Covered U.K. Employees, which grants a legally binding right to an Article F benefit.
- Defines U.S. Service timing based on U.S. income tax status:
  - U.S. Commencement Date: first day the employee becomes subject to U.S. income taxes.
  - U.S. Cessation Date: when the employee is no longer subject to U.S. income taxes or, if earlier, when Article F benefits commence.
- Sets the Article F benefit formula for Covered U.K. Employees as:
  - Benefit = Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit (as of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date) minus Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit (as of immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date), with both expressed as a single lump sum payable when Article F benefits commence.
- Defines key terms:
  - Modified U.S. Cessation Date: earliest of (i) no longer subject to U.S. income taxes, (ii) first satisfying clause (iv) of Section F.2, (iii) starting an assignment outside the United States, or (iv) Article F benefit commencement.
  - Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit: the total benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix, based on all service and compensation through the Modified U.S. Cessation Date that is (or would be but for U.K. legal limits) counted under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan, expressed as a lump sum payable at Article F commencement.
  - Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit: the benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, expressed as a lump sum payable at Article F commencement.
- Provides operating rules for calculations:
  - Accruals under the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan after the U.S. Cessation Date generally do not reduce the Article F benefit.
  - If those post-cessation accruals more than fully offset accruals under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix, the excess may offset Article F benefits, but only to the extent permitted under Code Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum valuations must use actuarial assumptions that comply with applicable Code/Section 409A requirements.

nodes.title: Operating Rules
nodes.heading: F.4 Operating Rules:
nodes.start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation in Section F .3. above.
nodes.summary:
- Defines “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit” as the lump-sum value, determined at Article F commencement, of the participant’s accrued benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix as of immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, calculated per Section F.4.
- Operating rules for calculating the Article F benefit:
  - Post–U.S. Cessation Date accruals in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan generally do not reduce the Article F benefit; however, any excess accruals that would have offset Supplementary Appendix benefits may offset the Article F benefit to the extent permitted by Code Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum valuations must use Code Section 417(e) actuarial assumptions as applied under the Salaried Plan at the relevant determination date.
  - The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is determined assuming the participant voluntarily terminated immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date.
  - If mid‑year amendments to the U.K. Plan or Supplementary Appendix would alter the Section F.3 result, application is delayed to the following year as necessary to comply with Code Section 409A.
  - If the participant later re-enters U.S. Service and again qualifies as a Covered U.K. Employee, Article F applies anew; any new benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to avoid duplication.
  - If the participant later becomes eligible for benefits under other provisions of the Plan, any such benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to avoid duplication.
- No other benefits are payable under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while the individual is (or would be but for specified clauses) a Covered U.K. Employee.
- Before an individual satisfies all requirements to be a Covered U.K. Employee, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit; the Company retains unfettered discretion to deny designation and prevent entitlement, regardless of services performed, until all requirements are met.

nodes.title: No Other Benefits
nodes.heading: F.5 No Other Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while he is a Covered U.K. Employee (or while he would be a Covered U.K. Employee if clauses (iv) and (v) of Section F .2. were not included in the definition of Covered U.K. Employee).
nodes.summary:
- Coordination of benefits for Covered U.K. Employees: If a Covered U.K. Employee has already earned a benefit under Article F, reaches the U.S. Cessation Date, and then works for PepsiCo in a role eligible under other plan provisions, any new benefit under those provisions is calculated for the new service but reduced by the lump-sum value of the prior Article F benefit to avoid duplication.
- Exclusivity and company discretion (F.5): While someone is a Covered U.K. Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan. Before all requirements to be a Covered U.K. Employee are met, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit. The Company may, in its unfettered discretion, take actions (e.g., not designating the individual as a Covered U.K. Employee) that prevent entitlement, regardless of services rendered.
- Appendix G (Delay Election for Certain Pre-2018 Terminees): Establishes a one-time opportunity, effective January 1, 2018, for Participants who separated before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension to delay distribution under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
- Eligibility for Delay Election (G.2): Must have separated before January 1, 2018; have a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date; and be selected and notified by the Company in its sole discretion.
- Requirements for Delay Election (G.3): Election must become effective and irrevocable at least 12 months before the existing Scheduled Payment Date, and the new payment date must be at least 5 years later than the original Scheduled Payment Date (with an upper limit not shown in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 Terminees
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE G - Delay Election For Certain Pre-2018 T erminees
nodes.start_phrase: This Article provides an opportunity for certain Participants, who Separated from Service before January 1, 2018 and who are eligible to receive a 409A V ested Pension, to make a one-time election to delay the distribution of their 409A V ested Pension as permitted by Code section 409A(a)(4)(C).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix G establishes a one-time “Delay Election” for Participants who separated from service before January 1, 2018 and are eligible for a 409A Vested Pension, allowing them to defer distribution under Code section 409A(a)(4)(C), effective January 1, 2018.
- Eligibility requires: (a) separation before January 1, 2018; (b) a Scheduled Payment Date at least 12 months after the election date; and (c) selection and notice by the Company in its sole discretion.
- Election requirements: it must be irrevocable at least 12 months before the original Scheduled Payment Date and set a New Scheduled Payment Date at least five years later, but no later than the first of the month on or after the Participant’s 65th birthday.
- The election cannot change the payment form; however, the annuity form is determined by marital status as of the New Scheduled Payment Date, and any early commencement reduction is recalculated by reference to the New Scheduled Payment Date.
- Cashout provisions in Section 4.9 continue to apply even if a Delay Election is made.
- Appendix H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for periods prior to January 1, 2019: from January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2018 the Plan does not recognize Eligible Domestic Partner status due to the Supreme Court’s 2015 same-sex marriage ruling, with a limited 2016 exception for Participants who had a qualifying domestic partner or civil union as of December 31, 2015 and met specified employment/participant criteria in 2015.
- It also begins rules for June 26, 2013 through December 31, 2015, including recognition of civil unions in states that did not permit same-sex marriage (details partially shown).

nodes.title: Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE H – Definitions of Eligible Domestic Partner Applicable Prior to January 1, 2019
nodes.start_phrase: This Article H provides the definition of Eligible Domestic Partner for periods prior to January 1, 2019.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article H defines “Eligible Domestic Partner” for periods before January 1, 2019, with time-specific rules:
  - Jan 1, 2016–Dec 31, 2018: Domestic partner status not recognized due to nationwide same-sex marriage; limited exception for 2016 for participants who had a qualifying same-sex domestic partner or civil union in place on Dec 31, 2015 and were active/on leave/participants during 2015.
  - June 26, 2013–Dec 31, 2015: For residents of states without same-sex marriage:
    - If the state allows same-sex civil unions: eligibility only if in a valid same-sex civil union.
    - If the state allows neither same-sex marriage nor civil unions: eligibility only if there is a legally binding same-sex domestic partner agreement meeting company requirements.
  - Jan 1, 2013–June 25, 2013: Recognizes spouses in valid same-sex marriages; residents of states permitting same-sex marriage can have an Eligible Domestic Partner only if married or if the state began permitting such marriages less than 12 months before the applicable date.
  - Pre-2013: No Eligible Domestic Partner status.
  - Additional rules: Opposite-sex partners never qualify; residents of states permitting same-sex marriage cannot have an Eligible Domestic Partner (must marry); a 12-month transition applies when a state newly permits marriage or civil unions. Defined terms: “applicable date” is the earlier of annuity start date or death; “state” includes domestic or foreign jurisdictions that sanction marriages or civil unions.

- Appendix Article I establishes a 409A Program makeup benefit for certain Pre-409A Participants:
  - Scope: Avoids “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program by not changing its early commencement actuarial factors; instead provides a makeup aligned with the 2019 Salaried Program Factors. For those already in the 409A Program, the makeup is provided under the main plan; this Article covers affected Pre-409A participants not otherwise eligible under the 409A Program.
  - Eligibility: Applies to Pre-409A Participants receiving a Vested Pension annuity starting before Normal Retirement Date on or after Jan 1, 2019, with the annuity reduced for early commencement under Pre-409A terms (additional criteria follow in the text).

nodes.title: 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE I – 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre-409A Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the definition of Actuarial Equivalent).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article I – 409A PEP Makeup for Certain Pre‑409A Benefits:
  - Purpose/Scope: Provides a 409A Program “make‑up” benefit to avoid materially modifying the Pre‑409A Program by updating early retirement factors; instead, it compensates certain Pre‑409A Participants for harsher early commencement reductions relative to the 2019 Salaried Program Factors. Applies here only to affected Pre‑409A Participants who otherwise are not entitled to a 409A benefit.
  - Eligibility: Must be a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Vested Pension annuity that starts before Normal Retirement Date on/after January 1, 2019; whose early commencement reduction under the Pre‑409A Program is greater than it would be using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors; and who otherwise has no 409A Pension payable on/after January 1, 2019 (or whose 409A Pension began before that date). Such individuals are “Eligible Persons.”
  - Benefit Amount: A single lump sum equal to the Actuarial Equivalent of the difference between (a) the Single Life Annuity using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion) and (b) the actual Single Life Annuity using the pre‑2019 factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion). If the applicable commencement date is December 1, 2019 and the Annuity Starting Date was earlier, the value is determined at the actual start date and brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019. Only the factors effective January 1, 2019 apply.
  - Time of Payment: Payable as of the latest of (a) the first of the month after Separation from Service, (b) December 1, 2019, or (c) the first of the month after age 55 (not applicable to Article PBG‑derived benefits). If payment is delayed under Section 6.6(a) of the Plan, interest is added for the delay under Section 6.6(c).
  - Non‑Duplication: The makeup is reduced to eliminate any duplication if a participant has or will receive a 409A Pension that already provides some/all of the makeup (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or if the Plan Administrator determines duplication would occur; this rule overrides any contrary provision.

- Appendix Article J – Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons (partial):
  - Scope: Establishes special benefit and distribution rules (to be detailed in Sections J.3 and J.4) for “Covered International Employees.”
  - Definitions: A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who (1) is ineligible for PERP, (2) would be barred from earning PIRP‑DB benefits under Section 9.14 of PIRP‑DB due to U.S. Person status, (3) is initially selected by the Vice President based on special retirement‑benefit circumstances, and (4) is subsequently determined by the Vice President to be entitled to this status. Both determinations are in the Vice President’s unfettered discretion. (Further benefit and distribution details not included in the excerpt.)

nodes.title: Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE J - Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons
nodes.start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below .
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article J covers certain international employees who are U.S. Persons within the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope (J.1): Applies to “Covered International Employees”; their benefit determination and distribution are addressed in Sections J.3 and J.4 (not included here).
- Definitions (J.2):
  - Covered International Employee: An employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who (1) is ineligible for PERP, (2) would be barred from earning a PIRP-DB benefit due to U.S. Person status, (3) is initially selected by the Vice President based on special circumstances affecting retirement benefits, and (4) is later determined by the Vice President to be entitled to this status.
  - Selection and entitlement are at the unfettered discretion of the Vice President; the entitlement determination is made in conjunction with the employee’s retirement and not before the year of the distribution date under Section J.4.
  - Prior to entitlement, a Selected International Employee has no legally binding right to a pension or distribution under Article J for purposes of Code Sections 409A and 457A.
  - Designated PepsiCo Affiliate: A non-U.S. organized employing entity designated by the Vice President.
  - PERP: PepsiCo Employees Retirement Plan A, I, H, or successors.
  - PIRP-DB: PepsiCo International Retirement Plan (DB Program).
  - Selected International Employee: Meets eligibility factors (ineligible for PERP, barred from PIRP-DB, initially selected) but not yet finally determined entitled by the Vice President.
  - U.S. Person and Vice President: As defined by PIRP-DB.

nodes.title: Benefit for Covered International Employees
nodes.heading: J.3 Benefit for Covered International Employees :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered International Employee’ s benefit under the Plan shall be determined by calculating the Pension to which he would be entitled under the main part of the Plan (which shall include treating the Covered International Employee as a Plan Participant and reflecting the dif ferences in the calculation of a Participant’ s Pension that is a Vested Pension versus a Retirement Pension), but giving ef fect to the following modifications.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets special rules for “Covered International Employees.”
- Benefit calculation: Determined under the main Plan as if the employee is a Plan Participant, accounting for Vested vs. Retirement Pension differences, with specific modifications.
- Salaried Plan factors: Any benefit-determining factors tied to the Salaried Plan are applied as if the employee was always eligible, subject to the modifications below.
- Offsets: Standard reductions under Section 5.1(a)(2) and (3) (Salaried Pension Plan and Pre-409A Pension Plan offsets) do not apply unless a “Reduction Amount” is listed in the Benefit Information Table; if listed, that amount is the reduction.
- PEP Guarantee: The Section 5.2 PEP Guarantee formula does not apply.
- Service Start Date override: If a “Service Start Date” is specified in the Benefit Information Table, service before that date is disregarded for this Appendix’s pension calculation.
- Earnings Start Date override: If an “Earnings Start Date” is specified, earnings before that date are disregarded for this Appendix’s pension calculation.
- Minimum Lump Sum floor: If a “Minimum Lump Sum” is specified, the pension converted to a single lump sum cannot be less than that amount.
- Example entry: GPID 01170077 has a Minimum Lump Sum of $1,126,465; no Reduction Amount, Service Start Date, or Earnings Start Date apply (all N/A).
- Distribution timing/form: Paid as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following Separation from Service, subject to the key employee delay rules in Section 6.6.
- Operating Rules: Referenced (Section J.5) but content not shown in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Time and Form of Distributions
nodes.heading: J.4 Time and Form of Distributions :
nodes.start_phrase: A Covered International Employee’ s Pension under this Appendix J shall be distributed as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month that is coincident with or next follows the Participant’ s Separation from Service, subject to Section 6.6 of the main part of the Plan (delay for Key Employees).
nodes.summary:
- Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets special rules for determining pensions for Covered International Employees.
- Service and earnings overrides: If a Service Start Date or Earnings Start Date is specified in the Benefit Information Table, any service or earnings before those dates are excluded from the pension calculation.
- Minimum Lump Sum protection: If a Minimum Lump Sum is specified, the pension, when converted to a Single Lump Sum, cannot be less than that amount.
- Example entry: GPID 01170077 shows N/A for reduction, service start, and earnings start dates, with a Minimum Lump Sum of $1,126,465.
- Distribution timing and form: Benefits are paid as a Single Lump Sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following Separation from Service, subject to the Section 6.6 key employee delay.
- Actuarial assumptions: Lump sum valuations use Code Section 417(e) assumptions, specifically those applied under the Salaried Plan for retirement lump sums at the determination date.
- Plan freeze alignment: Pension accruals, rights, and benefits under Appendix J are frozen effective December 31, 2025, to the same extent as the Salaried Plan freeze.
- No other benefits: While designated, Designated/Covered International Employees are not entitled to other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or termination indemnity arrangements.

nodes.title: Operating Rules
nodes.heading: J.5 Operating Rules:
nodes.start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation of a Covered International Employee’ s Pension under this Appendix J.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines operating rules for calculating a Covered International Employee’s Pension under Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Requires Single Lump Sum calculations to use actuarial assumptions compliant with Internal Revenue Code Section 417(e), specifically the same assumptions the Salaried Plan would use as of the lump-sum determination date.
- Confirms the pension is fully subject to the Salaried Plan freeze effective December 31, 2025, with all accruals, rights, and benefits frozen to the same extent as under the Salaried Plan.
- States in Section J.6 (No Other Benefits) that while an individual is a Designated or Covered International Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or any termination indemnity arrangement.

nodes.title: No Other Benefits
nodes.heading: J.6 No Other Benefits :
nodes.start_phrase: A Designated/Covered International Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB or a termination indemnity arrangement while he is a Designated International Employee or a Covered International Employee.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes operating rules for calculating a Covered International Employee’s Pension under Appendix J of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Specifies that any Single Lump Sum value must be determined using actuarial assumptions compliant with IRC Section 417(e), specifically the same assumptions used by the Salaried Plan for a retirement lump sum as of the calculation date.
- Confirms the pension is fully subject to the Salaried Plan freeze effective December 31, 2025, with all accruals, rights, and benefits frozen to the same extent as the Salaried Plan.
- States that while an individual is a Designated or Covered International Employee, they are not entitled to any other benefits under this Plan, the Salaried Plan, PIRP-DB, or any termination indemnity arrangement.

nodes.title: APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG
nodes.heading: APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG
nodes.start_phrase: Effective as of the end of the day on December 31, 2011, the PBG PEP is hereby merged with and into the PepsiCo PEP, with the PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan after the merger .
nodes.summary:
- Effective end of day December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) merged into the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PepsiCo PEP), with PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan.
- This Appendix Article PBG governs legacy PBG PEP benefits that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP document prior to the merger, except:
  - Articles VII (Administration), VIII (Miscellaneous), IX (Amendment and Termination), X (ERISA Plan Structure), and XI (Applicable Law) of the main PepsiCo PEP document apply instead.
  - For Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019, actuarial adjustments from a Single Life Annuity to optional annuities (e.g., survivor, period-certain, death-benefit, or other features) are determined under the main document’s provisions.
- The merger and incorporation of the 409A PBG PEP provisions into this Appendix do not change the time or form of payments for benefits subject to Code section 409A under either plan.
- History and purpose: PBG established the PBG PEP effective April 6, 1999 for salaried employees participating in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan; it was created as a successor to the PepsiCo PEP in connection with PBG’s April 6, 1999 IPO and retained historical PepsiCo provisions relevant to eligibility and benefit determinations.

nodes.title: HISTORY AND PURPOSE
nodes.heading: ARTICLE I T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - HIST ORY AND PURPOSE
nodes.start_phrase: The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. (“PBG”) established the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) ef fective April 6, 1999 for the benefit of salaried employees of the PBG Organization who participate in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan (“Salaried Plan”).
nodes.summary:
- Effective Dec 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (PBG PEP) is merged into the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PepsiCo PEP), with PepsiCo PEP as the surviving plan.
- This Appendix governs PBG PEP benefits that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP Document before the merger, except:
  - Administration, Miscellaneous, Amendment and Termination, ERISA Plan Structure, and Applicable Law are governed by the main PepsiCo PEP document (Articles VII–XI).
  - For Annuity Starting Dates on or after Jan 1, 2019, actuarial adjustments for optional annuities (e.g., survivor, period certain, death benefit) follow the main document.
- The merger and incorporation of the 409A PBG PEP provisions do not change the time or form of payments for benefits subject to Code section 409A under either plan.
- History and purpose:
  - PBG established the PBG PEP on Apr 6, 1999 (post-IPO) as a successor to the PepsiCo PEP for salaried employees in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan.
  - Provides supplemental benefits where qualified plan benefits are limited by the Internal Revenue Code and for certain employees under the pre-1989 formula.
  - Effective Apr 1, 2009, covers pay reductions from deferrals under the PBG Executive Income Deferral Program and certain executives (salary bands E3–E8 or MP) who would otherwise be grandfathered under the Salaried Plan.
  - Intended as a nonqualified, unfunded deferred compensation plan; for ERISA, split into:
    - An “excess benefit plan” (ERISA §4(b)(5)) for Code §415 limitations.
    - A “top-hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 301(a)(3), 401(a)(1)).
  - Amended multiple times, including a full restatement effective Apr 1, 2009; further amended following the 2009 merger to facilitate PepsiCo’s assumption as plan sponsor.
- Effect of amendment and restatement:
  - Defines the Prior Plan as the plan in effect on Oct 3, 2004 and the “Grandfathered Benefit” as the benefit determined as if termination occurred Dec 31, 2004, paid in the time and form under the Oct 3, 2004 terms.
  - Post-2004 accruals (net of the Grandfathered Benefit) are paid per the current plan.
  - The current plan superseded the Prior Plan effective Jan 1, 2009 for amounts accrued and vested after 2004 for participants not in pay status as of that date.
  - From 2005–2008, the plan was administered in good faith compliance with Code §409A; post-2004 amounts are treated as a separate plan for §409A purposes.
- Definitions and construction:
  - Terms used have the meanings set in this Plan; unless otherwise specified, terms align with those in the PBG Salaried Employees Retirement Plan.

nodes.title: DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE II T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - DEFINITIONS AND CONSTRUCTION
nodes.start_phrase: The following words and phrases, when used in this Plan, shall have the meaning set forth below unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes “Grandfathered Benefit” treatment: benefits determined under plan terms in effect on October 3, 2004 as if employment ended December 31, 2004, disregarding post‑2004 compensation or events (other than survival/elections), to be paid in the time and form provided under the 2004 plan terms.
- Provides that non‑grandfathered benefits (total accrued under Prior Plan and this Plan minus the Grandfathered Benefit) are payable under this Plan’s time/form rules; the Plan superseded the Prior Plan effective January 1, 2009 for amounts accrued and vested after 2004 for participants not yet in pay status.
- Describes Section 409A compliance history: administered in good faith with 409A from 2005–2008; amounts accrued after 2004 treated as a separate plan for 409A purposes.
- Defines key terms and structure (Article II), including:
  - Actuarial Equivalent; Annuity; Code; ERISA; Plan, PepsiCo Prior Plan, and Plan Administrator (PepsiCo Administration Committee); Effective Date (April 6, 1999) and Effective Time (February 26, 2010); Company (PepsiCo, Inc.; previously The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. before the Effective Time).
  - Compensation Limitation (Code §401(a)(17)) and Section 415 Limitation; Salaried Plan (Part C governs); Salaried Plan Participant; Employer; Employee; Participant.
  - PepsiCo/PBG Organization (controlled group under Code §414).
  - PEP Pension and Grandfathered Benefit; Single Lump Sum (for the portion in excess of Grandfathered Benefit).
  - Separation from Service; Section 409A; Plan Year.
  - Primary Social Security Amount assumptions and exclusions for pension calculations (assumes wages at the taxable wage base until retirement/severance; special rule for vested pensions; excludes spouse/dependent and post‑severance adjustments; measured as of Severance from Service Date).
  - Vested Pension.
- Provides comprehensive “Specified Employee” identification rules for 409A (officers/owners thresholds; annual December 31 determination effective the following April 1; administrative convenience rule treating E5+ as specified employees subject to a 200‑person cap; special transition combining lists Feb 26–Mar 31, 2010; post‑April 1, 2010 method using Band IV/E7/Salary Grade 19 classifications with caps; intended as an alternative method under Treas. Reg. §1.409A‑1(i)(5)).
- Sets construction rules (gender/number usage; “hereof/hereunder” refer to entire Plan).
- Defines participation eligibility (Article III): all Salaried Plan Participants whose benefits are limited by §401(a)(17) or §415; specified groups tied to Grandfathered status and elective deferrals to the Executive Income Deferral Program during 4/1/2009–12/31/2010 (with special treatment for certain E3–E8 or MP classifications as of 3/31/2009); and those with 1988 pensionable earnings of $75,000 or more.

nodes.title: PARTICIPATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE III T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - P ARTICIP ATION
nodes.start_phrase: Each Salaried Plan Participant whose benefit under the Salaried Plan is curtailed by the Compensation Limitation or the Section 415 Limitation, or both, and each other Salaried Plan Participant (i) who is a Grandfathered Employee as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan and who made elective deferrals to the EID on or after April 1, 2009 and before January 1, 2011 (inclusively); (ii) who would have been considered a Grandfathered Participant as defined in Section 3.7 of the Salaried Plan during the period April 1, 2009 through December 31, 2010 if the Participant had not been classified by the Employer as salary band E3-E8 or MP on March 31, 2009; or (iii) whose 1988 pensionable “earnings” under the Salaried Plan, as described in Section 4.2(a), were $75,000 or more, shall participate in this Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program defining key terms and calculation rules.
- Defines “Vested Pension” as the PEP benefit for a participant who is vested but not eligible for a Retirement Pension.
- Sets plan construction rules: gender-neutral usage, singular/plural flexibility, and that “hereof,” “hereunder,” etc., refer to the entire plan.
- Establishes participation eligibility for certain Salaried Plan Participants, including those whose Salaried Plan benefits are limited by the Compensation Limitation or IRC Section 415 limits; specified “Grandfathered” groups tied to elective deferrals to the EID between April 1, 2009 and December 31, 2010; those who would have been Grandfathered but for classification as salary band E3–E8 or MP on March 31, 2009; and those with 1988 pensionable earnings of $75,000 or more.
- Outlines the PEP Pension amount: determined at Separation from Service and subject to Sections 4.5 and 8.7. When paid in the same form and at the same time as the Salaried Plan pension, the monthly PEP Pension equals the excess of (i) the hypothetical Salaried Plan benefit ignoring the Compensation Limitation, Section 415 limits, certain 2009–2010 EID deferral exclusions, and specified Grandfathered Participant exclusions (or, if applicable, an amount under Section 4.2), over (ii) the actual monthly benefit payable under the Salaried Plan.

nodes.title: AMOUNT OF RETIREMENT PENSION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE IV T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - AMOUNT OF RETIREMENT PENSION
nodes.start_phrase: PEP Pension . Subject to Sections 4.5 and 8.7, a Participant’ s PEP Pension shall equal the amount determined under (a) or (b) of this Section 4.1, whichever is applicable.
nodes.summary:
- Document scope: Article IV of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program setting how the “PEP Pension” (an excess pension) is determined as of a participant’s Separation from Service, with references to Sections 4.5, 6.2, and 8.7.
- Core formula (Section 4.1):
  - Greater‑of basis: Compares (i) the pension the participant would receive under the Salaried Plan ignoring certain limits/exclusions with (ii) any applicable PEP Guarantee under Section 4.2.
  - Limits/exclusions ignored in the hypothetical Salaried Plan benefit: the Compensation Limitation (401(a)(17)), the Section 415 Limitation, exclusion of earnings deferred under the EID from Apr 1, 2009–Dec 31, 2010, and the 2009–2010 exclusion from the Salaried Plan’s “Grandfathered Participant” definition for specified salary bands (E3–E8 or MP) meeting age/service thresholds.
  - Offset: Reduces the result by the actual benefit payable under the Salaried Plan.
  - Grandfathered Benefit: Any portion identified as the participant’s Grandfathered Benefit is excluded from the PEP amount payable; payments follow Section 6.2.
- Payment coordination by form/timing:
  - Same form/time as Salaried Plan (4.1(a)): Monthly PEP equals the excess of the greater‑of amount over the actual Salaried Plan benefit, less any Grandfathered Benefit.
  - Different form/time (4.1(b)): Calculates the greater‑of amount in the PEP’s elected form/time, then applies a fraction based on actuarial values to reflect the difference between the uncapped and actual Salaried Plan benefits; valuation is on a reasonable and consistent basis at the Plan Administrator’s discretion; subtracts any Grandfathered Benefit; paid per Section 6.2.
- QDRO coordination: If an alternate payee is awarded benefits under a qualified domestic relations order (Code §414(p)), the PEP Pension is adjusted so that the combined payments from this Plan and the Salaried Plan to the participant and alternate payee equal the amounts produced by the Section 4.1 formulas.
- PEP Guarantee (Section 4.2):
  - Subject to Section 8.7.
  - Eligibility: Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings recognized for accrual under the 1988 Salaried Plan; excludes remuneration from periods when the paying entity was not an Employer.
  - Benefit amount to be determined under Section 4.2(b) (not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: PEP Guarantee Formula
nodes.heading: (b) PEP Guarantee Formula .
nodes.start_phrase:
The amount of a Participant’ s PEP Guarantee shall be determined
under paragraph (1), subject to the special rules in paragraph (2).
nodes.summary:
- Sets the PEP Guarantee formula:
  - 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for the first 10 years of Credited Service, plus
  - 1% of HAME for each year of Credited Service over 10, minus
  - 1 2/3% of the Primary Social Security Amount times Credited Service (capped at 30 years).

- Describes vested pension methodology:
  - First, project Credited Service to Normal Retirement Age and use HAME and Primary Social Security Amount at the earlier of Severance from Service or accrual cessation.
  - Then prorate by the ratio of actual Credited Service to projected Credited Service to Normal Retirement Age.

- Special calculation rules:
  - Survivor benefit for Eligible Spouse/Domestic Partner: 50% of the Participant’s annuity with no reduction to the Participant’s annuity; if the survivor is over 10 years younger, reduce by 0.8% per full year ages 11–20 and an additional 0.4% per full year beyond 20; applies to those retiring on/after Early Retirement Date.
  - Early retirement reduction: 3/12 of 1% per month benefits commence before Normal Retirement Date.
  - Vested Pension commencing before Normal Retirement Date: convert to Actuarial Equivalent; apply Salaried Plan reductions for Pre-Retirement Spouse/Domestic Partner coverage.
  - If electing:
    - A form with greater surviving spouse/partner benefits than the standard 50%,
    - A survivor annuity for a non-eligible beneficiary, or
    - An annuity with inflation protection,
    then reduce the PEP Guarantee so the total value equals the Actuarial Equivalent of the standard form (e.g., Single Life Annuity or elected annuity without inflation protection, as applicable).
  - Lump sum distribution: convert PEP Guarantee to its Actuarial Equivalent, factoring in survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.

- April 1, 2009 Salaried Plan changes:
  - Certain employees (salary bands E3–E8 or MP) who as of March 31, 2009 were age 50 with 5 years of Service or had age + Service ≥ 65 are treated as Grandfathered for April 1, 2009–December 31, 2010 (Earnings and Credited Service not frozen).
  - HAME disregards exclusions for EID elective deferrals made between April 1, 2009 and December 31, 2010.

- Notes upcoming Section 4.3: benefits are subject to additional adjustments; defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or a similar nonqualified pension plan sponsored by a PBG member.

nodes.title: Certain Adjustments
nodes.heading: 4.3 Certain Adjustments .
nodes.start_phrase:
Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to
adjustment as provided in this section.
nodes.summary:
- Explains how the PEP Guarantee is converted to a lump sum as the actuarial equivalent of the annuity, factoring in survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
- Details special April 1, 2009 Salaried Plan provisions:
  - Certain E3–E8/MP participants meeting age/service thresholds (age 50 with 5 years, or age + service ≥ 65) are treated as Grandfathered Participants from April 1, 2009, so Earnings and Credited Service were not frozen through December 31, 2010.
  - Highest Average Monthly Earnings are calculated without excluding participant EID deferrals made from April 1, 2009 to December 31, 2010.
- Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified pension plans within the PBG organization whose benefits are not based on participant deferrals, including the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
- Provides adjustment rules:
  - Rehired participants: If the Salaried Plan benefit is (or would have been) recalculated for additional Credited Service after the annuity start date, the PEP Pension is recalculated, with adjustments for prior/in‑service distributions and coordination with specified plans.
  - Increases in benefits under specified plans after PEP determination trigger a PEP recalculation; overpayments may be recovered; no duplication of benefits is intended.
  - Offsets are limited to avoid changes in time or form of payment prohibited by Section 409A; the Company may arrange 409A‑compliant coordination under qualifying plans to permit offsets without violating 409A.
- Addresses reemployment: Non‑Grandfathered PEP Pension payments continue during reemployment; any additional PEP accrued after reemployment will be reduced at subsequent separation by the present value of prior PEP payments.
- States vesting: A participant’s PEP Accrued Benefit vests when the participant vests under the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 and further plan provisions (text incomplete).

nodes.title: Reemployment of Certain Participants
nodes.heading: 4.4 Reemployment of Certain Participants .
nodes.start_phrase:
In the case of a current or former Participant who is
reemployed and is eligible to reparticipate in the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, payment of his non-
Grandfathered PEP Pension will not be suspended.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies how the Salaried Plan’s Transfers and Non-Duplication rules (Part A §3.8 and Part C §3.6) apply when calculating benefits under §4.1(a)(1) or §4.1(b)(1): they apply only to the extent they do not cause a change in the time or form of payment prohibited by IRC §409A.
- States the Company’s intent to implement legally permissible, §409A-compliant special arrangements under any qualifying plan to avoid prohibited changes in payment timing/form; if such arrangements are timely implemented, the usual limit on offsets will not apply.
- Reemployment rules (§4.4): If a participant is reemployed after his Annuity Starting Date and is eligible to re-enter the Salaried Plan, payments of his non-Grandfathered PEP Pension will continue (no suspension). If additional PEP benefits accrue after reemployment, the subsequent benefit will be reduced by the present value of PEP benefits previously paid.
- Vesting and misconduct (§4.5, partial): A participant becomes fully vested in his PEP Accrued Benefit when he is fully vested under the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 and potential misconduct provisions (text truncated).
- Overall context: Provisions are part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, addressing offsets, reemployment, vesting, and compliance with §409A.

nodes.title: Vesting; Misconduct
nodes.heading: 4.5 Vesting; Misconduct .
nodes.start_phrase:
Subject to Section 8.7, a Participant shall be fully vested in his Accrued Benefit at
the time he becomes fully vested in his accrued benefit under the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Coordination with Salaried Plan non-duplication/transfer rules: Offsets under the Salaried Plan’s Non-Duplication provisions apply to PEP Pension calculations only to the extent they do not change the time or form of payment in a way prohibited by Section 409A. The Company intends to implement 409A-compliant special arrangements under qualifying plans to avoid such changes; when such arrangements are in place, the offset limits do not apply.
- Reemployment after annuity starting date: Payments of a non-Grandfathered PEP Pension are not suspended upon reemployment. If additional PEP benefits accrue after reemployment, the subsequent PEP Pension is reduced by the present value of previously paid PEP benefits.
- Vesting and misconduct: Vesting in the PEP mirrors vesting under the Salaried Plan (subject to Section 8.7). A participant forfeits the entire PEP Pension if the Plan Administrator, in good faith, finds “Misconduct,” regardless of whether it occurred before or after severance. The Plan Administrator may also require repayment of PEP amounts paid within the prior 12 months.
- Definition of “Misconduct”: Includes violations of agreements (e.g., confidentiality, non-solicit, non-compete), duties (including Code of Conduct), disparagement, misuse or disclosure of confidential information, unlawful trading/insider trading, actions against the Company’s best interests (including employee solicitation), and felonies or gross misconduct. Whistleblowing to government authorities is protected; attorney-client privilege is preserved.
- Death benefits: For participants who die before their annuity starting date, the death benefit equals what would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP applied there. The portion above the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a single lump sum at death. Beneficiaries mirror the Salaried Plan, including eligible domestic partners for deaths on/after January 1, 2013.
- Distributions: Article VI governs the form and timing of PEP Pension distributions, subject to Section 6.5.

nodes.title: DEATH BENEFITS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE V T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - DEA TH BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase:
Each Participant entitled to a PEP Pension under this Plan who dies before his Annuity
Starting Date shall be entitled to a death benefit equal in amount to the additional death benefit to which the
Participant would have been entitled under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension as determined under Article IV was
payable under the Salaried Plan instead of this Plan.
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines that while certain conduct may be deemed gross misconduct, participants are not prohibited from communicating with government authorities about potential legal violations; the company maintains its attorney-client privilege. It then details Article V (Death Benefits) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program: if a participant entitled to a PEP Pension dies before their annuity start date, the death benefit equals the additional amount that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan as if the PEP Pension were paid there; any portion exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a single lump sum at death. Benefits are paid to beneficiaries in the same manner and proportions as under the Salaried Plan, including to eligible domestic partners for deaths on or after January 1, 2013. Article VI (Distributions) states that it governs how PEP Pensions are distributed, with Section 6.1 addressing the form and timing of payments, subject to Section 6.5.

nodes.title: Death Benefits
nodes.heading: 5.1 Death Benefits .
nodes.start_phrase:
Each Participant entitled to a PEP Pension under this Plan who dies before his Annuity
Starting Date shall be entitled to a death benefit equal in amount to the additional death benefit to which the
Participant would have been entitled under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension as determined under Article IV was
payable under the Salaried Plan instead of this Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that while certain conduct may constitute gross misconduct, the Plan does not restrict Participants from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations; the Company maintains attorney-client privilege over protected information.
- Article V (Appendix PBG) outlines pre-retirement death benefits for Participants entitled to a PEP Pension who die before their Annuity Starting Date:
  - The death benefit equals the additional death benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension were paid there instead.
  - Any portion of the PEP Pension exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is payable as a single lump sum on the date of death.
  - Benefits are paid to the same beneficiaries and in the same proportions as under the Salaried Plan, including Eligible Domestic Partners for deaths on or after January 1, 2013.
- Article VI (Appendix PBG) introduces rules governing distributions of PEP Pensions, with Section 6.1 addressing the form and timing of distributions (subject to Section 6.5).

nodes.title: DISTRIBUTIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE VI T O APPENDIX ARTICLE PBG - DISTRIBUTIONS
nodes.start_phrase:
The terms of this Article govern the distribution of benefits to a Participant who becomes entitled to payment of
a PEP Pension under the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Confirms that, despite rules around misconduct, participants are not restricted from communicating with government authorities about possible legal violations; the company preserves attorney‑client privilege.
- Article V (Appendix Article PBG – Death Benefits):
  - If a participant entitled to a PEP Pension dies before the Annuity Starting Date, a death benefit is provided equal to the additional death benefit that would apply under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension were paid there.
  - Any portion of the PEP Pension death benefit exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a single lump sum on the date of death.
  - Death benefits are paid to the same beneficiaries and in the same proportions as under the Salaried Plan, including Eligible Domestic Partners for deaths on/after January 1, 2013.
- Article VI (Appendix Article PBG – Distributions):
  - Sets the rules for distribution of PEP Pensions, with Section 6.1 addressing the form and timing of distributions, subject to Section 6.5.

nodes.title: Form and Timing of Distributions
nodes.heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions .
nodes.start_phrase:
Subject to Section 6.5, this Section shall govern the form and timing
of PEP Pensions.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies that certain conduct constitutes gross misconduct, but affirms participants’ right to communicate with government authorities about possible legal violations; preserves the Company’s attorney-client privilege.
- Article V (Death Benefits):
  - For participants entitled to a PEP Pension who die before their Annuity Starting Date, the death benefit equals the additional death benefit that would have been payable under the Salaried Plan if the PEP Pension were paid there.
  - The portion of the death benefit exceeding the Grandfathered Benefit is paid as a Single Lump Sum on the date of death.
  - Payments follow the beneficiary designations/proportions under the Salaried Plan, including Eligible Domestic Partners for pre-retirement deaths on or after January 1, 2013.
- Article VI (Distributions of PEP Pensions):
  - Section 6.1 Form and Timing:
    - Grandfathered Benefit: paid per plan terms in effect on October 3, 2004.
    - Non-Grandfathered Benefit: generally paid as a Single Lump Sum upon Separation from Service.
    - Special cases:
      - Certain vested pensions: participants who separated between Jan 1, 2005–Dec 31, 2008 and whose Annuity Starting Date had not occurred by Jan 1, 2009 receive a Single Lump Sum on Jan 1, 2009.
