      - Annuity election: participants age 50 by Jan 1, 2009 who irrevocably elected an annuity by Dec 31, 2008 and who terminate on/after July 1, 2009 after meeting specified age/service milestones (age 55 + 10 years of service, or age 65 + 5 years) receive the elected annuity starting the first day of the month on/after Separation; otherwise, a Single Lump Sum at Separation applies.
      - 2008 reorganization: certain involuntary separations between Nov 1–Dec 19, 2008 (age 50–54, 10+ years of service, eligible under a letter agreement) receive a Single Lump Sum on the last day of the defined Transition Period.
      - Specified Employees (409A): six-month payment delay after Separation; suspended amounts accrue interest at the applicable lump-sum rate.
      - Actual payment date: paid as soon as administratively feasible, no later than end of the calendar year of the specified date or the 15th day of the third month thereafter; further delay permitted if calculation is impracticable beyond the participant’s control, with payment in the first practicable year.
  - Section 6.2 Special Rules for Survivor Options:
    - If a participant who made an annuity election under 6.1(b)(2) dies before Separation, the election is disregarded.
    - Participants may change the coannuitant for a Joint and Survivor Annuity prior to Separation and may change the beneficiary of a 10-Year Certain and Life Annuity at any time.
    - If death occurs after the election is effective but before non-Grandfathered payments commence, the election is honored; survivor benefits to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month following death; any back payments due are paid to the estate.
    - The excerpt ends mid-provision regarding the 10-Year Certain and Life Annuity.

nodes.title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
nodes.heading: 6.2 Special Rules for Survivor Options .
nodes.start_phrase:
If a Participant makes an Annuity election described in Section
6.1(b)(2) and the Participant dies before his Separation from Service, the election shall be disregarded.
nodes.summary:
- Payment timing: Benefits due on dates specified in Articles V or VI must be paid as soon as administratively feasible, no later than the later of the end of the calendar year of the specified date or the 15th day of the third month following that date. Participants cannot choose the taxable year. Payment may be further delayed if calculation is impracticable due to events beyond the participant’s control, with payment in the first calendar year when practicable.

- Survivor option rules:
  - If a participant elected an annuity with a survivor option and dies before separation from service, the election is disregarded. The coannuitant for a Joint and Survivor Annuity can be changed any time before separation; the beneficiary for a Ten Years Certain and Life Annuity can be changed at any time.
  - If the participant dies after the election becomes effective but before the non-Grandfathered PEP Pension starts, the election is honored; survivor payments to the Eligible Spouse, Eligible Domestic Partner, or other beneficiary begin the first day of the month after death; any back payments owed to the participant go to the estate.
  - For a Ten Years Certain and Life Annuity: if the participant dies after commencement, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and fewer than 120 payments have been made, remaining payments go to the participant’s estate. If a beneficiary was receiving payments and dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - If the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner: a 100% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 10 years younger; a 75% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 19 years younger.

- Beneficiary designation: Participants electing a form with a survivor option must designate a beneficiary on a PEP Election Form; they may change or revoke the designation until the election is finally effective. Designations and changes must follow Plan Administrator rules and are not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.heading: 6.3 Designation of Beneficiary .
nodes.start_phrase:
A Participant who has elected to receive all or part of his pension in a form
of payment that includes a survivor option shall designate a beneficiary who will be entitled to any amounts payable
on his death.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses death-benefit handling under certain annuity/survivor payment forms: if a participant dies after payments start, has no surviving primary or contingent beneficiary, and fewer than 120 payments have been made, the remaining payments go to the participant’s estate; if a beneficiary had begun receiving payments and then dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
- Imposes age-difference limits when the beneficiary is not an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner: the 100% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 10 years younger; the 75% survivor option cannot be elected with a beneficiary more than 19 years younger.
- Sets beneficiary designation rules for forms with a survivor option: the participant must designate the beneficiary on a PEP Election Form; may change or revoke the designation any time before the election becomes finally effective; designations must follow Plan Administrator rules and are not effective until filed with the Plan Administrator.
- Excerpt is from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Determination of Single Lump Sum Amounts
nodes.heading: 6.4 Determination of Single Lump Sum Amounts .
nodes.start_phrase:
Except as otherwise provided below , a Single Lump
Sum payable under Article V or Section 6.1 shall be determined in the same manner as the single lump sum payment
option prescribed in Section 6.1(b)(3) of the Salaried Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how Single Lump Sum amounts under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program) are calculated, generally mirroring the single lump sum option in Section 6.1(b)(3) of the Salaried Plan for payments under Article V or Section 6.1.
- For participants with vested pensions who are not eligible for an immediate pension at separation, the lump sum is determined using the Salaried Plan’s method, but for plan years beginning before 2012 substitutes applicable segment rates in place of the blended 30-year Treasury and segment rates otherwise used.
- Creates a special rule for participants involuntarily terminated due to the 2008 Reorganization between November 1 and December 19, 2008: their lump sum is calculated using the Salaried Plan’s December 2008 optional lump sum interest and mortality assumptions, with a floor equal to the amount that would be determined using the interest and mortality assumptions applicable in the actual month of distribution.
- Adds a Section 162(m) postponement provision: no PEP Pension will be paid before the earliest date on which the Company’s federal income tax deduction for the payment would not be disallowed under Internal Revenue Code Section 162(m).

nodes.title: Section 162(m) Postponement
nodes.heading: 6.5 Section 162(m) Postponement .
nodes.start_phrase:
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , no
PEP Pension shall be paid to any Participant prior to the earliest date on which the Company’ s federal income tax
deduction for such payment is not precluded by
nodes.summary:
- Defines how Single Lump Sum benefits are calculated under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program), generally mirroring the single lump sum option in the Salaried Plan (Section 6.1(b)(3)), unless stated otherwise.
- For participants not eligible for an immediate pension at separation (vested but not immediately payable), the lump sum is determined using the Salaried Plan method, substituting applicable segment rates (for plan years beginning before 2012) in place of the blended 30-year Treasury/segment rates otherwise used.
- Provides a special rule for employees involuntarily terminated due to the 2008 Reorganization between Nov 1 and Dec 19, 2008: their lump sum uses the Salaried Plan’s December 2008 interest rates and mortality; however, the amount cannot be less than what would result from the interest rates and mortality applicable in the month of actual distribution.
- Imposes a Section 162(m) postponement: no PEP Pension payments are made until they are tax-deductible to the Company under Section 162(m); once deductible, payment is made as soon as administratively feasible, with simple interest at 6% per year credited for the delay period.
- Introduces an Appendix to Article PBG that overrides the main plan text where conflicts exist and adds provisions for specified individuals.
- Article IPO (Transferred and Transition Individuals) clarifies rights and benefits following the spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan and provides special definitions, including “Agreement,” defined as the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.

nodes.title: Foreword
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX T O ARTICLE PBG 
Foreword
nodes.start_phrase:
This Appendix sets forth additional provisions applicable to individuals specified in the Articles of this
Appendix.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses payment timing under Section 162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code: if a payment is delayed solely to preserve the Company’s tax deduction, it must be paid as soon as administratively feasible once the deduction is permitted, with deferred amounts accruing simple interest at 6% annually for the delay period.
- Introduces an Appendix to Article PBG that contains additional provisions for specified individuals and states that, in any conflict with the main Plan text, the Appendix controls.
- Establishes Article A (Article IPO) for Transferred and Transition Individuals, outlining rights and benefits following the spin-off of this Plan from the PepsiCo prior plan.
- Provides a definitions section (IPO.2) for boldface, underlined terms used in the Article, including “Agreement,” defined as the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.
- Identifies the document context as part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Transferred and Transition Individuals
nodes.heading: Article A (Article IPO) – T ransferred and T ransition Individuals
nodes.start_phrase:
This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and
benefits of T ransferred and T ransition Individuals following the spinof f of this Plan from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Explains treatment of payments limited by Internal Revenue Code Section 162(m): if a payment is delayed solely due to the deduction cap, it will be paid as soon as administratively feasible once the limitation no longer applies, with simple interest at 6% annually for the delay period.
- Introduces an Appendix to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program that contains additional provisions for specified individuals and supersedes the main Plan text in case of conflict.
- Establishes Article A (Article IPO) covering Transferred and Transition Individuals after the Plan’s spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan, detailing scope and applicability.
- Sets out definition rules for terms used in Article IPO, referencing Section 2.1 of the Plan for undefined terms, and specifically defines “Agreement” as the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.

nodes.title: Scope
nodes.heading: IPO.1 Scope .
nodes.start_phrase:
This Article supplements the main portion of the Plan document with respect to the rights and
benefits of T ransferred and T ransition Individuals following the spinof f of this Plan from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses Section 162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code: if a payment’s tax deductibility is precluded, payment is delayed until deductible, then paid as soon as administratively feasible with simple interest at 6% for the delay period.
- Introduces an Appendix to Article PBG that contains additional provisions for specified individuals; the Appendix controls in case of conflict with the main Plan text.
- Article A (Article IPO) covers Transferred and Transition Individuals, outlining supplemental rights and benefits following the spin-off of this Plan from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
- Provides a specialized Definitions section for Article IPO: defined terms in bold/underlined apply as stated; otherwise, terms use meanings from Plan Section 2.1.
- Defines “Agreement” as the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc.
- Document context: PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: IPO.2 Definitions .
nodes.start_phrase:
This section provides definitions for the following words or phrases in boldface and
underlined.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses Section 162(m) deduction limits: if a payment is delayed solely due to this tax rule, it will be paid as soon as deductible, with simple interest at 6% annually for the delay.
- Introduces an Appendix to the Plan that provides additional provisions for specified individuals; in case of conflict, the Appendix controls over the main Plan text.
- Article A (IPO) covers Transferred and Transition Individuals after the Plan’s spinoff from the PepsiCo Prior Plan.
  - Defines key terms by reference to the 1999 Employee Programs Agreement between PepsiCo, Inc. and The Pepsi Bottling Group, Inc. (Agreement), including Close of the Distribution Date, Transferred Individual, and Transition Individual; other terms follow Plan Section 2.1.
  - Provides that all Transferred Individuals who participated in the PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately before the Effective Date automatically become Participants in this Plan as of the Effective Date.
  - Confirms no break in Service or Credited Service due to the spinoff for Transferred or Transition Individuals.
  - Ensures prior service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations recognized under the PepsiCo Prior Plan continue under this Plan as if they occurred here, avoiding duplication of benefits.
  - States that Transition Individuals’ benefits are determined in accordance with Agreement Section 8.02.
- Article B (Special Cases) supplements the main Plan and is effective January 28, 2002.

nodes.title: Rights of Transferred and Transition Individuals
nodes.heading: IPO.3 Rights of T ransferred and T ransition Individuals .
nodes.start_phrase:
All Transferred Individuals who participated in the
PepsiCo Prior Plan immediately prior to the Ef fective Date shall be Participants in this Plan as of the Ef fective Date.
nodes.summary: Excerpt outlines cross-referenced definitions (“Close of the Distribution Date,” “Transferred Individual,” “Transition Individual”) and details how a spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program affects participants. Transferred Individuals who were in the prior plan immediately before the Effective Date automatically become participants in the new plan as of that date, and the spin-off does not cause a break in Service or Credited Service for Transferred or Transition Individuals. All service, compensation, and other benefit-affecting determinations recognized under the prior plan as of the Close of the Distribution Date will be fully recognized under the new plan as if incurred there, except where this would duplicate benefits. Benefits for Transition Individuals are determined per section 8.02 of the Agreement. Article B – Special Cases is noted as supplementing the main plan and effective January 28, 2002.

nodes.title: Special Cases
nodes.heading: Article B – Special Cases
nodes.start_phrase:
This Article B of the Appendix supplements the main portion of the Plan document and is ef fective as of
January 28, 2002.
nodes.summary:
- Defines and cross-references key terms (Close of the Distribution Date, Transferred Individual, Transition Individual) to an underlying Agreement.
- Establishes rights for Transferred and Transition Individuals after a spin-off from the PepsiCo Prior Plan:
  - Automatic participation as of the Effective Date for prior participants.
  - No break in service or credited service due to the spin-off.
  - Full recognition under the new plan of prior service, compensation, and benefit-affecting determinations from the PepsiCo Prior Plan as of the Close of the Distribution Date, avoiding duplication of benefits.
  - Transition Individuals’ benefits governed by section 8.02 of the Agreement.
- Introduces Article B – Special Cases (effective January 28, 2002) for certain highly compensated Band IV hires designated for a supplemental retirement benefit:
  - Defines the PEP Pension as the excess of a hypothetical uncapped Salaried Plan benefit (ignoring Compensation and Section 415 limits and assuming employment began September 10, 1990) over the sum of actual benefits payable from the Salaried Plan and other PepsiCo/affiliate/Tricon/YUM! defined benefit plans, adjusted for differing commencement dates.
  - Provides a death benefit for eligible individuals who die while employed, calculated under the same formula, reduced by survivor benefits from the referenced plans, and paid as a single lump sum per Article V.
  - Grants the Plan Administrator discretion to adjust benefits to ensure the aggregate does not exceed the intended overall pension equivalent to continuous service with the Company from September 10, 1990 through separation.

nodes.title: Transfers From/To PepsiCo, Inc.
nodes.heading: Article C – T ransfers From/T o PepsiCo, Inc.
nodes.start_phrase:
The provisions of this Article C shall only apply to transfers that occur before February 26, 2010 and shall not
apply to any transfer to PepsiCo, Inc. or from PepsiCo, Inc. that occurs on or after such date.
nodes.summary:
- Article C governs pension treatment for employees transferring between the Company and PepsiCo, Inc. only for transfers occurring before February 26, 2010, and it supersedes the main Plan for these cases.
- Transfers to PepsiCo, Inc.: The PEP Pension is fixed as of the transfer date using Article IV rules, including applying the Salaried Plan offset whether or not that benefit moves to a PepsiCo qualified plan. The determined benefit is payable at Separation from Service per Article VI.
- Transfers from PepsiCo, Inc.: The PEP Pension is determined at Separation from Service per Article IV and reduced by any PepsiCo plan benefits based on overlapping credited service so the combined benefits do not exceed what the Participant would have received if always employed by the Company. For transfers on or after January 1, 2005, the benefit cannot be less than the Company-only benefit. The Plan Administrator may adjust calculations to carry out this intent.
- Appendix Article PAC sets guiding principles for appointing members of the PAC (benefit plan committee).
  - Eligibility: must be a PepsiCo Organization employee at Leadership Group 1 or higher, able to devote sufficient time, and act prudently and solely in participants’ and beneficiaries’ interests.
  - Experience: each member should have benefit plan/ERISA administration experience (or comparable), the committee collectively should cover ERISA health/welfare and retirement plan expertise, and members should be able to evaluate plan expenses prudently.
  - The PAC Chair may consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify qualified candidates.

nodes.title: Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.heading:
APPENDIX ARTICLE P AC
Guiding Principles Regarding Benefit Plan Committee Appointments
nodes.start_phrase:
This Article P AC supplements the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan document with respect to
the appointment of the members of the P AC.
nodes.summary:
- Appendix Article PAC sets guiding principles for appointing members to PepsiCo’s Benefit Plan Committee (PAC) under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope: Supplements the plan document specifically on PAC member appointments.
- Eligibility criteria: Must be a PepsiCo employee at Leadership Group 1 or above, able to devote sufficient time, and possess the character and prudence to act solely in the interests of plan participants and beneficiaries.
- Additional PAC membership guidelines: 
  - Individual experience with benefit plan administration or transferable ERISA-related experience.
  - Collective committee expertise across ERISA health and welfare and retirement plan administration.
  - Ability to prudently evaluate plan-related expenses.
- Chair’s process: May consult internal leaders (Controller, CFO, CHRO) to identify well-qualified candidates.
- Legal note: These guidelines are advisory for the Chair and do not alter ERISA’s legal standards.
- Exhibit 21: Begins a roster of PepsiCo, Inc. subsidiaries (as of Dec. 25, 2021) with entity names and jurisdictions spanning multiple countries and U.S. states, including numerous “Blue Cloud Distribution” state entities and other global subsidiaries; the list is partial in the excerpt.

structure.title: PEPSICO, INC. SUBSIDIARIES (as of December 25, 2021)
structure.heading:
EXHIBIT 21
PEPSICO, INC. SUBSIDIARIES (as of December 25, 2021)
structure.start_phrase: Entity Name Jurisdiction
structure.summary:
- Purpose: A statutory Exhibit 21 listing PepsiCo, Inc.’s consolidated subsidiaries as of December 25, 2021.
- Format: An alphabetical roster of hundreds of legal entities paired with their jurisdictions of incorporation/organization.
- Scope of entities: Operating companies, bottling and concentrate manufacturers, sales and distribution arms, R&D and shared services centers, logistics, real estate, treasury/financing vehicles, holding companies, and captive insurance entities.
- Geographic breadth: Subsidiaries span North America (notably many U.S. Delaware entities and state-specific Blue Cloud Distribution companies), Latin America (e.g., Mexico, Guatemala, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, Chile, Colombia), Europe (e.g., UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Portugal, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Hungary, Czech Republic, Belgium, Cyprus, Switzerland, Russia, Ukraine, Serbia, Romania), Middle East & Africa (e.g., Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Nigeria, South Africa, Ethiopia), and Asia-Pacific (e.g., China, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand), plus Central Asia (e.g., Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan).
- Major brands/business units represented: Frito-Lay, Pepsi-Cola (bottling, manufacturing, and concentrate operations), Quaker Oats, Gatorade/Stokely-Van Camp, Walkers/Smith’s, Sabritas/Gamesa, Pioneer Foods, SodaStream, Tropicana/Alvalle, Evercrisp, Chipsy, Marbo, Lebedyansky and Wimm-Bill-Dann, Ceres, Baicaowei, Stacy’s, Health Warrior, Bare Foods, BFY Brands/PopCorners.
- Structural features: Extensive use of international holding and finance entities (e.g., in the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Ireland, Curaçao), multiple LLCs/B.V.s/GmbHs/S.à r.l.s across regions, captive insurers, pension trustee, and numerous specialized distribution, logistics, and promotional companies.
- Overall takeaway: The exhibit evidences PepsiCo’s global footprint and complex corporate structure supporting its diversified portfolio of beverages and foods through manufacturing, distribution, branding, and financial/administrative functions worldwide.

nodes.start_phrase: In connection with the Annual Report of PepsiCo, Inc. (the “Corporation”) on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 25, 2021 as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on the date hereof (the “Report”), I, Hugh F. Johnston, Chief Financial Officer of the Corporation, certify to my knowledge, pursuant to Section 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (18 U.S.C. Section 1350), that:
nodes.summary:
- Exhibit 32: Sarbanes-Oxley Act Section 906 certifications for PepsiCo, Inc.’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 25, 2021.
- Signatories: Ramon L. Laguarta (Chairman of the Board & CEO) and Hugh F. Johnston (CFO).
- Each certifies, to their knowledge and pursuant to 18 U.S.C. §1350, that:
  - The Form 10-K complies with Section 13(a) or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
  - The report fairly presents, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition and results of operations.
- Filed with the SEC; both certifications dated February 9, 2022, and signed by the respective officers.
